# Curl (C# port) functional gap report: differences from curl 8.22.0

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Subject:** Curl, a C# reimplementation of the curl command-line tool and libcurl API: [github.com/StewartScottRogers/Curl](https://github.com/StewartScottRogers/Curl), branch `master` at commit `b0d27d68`.
- **Audience:** the project's Dark Factory pipeline. Every issue below is written to be confirmed and fixed on its own: it carries its own setup, repro commands, expected and actual behaviour, suspected source location and an acceptance criterion.

## 1. Scope, references and method

### Scope

This is a third-party **functional** review. It compares what the port does (exit codes, stdout and stderr bytes, files written, bytes on the wire, libcurl return codes and CURLINFO values) with real curl. **Speed, memory use and binary size are out of scope by the owner's instruction** and are not reported anywhere in this document. A hang (no exit within a timeout where real curl exits) is reported, because it is a functional failure.

### Reference and tested binaries

| Role | Platform | Version | Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| REF (primary oracle) | Windows 11 | curl 8.22.0, Schannel, Git for Windows ucrt64 build (a Debug, non-UNICODE build: argv is read in the ANSI code page, cp1252 here) | `C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\bin\curl.exe` |
| REF libcurl | Windows 11 | libcurl 8.22.0 (same build) | `C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\bin\libcurl-4.dll` |
| PORT | Windows 11 | Curl, native AOT, master @ b0d27d68 | `SCR\bin\win\curl.exe` |
| PORT libcurl | Windows 11 / WSL | Libcurl.dll built from the port source (driven through its C# API; the port has no C exports) | `SCR\Curl\Libcurl\bin\Release\net10.0\Libcurl.dll` |
| REF-LINUX (secondary oracle) | WSL Ubuntu | curl 8.18.0, OpenSSL 3.5.5, nghttp2 1.68 (older than the 8.22.0 target) | `/usr/bin/curl`, `libcurl.so.4` |
| PORT-LINUX | WSL Ubuntu | Curl, self-contained build of the same commit | `~/curlnet/curl` |

`SCR` = `C:\Users\STEWAR~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\Z--repos-Curl-ThirdPartyReview\3796612b-55d9-44ec-9722-80e35c3282a1\scratchpad` (the review scratchpad). All evidence folders, harnesses and test servers named below live under `SCR\evidence\<area>\`. `SCR\Curl` is a read-only checkout of the port at b0d27d68; source locations in this report are relative to the port repository root.

**Note for the Dark Factory:** the scratchpad is a temporary folder. If it is no longer available, rebuild the repro from the commands and server descriptions in each issue; every issue states the server behaviour it needs.

### Method

- **Differential testing.** For each of 21 areas, a tester built loopback-only servers and harnesses and ran the same command line through REF and PORT (and REF-LINUX and PORT-LINUX in WSL), comparing exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, request bytes on the wire, files written and server-side logs. Every run was wrapped in a timeout. No traffic left the machine (127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost only).
- **Independent verification.** Every finding was re-run by a separate verifier from its repro. Findings the verifier could not reproduce, or showed to be non-differences, were refuted and are listed in Appendix C.
- **Normalisation.** Only values that legitimately change per run were masked: dates, OS-chosen ports, timings (`after N ms`, speed columns), multipart boundaries, random nonces/cnonces/keys, the `curl/8.x.y` version string, and lines that only REF's Debug build prints. Each issue's setup line names the area harness; the area harness documents its exact normalisations.
- **Linux results** compare against REF-LINUX 8.18.0, which is older than the 8.22.0 target. A Linux-only difference is marked Probable unless it was shown not to depend on the curl version (for example the same result against Windows REF 8.22.0, an RFC MUST enforced by nghttp2/OpenSSL in every version, or curl's 8.22.0 source/docs).
- **Confidence.** *Confirmed* = reproduced at least twice (finder and verifier). *Probable* = reproduced, but the oracle is only REF-LINUX 8.18.0, or the result depends on timing or build options.
- **Severity.** *Critical*: crash, hang, data loss or corruption, or security-relevant wrong behaviour. *High*: wrong output or exit code in common use. *Medium*: wrong in less common use or an edge case. *Low*: cosmetic (message text, verbose lines, ordering) or rare.
- **Duplicates.** The same defect found in several areas has been merged into one issue; the issue lists every contributing area and source finding, and keeps each one's repro. Appendix D maps every area finding ID to its CGR issue.
- **Running repro commands.** In repro commands, `curl` means each binary in turn, called by its full path (REF, then PORT). WSL commands are run by writing a bash script with LF line endings into SCR and calling `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "/mnt/c/Users/Stewart Rogers/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/Z--repos-Curl-ThirdPartyReview/3796612b-55d9-44ec-9722-80e35c3282a1/scratchpad/<script>.sh"`. Never use `C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe` (8.21) or the WinGet curl as the oracle.
- **Volume.** 373 area findings (after excluding refuted ones) were merged into 294 distinct issues.

## 3. Issues

Sorted by severity, then by primary area (in the order of the area table above). Each issue lists the area finding IDs it came from (for example `http-responses HR-1`); Appendix D maps them back.

<a id="cgr-001"></a>
### CGR-001: HTTP/1.1 response desync: after a Content-Length body followed by extra bytes, PORT keeps the connection and returns the stale bytes as the response to the next URL

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Area:** http-responses, network-robustness
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: [http-responses HR-1] Both (Windows and Linux); [network-robustness NR-8] Windows (not run on Linux).
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [http-responses HR-1] Confirmed. The original tester reproduced it 3 times on Windows and once on Linux; the verifier reproduced it again on both.; [http-responses HR-2] Confirmed (Windows and Linux)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0072, GF-0002
- **Source findings:** `http-responses HR-1`, `http-responses HR-2`, `network-robustness NR-8`

Same root cause in all three findings: `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpProtocolHandler.cs:1096` (`SettleConnection`) marks the connection reusable without checking for bytes read past the Content-Length body. curl prints `* Excess found ...` and closes the connection.

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-responses):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-responses`. Canned-response server: `dotnet run EV\server\server.cs -- 20400 EV\resp EV\logs`; `GET /NAME` returns the bytes of `EV\resp\NAME.bin` (if `EV\resp\NAME.opts` contains `keep`, the connection stays open). Differential: `EV\diff.ps1 -Name NAME -CArgs ... [-Opts keep]`; verifier `EV\verify\vdiff.ps1` (port 20420) driven by `EV\verify\vcases.ps1`. Linux: `EV\linux\server.py` serves the same fixtures (verifier: port 20460 via `EV\verify\linux\vrun.sh`; port 20450 in the original runs).
- *Setup (network-robustness):* EV = `SCR\evidence\network-robustness`. Windows server: `EV\srvbin\server.exe 21100 21101` (source `EV\srv\server.cs`); repro script `EV\repro_findings.sh` (uses the `d.sh` diff harness). Linux: `python3 EV/linux/srv.py 21150 21151`; repro `EV/linux/verify_lin.sh`. `H=http://127.0.0.1:21100` (21150 on Linux); `b64() { printf "$1" | base64 -w0 | sed 's/+/%2B/g; s/\//%2F/g; s/=/%3D/g'; }`; `$H/raw?b=<b64>` replies with exactly those bytes (`&keep=1` keeps the connection).
- **[http-responses HR-1]** Response desync: after a Content-Length response followed by extra bytes, PORT reuses the connection and returns the stale bytes as the reply to the next URL
  - `EV\resp\desync_16384.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nhe` + 16344 x `P` + `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\n\r\nEVIL`, with opts `keep`.
  - `EV\resp\desync_b.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\n\r\nGOOD`, with opts `keep`.
  - Script: `EV\repro_desync.ps1`.
  - Command: `curl -v http://127.0.0.1:20400/desync_16384 http://127.0.0.1:20400/desync_b`
  - Variant: `desync_65536` (64K of padding), run with `-s -S`.
- **[http-responses HR-2]** Connection reused after excess body bytes where curl closes it (%{num_connects}, missing "Excess found")
  - `keep_two_bigcl.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nhello`, opts `keep`.
    Command: `curl -s -S -w "%{num_connects}\n" http://127.0.0.1:20400/keep_two_bigcl http://127.0.0.1:20400/keep_two_bigcl`
  - `keep_204_body.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 204 No\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhelloHTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nok`, opts `keep`.
    Command: `curl -s -S -w "%{num_connects} %{http_code}\n" <url> <url>`
- **[network-robustness NR-8]** Excess bytes after a Content-Length body do not stop connection reuse
  - `curl -s -w '[%{num_connects}]' "$H/raw?keep=1&b=$(b64 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nabcdef')" $H/ok`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-responses HR-1]
EV\repro_desync.ps1
curl -v http://127.0.0.1:20400/desync_16384 http://127.0.0.1:20400/desync_b
# [http-responses HR-2]
curl -s -S -w "%{num_connects}\n" http://127.0.0.1:20400/keep_two_bigcl http://127.0.0.1:20400/keep_two_bigcl
curl -s -S -w "%{num_connects} %{http_code}\n" <url> <url>
# [network-robustness NR-8]
curl -s -w '[%{num_connects}]' "$H/raw?keep=1&b=$(b64 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nabcdef')" $H/ok
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-1]** prints `* Excess found writing body: excess = 16386, size = 2, maxdownload = 2, bytecount = 2`, then `* shutting down connection #0`, and opens a new connection for URL 2. stdout is `heGOOD`, exit 0. REF-LINUX 8.18 does the same.
- **[http-responses HR-2]** `he1\nhe1\n`, and for the 204 case `1 204\n1 204\n`. The second URL uses a new connection.
- **[network-robustness NR-8]** closes the connection and opens a new one. The server sees 2 connections; stdout `ab[1]aaaaa[1]`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-1]** prints `Connection #0 ... left intact`, then `Reusing existing http: connection`.
  - 16K padding: stdout is `heEVIL`, exit 0. The injected bytes are taken as the response to URL 2.
  - 64K padding: stdout is `he`, exit 8 `curl: (8) Invalid status line`, because the leftover `PPPP...` bytes are parsed as URL 2's status line.
  - Same result on Linux.
- **[http-responses HR-2]** `he1\nhe0\n`, and for the 204 case `1 204\n0 204\n`. The connection is reused. Same on Linux.
- **[network-robustness NR-8]** reuses the connection. The server sees 1 connection; stdout `ab[1]aaaaa[0]`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-responses HR-1]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary\HttpProtocolHandler.cs:1096` (`SettleConnection`) marks the connection reusable when the outcome is "left intact". Nothing checks for bytes already read past the Content-Length body. `HttpResponseBodyReader.cs` reports leftovers only for chunked bodies.
- **[http-responses HR-2]** same root cause as HR-1, `HttpProtocolHandler.cs:1096` `SettleConnection`. This is the observable symptom when the stale bytes happen to be harmless.
- **[network-robustness NR-8]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary` has no "Excess found" handling (grep finds nothing); the persistence decision is in HttpProtocolHandler

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-002"></a>
### CGR-002: `--retry` does not rewind the upload: retried `-T <file>` PUTs are sent with Content-Length 0 and exit 0 (silent data loss), and retried `-F` forms fail with exit 26

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Area:** http-stateful
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [http-stateful HS-1] Confirmed (re-run on Windows and Linux); [http-stateful HS-2] Confirmed (Windows and Linux)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0005
- **Source findings:** `http-stateful HS-1`, `http-stateful HS-2`

Same root cause: `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary/TransferRetrier.cs:96-98` calls `transfer(context)` again with the same context and never rewinds the upload source.

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-stateful):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-stateful`. Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Replay a case: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 <case>`; ad hoc: `EV\vrun.ps1 <routesdir> <curl args>`. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` with `EV\linux\vpat.txt`.
- **[http-stateful HS-1]** --retry with -T <file> resends an empty body; every retried PUT has Content-Length: 0 and curl exits 0
  - Routes: `p.1.http` = `HTTP/1.1 503 X`, `Content-Length: 2`, body `e\n`. `p.2.http` = `200 OK`, body `ok\n`.
  - Commands: `printf upload > u.txt`, then `curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -T u.txt http://127.0.0.1:20500/p`.
  - Also fails with `--retry-all-errors` after a dropped connection (case rT-drop-all) and with `-L --retry 1` across a 307 (case rT-retry-L).
  - Cases: `EV\cases\retry-T`, `rT-again`, `rT-drop-all`, `rT-retry-L`. Replay: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 retry-T,rT-drop-all,rT-retry-L`.
- **[http-stateful HS-2]** --retry with any -F form fails on the retry with exit 26 "client mime read EOF fail"
  - the same 503-then-200 routes as HS-1. Run `curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -F f=@u.txt http://127.0.0.1:20500/p` and `curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -F f=value http://127.0.0.1:20500/p`. Cases: `EV\cases\rF`, `rF-str`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-stateful HS-1]
printf upload > u.txt
curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -T u.txt http://127.0.0.1:20500/p
pwsh EV\verify.ps1 retry-T,rT-drop-all,rT-retry-L
# [http-stateful HS-2]
curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -F f=@u.txt http://127.0.0.1:20500/p
curl -sS --retry 2 --retry-delay 1 -F f=value http://127.0.0.1:20500/p
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-stateful HS-1]** every attempt sends `PUT /p`, `Content-Length: 6` and the body `upload`. Stdout `e\nok\n`, exit 0.
- **[http-stateful HS-2]** resends the whole multipart body (Content-Length 198 or 153) and gets the 200. Stdout `e\nok\n`, exit 0.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-stateful HS-1]** 
  - Attempt 1 sends `Content-Length: 6` and `upload`. Attempt 2 and every later one sends `PUT /p` with `Content-Length: 0` and no body.
  - Exit is 0, so the server stores an empty file and nothing reports an error.
  - With -L, both retried hops (/p and /q) are sent empty.
  - `-T -` (stdin) matches REF.
- **[http-stateful HS-2]** sends only the first request, then prints `curl: (26) client mime read EOF fail, only 0/153 of needed bytes read` (0/198 for the file form). Exit 26, stdout `e\n`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-stateful HS-1]** `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary/TransferRetrier.cs:96-98`. The attempt loop calls `transfer(context)` again with the same context and never rewinds the upload source.
- **[http-stateful HS-2]** `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary/TransferRetrier.cs:96-98` (no rewind between attempts). The message comes from `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpRequestBodyWriter.cs`.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-003"></a>
### CGR-003: POP3/IMAP/SMTP ignore --connect-timeout while waiting for the server greeting (hang)

- **Severity:** Critical (hang)
- **Area:** writeout-verbose
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (reproduced by the original tester and the verifier, on Windows and Linux).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `writeout-verbose WV-01`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (writeout-verbose):* EV = `SCR\evidence\writeout-verbose`. Windows server: `cd EV\srv && dotnet run wvsrv.cs -- 20700 EV\resp EV\req.log` (HTTP on 127.0.0.1/::1:20700, a mini FTP server on 20701, TLS on 20702; `/raw/<name>` serves `EV\resp\<name>.txt`; other routes `/code/N`, `/redir/N`, `/hang/ms`, `/close` (empty reply), `/ka`, `/echo`, `/p`). Linux: `EV\linux\srv.py` on 20710. One-line repros for every finding: `EV\repro_findings.sh` (Windows) and `EV\linux\verify_linux.sh`.
- A listener that accepts the connection and never sends anything. The HTTP port of wvsrv.cs waits for a request, so it qualifies.
  - `curl -sS -w '%{exitcode}|%{errormsg}\n' pop3://127.0.0.1:20700/ --connect-timeout 2`
  - Same with `imap://` and `smtp://`.
  - Linux: port 20710.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -sS -w '%{exitcode}|%{errormsg}\n' pop3://127.0.0.1:20700/ --connect-timeout 2
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- After about 2 s, exit 28 with `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2012 milliseconds with 0 bytes received`. REF-LINUX 8.18 behaves the same.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Never exits. It was killed by the 20 s timeout (exit 124) with no output. This happens on Windows and Linux. `ftp://` in the same setup matches REF.

**Suspected location in source**

- The greeting read in Curl.Original.Protocol.Pop3/Imap/Smtp.UnitLibrary is not bounded by the connect deadline.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Harnesses `E\tlsdiff.ps1`, `E\linux\tlsdiff.sh`; verifier `E\verify\vwin1.ps1`, `vwin2.ps1`, `vlin.sh` (cases `E\cases\V_*`, `E\linux\cases\V_L_*`).
- *Setup (proxy-connect):* EV = `SCR\evidence\proxy-connect`. Scripted recording server: `EV\srv\out\srv.exe <port> <log> '<script for conn 1>' ['<script for conn 2>' ...]` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`); steps are `;`-separated: `H` read a request head, `HN` read a head and answer nothing yet, `OK`/`CE`/`403`/`403B`/`407B` canned replies, `W:<bytes>` write literal bytes, `S4`/`S5G`/`S5U`/`S5R` read SOCKS messages, `E` record raw bytes until EOF. In repros `srv` means this binary. Harnesses `EV\harness.ps1` and `EV\lharness.sh`; verifier `EV\v_win*.ps1`, `EV\v_linux.sh`, `EV\v_l3.sh`.
- **[tls TLS-02]** The Windows default TLS minimum is not TLS 1.2. PORT silently negotiates TLS 1.0/1.1 when no version option is given

Then run `curl -sS -k https://localhost:20803/index.txt`, and `curl -sS --cacert E\pki\ca.crt --ssl-no-revoke https://localhost:20803/index.txt`. Cases: `V_srv11_default`, `V_srv10_default`, `V_srv11_default_ca`.
- **[proxy-connect PC-18]** The ClientHello offers TLS 1.1 and 1.0 in supported_versions; the Schannel reference offers only 1.3 and 1.2
  - run `srv 20600 log 'E'`, then `curl -sS -k --resolve ex.test:20600:127.0.0.1 https://ex.test:20600/x`, or `curl -sS --proxy-insecure -x https://127.0.0.1:20600 http://ex.test/x`. Both exit 35 once the server closes. Verifier cases: v25, v25b, v27, v27b, v28 and v28b.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [tls TLS-02]
openssl s_server -accept 20803 -cert E\pki\srv.crt -key E\pki\srv.key -WWW -tls1_1 -cipher DEFAULT@SECLEVEL=0
curl -sS -k https://localhost:20803/index.txt
curl -sS --cacert E\pki\ca.crt --ssl-no-revoke https://localhost:20803/index.txt
# [proxy-connect PC-18]
srv 20600 log 'E'
curl -sS -k --resolve ex.test:20600:127.0.0.1 https://ex.test:20600/x
curl -sS --proxy-insecure -x https://127.0.0.1:20600 http://ex.test/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[tls TLS-02]** Exit 35 `curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: SEC_E_UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION (0x80090302) - The function requested is not supported`. Its ClientHello supported_versions lists only TLS 1.3 and 1.2.
- **[proxy-connect PC-18]** `00 2b 00 05 04 03 04 03 03` (TLS 1.3, TLS 1.2).

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[tls TLS-02]** Exit 0. It prints `hello tls` over TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.0. Its ClientHello offers TLS 1.3, 1.2, 1.1 and 1.0.
- **[proxy-connect PC-18]** `00 2b 00 09 08 03 04 03 03 03 02 03 01` (TLS 1.3, 1.2, 1.1, 1.0). The rest of the extension list is identical.

**Notes**

- **[proxy-connect PC-18]** *Correction:* the tester's claim that REF also sends status_request and PORT omits it was not reproduced. Neither side sent status_request in any run, with or without -k, including the tester's own e60, n54, t14 and f15 captures.
- **[proxy-connect PC-18]** Whether a TLS 1.0/1.1 handshake would complete also depends on the Windows SChannel policy; it was not tested.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[tls TLS-02]** `Curl.Networking.UnitLibrary\TlsVersionRange.cs:40-52`. `ToSslProtocols` returns `SslProtocols.None` (the OS default) when no minimum is set. It should return Tls12|Tls13, the clamp that `HandBuiltTlsProvider` applies.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-005: FTPS with PROT P in passive mode hangs: PORT does the data-connection TLS handshake before sending TYPE/SIZE/RETR, deadlocking with servers (vsftpd/proftpd ordering) that start data TLS after the transfer command

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Area:** ftp-file-tftp, tls
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [ftp-file-tftp FTP-1] Confirmed (reproduced by the original tester and again here, on Windows and Linux); [tls TLS-01] Confirmed (verifier reproduced it on Windows and on Linux)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0048
- **Source findings:** `ftp-file-tftp FTP-1`, `tls TLS-01`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (ftp-file-tftp):* EV = `SCR\evidence\ftp-file-tftp`. Scripted FTP/TFTP stub: `EV\stub\win3\stub.exe` (Linux `EV/stub/linux/stub`, source `EV\stub\Program.cs`) with fixture root `EV\fixture\root` (file.txt is 18 bytes). Differential harness `EV\dt.sh NAME 'script' curl-args`, where `@U@` = `ftp://127.0.0.1:$CPORT`, script lines are `CMD=reply` or `OPT key=value` separated by `;;`, and `STUBEXTRA=EV\tls.pfx` enables FTPS. Verifier: `EV\v1.sh`, `EV\v2.sh` (Windows), `EV\vl.sh` (Linux).
- *Setup (tls):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls`. PKI in `E\pki` (`index.txt` contains `hello tls`; pfx password `x`). Servers: `openssl s_server -accept <p> -cert E\pki\srv.crt -key E\pki\srv.key -WWW [options]` (Git ucrt64 openssl on Windows, system openssl in WSL, run from a directory containing `index.txt`), `E\srv\out\starttls.exe <proto> <port> <pfx> [implicit|refuse|noext]` (source `E\srv\starttls.cs`), `E\linux\stsrv.py` (same idea in Python). Harnesses `E\tlsdiff.ps1`, `E\linux\tlsdiff.sh`; verifier `E\verify\vwin1.ps1`, `vwin2.ps1`, `vlin.sh` (cases `E\cases\V_*`, `E\linux\cases\V_L_*`).
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-1]** FTPS with PROT P (`--ssl-reqd`, `--ssl`, `ftps://`) hangs forever in passive mode when the server starts data-channel TLS only after the transfer command (vsftpd/proftpd ordering)
  - Stub with TLS, using the default lazy data-TLS mode: `stub.exe ftp 20960 <root> <script> <log> EV\tls.pfx` (in the harness, `STUBEXTRA=EV\tls.pfx`). Run `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt`. Implicit FTPS uses script `OPT implicit=1` with `curl -sS -k ftps://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt`. Cases: `v_s_reqd` and `v_s_implicit` (Windows, `EV\v1.sh`); `v_s_reqd` (Linux, `EV\vl.sh`). The original cases are under `EV\cases\s_*`.
- **[tls TLS-01]** FTPS with PROT P (passive mode) hangs. PORT does the data-connection TLS handshake before it sends TYPE/SIZE/RETR
  - *(Windows):* `E\srv\out\starttls.exe ftp 20800 E\pki\srv.pfx`. The server does the data-channel TLS accept only after RETR/LIST, as vsftpd does. Then run `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd ftp://localhost:20800/file.txt`. The same happens with `--ssl`, `--ftp-ssl`, `--ftp-ssl-reqd`, `--ftp-ssl-control`, `--ftp-ssl-ccc`, a directory LIST, and implicit `ftps://` (server flag `implicit`). Script: `E\verify\vwin1.ps1` (cases `V_ftp_sslreqd`, `V_ftps_implicit`); the original run is `E\batch5.ps1`.
  - *(Linux):* `python3 E/linux/stsrv.py ftp <port> <pkidir>`, then the same command (`E\verify\vlin.sh`, cases `V_L_ftp_sslreqd`, `V_L_ftps_implicit`).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [ftp-file-tftp FTP-1]
stub.exe ftp 20960 <root> <script> <log> EV\tls.pfx
export STUBEXTRA=EV\tls.pfx
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt
curl -sS -k ftps://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt
EV\v1.sh
EV\vl.sh
# [tls TLS-01]
E\srv\out\starttls.exe ftp 20800 E\pki\srv.pfx
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd ftp://localhost:20800/file.txt
E\verify\vwin1.ps1
E\batch5.ps1
python3 E/linux/stsrv.py ftp <port> <pkidir>
E\verify\vlin.sh
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-1]** Connects the data socket and keeps the TLS handshake pending. It sends TYPE I, SIZE and RETR on the control connection, and the handshake completes after RETR. Exit 0, the file is delivered.
- **[tls TLS-01]** After `229 EPSV` it sends `TYPE I`, `SIZE file.txt`, `RETR file.txt`. The server then accepts TLS on the data connection and REF prints `hello ftp`. Exit 0 on Linux. On Windows the exit is 0 or `56 Recv failure: Connection was aborted`, caused by the stand-in server's close.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-1]** After the 229 reply it connects the data socket and blocks in the data TLS handshake. It never sends TYPE I, so client and server deadlock. The run was killed by the timeout wrapper: exit 124 at 30 s in this run, and still hung at 200 s in the original run. Wire diff: REF sends `TYPE I`, `SIZE file.txt`, `RETR file.txt` and `QUIT`; PORT sends nothing after `EPSV`.
  - Control: with script `OPT eagertls=1`, where the server starts the handshake at accept time, PORT matches REF (`v_se_reqd` is SAME on both OSes). Active mode (`-P`) is not affected.
- **[tls TLS-01]** The server log stops at `EPSV`. PORT has connected the data socket and blocks in the TLS handshake, so the two sides deadlock. There is no output until the process is killed (20 s harness timeout; Linux exit 124). With `-m 5` it exits 28 `Operation timed out after 5007 milliseconds with 0 bytes received`. A plain `ftp://` transfer without TLS matches REF.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-1]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary/FtpSession.cs:1788-1808` `OpenPassiveDataConnectionAsync` calls `SecureDataConnectionAsync` (`:1757`) right after the passive connect, before the transfer command. curl only adds the SSL filter there and completes the handshake without blocking after RETR/STOR/LIST.
- **[tls TLS-01]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary\FtpSession.cs:1808`. On the EPSV path, `SecureDataConnectionAsync()` is awaited right after the dial. The same happens in `ConnectDataAsync` at about line 1900, where a comment says the handshake runs "at once, before TYPE". `SecureDataConnectionAsync` (line 1757) awaits the whole handshake.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-006"></a>
### CGR-006: Windows FTPS uploads end the TLS data connection with a TCP reset: in passive mode the server receives 0 bytes while PORT exits 0 (silent data loss); in active mode over TLS 1.3 a strict server answers 426 and PORT exits 18

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Area:** ftp-file-tftp, tls-protocols-revocation
- **Platform(s):** Windows. Detail: [ftp-file-tftp FTP-2] Windows (the same case on Linux matches REF)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [ftp-file-tftp FTP-2] Confirmed (reproduced twice here, plus the original runs)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `ftp-file-tftp FTP-2`, `tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05`

Both findings point at the same close path after `SecureDataConnectionAsync` (`Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary/FtpSession.cs`, about line 1757). The likely cause is closing the socket with unread TLS 1.3 post-handshake data (NewSessionTicket) or without close_notify, which makes Windows send RST.

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (ftp-file-tftp):* EV = `SCR\evidence\ftp-file-tftp`. Scripted FTP/TFTP stub: `EV\stub\win3\stub.exe` (Linux `EV/stub/linux/stub`, source `EV\stub\Program.cs`) with fixture root `EV\fixture\root` (file.txt is 18 bytes). Differential harness `EV\dt.sh NAME 'script' curl-args`, where `@U@` = `ftp://127.0.0.1:$CPORT`, script lines are `CMD=reply` or `OPT key=value` separated by `;;`, and `STUBEXTRA=EV\tls.pfx` enables FTPS. Verifier: `EV\v1.sh`, `EV\v2.sh` (Windows), `EV\vl.sh` (Linux).
- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-2]** FTPS upload on Windows loses all data while the exit code is 0
  - Stub with `EV\tls.pfx` and script `OPT eagertls=1`. Run `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -T upload.txt ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/u.txt`, where upload.txt contains `up1\nup2\n` (8 bytes). Cases: `v_se_up` and `v_se_up2` (`EV\v1.sh`); originals `EV\cases\se_up_r2`, `se_up_r3`, `se_reqd_up`.
- **[tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05]** Windows: FTPS uploads in active mode over TLS 1.3 end the data connection with a TCP reset, so a strict server answers 426 and PORT exits 18
  - `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ftp 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx updir=E\up tls=implicit strict=1`. With `strict=1` the server answers `426 Failure reading network stream.` when the data connection ends with an error, as vsftpd does. Then run `curl -sS -k -P 127.0.0.1 -T up.txt ftps://localhost:21900/new.txt`. Explicit variant: the server without `tls=implicit`, client `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -P 127.0.0.1 -T up.txt ftp://localhost:21900/new.txt`. Verifier cases: `v_P_stor_strict`, `v_P_stor_reqd_strict`, plus the controls `v_P_stor12_strict` (TLS 1.2, matches) and Linux `V_P_stor_strict` (matches).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [ftp-file-tftp FTP-2]
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -T upload.txt ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/u.txt
EV\v1.sh
# [tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05]
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ftp 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx updir=E\up tls=implicit strict=1
curl -sS -k -P 127.0.0.1 -T up.txt ftps://localhost:21900/new.txt
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -P 127.0.0.1 -T up.txt ftp://localhost:21900/new.txt
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-2]** The server receives the 8 bytes and replies 226. u.txt holds `up1\nup2\n`. Exit 0.
- **[tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05]** The server reads the whole upload with a clean end of stream and answers 226. Exit 0.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-2]** The server log shows `DATA recv error after 0 bytes: IOException: ... An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host`, followed by `DATA recv 0 bytes`. u.txt on the server is empty, yet PORT exits 0 and sends QUIT. The only harness diff is ROOTFILES, so the upload looks successful. The data connection is reset before the server reads any application data.
  - Suspected cause: the socket is closed while TLS 1.3 post-handshake data (the session ticket) is unread, which makes Windows send RST, or it is closed without close_notify.
  - Linux `v_se_up` is SAME.
- **[tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05]** The 14 upload bytes arrive (same SHA), but the server's read ends with `IOException: … An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host` (RST). The strict server answers 426, and PORT exits 18 `curl: (18) server did not report OK, got 426`. Against a lenient server the exit is 0, but the reset is still on the wire (original `b2_*_P_stor*`, `b2_reqd_P_stdin`).

**Suspected location in source**

- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-2]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary/FtpSession.cs`, the upload data-connection close path after `SecureDataConnectionAsync` (`:1757`). Not narrowed further.
- **[tls-protocols-revocation TPR-05]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary\FtpSession.cs`, the upload data-connection close after `SecureDataConnectionAsync` (about line 1757). The likely cause is closing the socket with unread TLS 1.3 post-handshake data (NewSessionTicket), which makes Windows send RST. Not narrowed further.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-007"></a>
### CGR-007: TELNET -T upload is written concurrently with option-negotiation replies, so upload bytes can land inside an `IAC SB NAWS ... IAC SE` subnegotiation

- **Severity:** Critical (the telnet stream is corrupted)
- **Area:** other-protocols
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Both. The upload goes out before or between the negotiation replies on Windows and Linux. The upload inside SB was seen on Windows.
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. The verifier reproduced the SB split (1 of 3 large-upload runs on Windows) and the ordering difference (40/40 on Windows and 7/7 on Linux).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0043
- **Source findings:** `other-protocols OP-1`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (other-protocols):* EV = `SCR\evidence\other-protocols`. Scripted per-protocol loopback servers and runner in `EV\bench\Program.cs`; Windows `pwsh -File EV\run.ps1 <file>.cases [filter]`, Linux `bash EV/run.sh <file>.cases` (set `FILTER=`) or `EV/verify-linux.sh [filter]`. Each `.cases` line is `name | server-mode | server options | curl args`. Default servers: SMTP answers 250 and offers AUTH PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5 XOAUTH2 OAUTHBEARER; POP3 offers SASL PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5; IMAP offers AUTH=PLAIN AUTH=LOGIN AUTH=CRAM-MD5 SASL-IR.
- Server mode `telnet`. On connect it sends `FF FD 18 FF FD 1F FF FD 27 FF FD 23 FF FB 01 FF FB 03 FF FD 03`, reads for 700 ms, then sends SB SEND for TTYPE, XDISPLOC and NEW-ENVIRON, then some text, and records what the client sends.
- Small upload: `pwsh -File EV\run.ps1 telnet.cases t17`, which runs `curl -s -S -T EV\data\tel_in.txt telnet://127.0.0.1:21001`.
- Large upload (makes the split easy to hit): `EV\verify\telbig.cases`, which runs `curl -s -S -T EV\data\big_lf.txt telnet://127.0.0.1:<port>` (410 KB). Linux: `EV/verify-linux-tel.sh`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
pwsh -File EV\run.ps1 telnet.cases t17
curl -s -S -T EV\data\tel_in.txt telnet://127.0.0.1:21001
curl -s -S -T EV\data\big_lf.txt telnet://127.0.0.1:<port>
EV/verify-linux-tel.sh
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- REF handles the whole batch of server negotiation first, then sends the upload. The wire starts `FF FC 18 FF FB 1F FF FA 1F 00 00 00 00 FF F0 FF FC 27 FF FC 23 FF FD 01 FF FD 03 FF FB 03 FF FB 00 FF FD 00` and is followed by the data. This was the result in 40/40 verifier runs on Windows and in every Linux run.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Order: the upload goes out first or at arbitrary reply boundaries. In 40/40 verifier runs of t17 on Windows, and in every Linux run, `hello telnet\r\n...` came before any negotiation reply.
- Corruption, large upload, Windows run 1 (`EV\verify\telbig.port.1.wire`): `FF FA 1F` is at offset 49173, then 16 KB of upload data, then `00 00 00 00 FF F0` at offset 65555. The window-size subnegotiation therefore contains 16 KB of file data.
- Corruption, small upload: the original tester saw the same thing in 7/68 Windows runs (`EV\telnet-race\port.32.wire`): `FF FA 1F 00 00 00 00 'hello telnet\r\nsecond line\n' FF FF ' byte\n' FF F0`.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Telnet.UnitLibrary\TelnetProtocolHandler.cs:184-199`: the upload runs as its own task (`SendUploadAsync`, line ~404).
- `TelnetProtocolHandler.cs:446-488`: `SendReplyAsync` takes `sendLock` once per reply piece.
- `TelnetReceiver.cs:433-439` (`AppendWindowSize`) queues `IAC SB NAWS`, the size bytes and `IAC SE` as three separate sends, so the upload task can win the lock between them.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-008"></a>
### CGR-008: PORT-LINUX aborts (SIGABRT, exit 134) when stderr is a full device (ENOSPC)

- **Severity:** Critical (crash)
- **Area:** network-robustness
- **Platform(s):** Linux
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. This is a process crash, so the REF-LINUX 8.18 version does not explain it.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `network-robustness NR-1`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (network-robustness):* EV = `SCR\evidence\network-robustness`. Windows server: `EV\srvbin\server.exe 21100 21101` (source `EV\srv\server.cs`); repro script `EV\repro_findings.sh` (uses the `d.sh` diff harness). Linux: `python3 EV/linux/srv.py 21150 21151`; repro `EV/linux/verify_lin.sh`. `H=http://127.0.0.1:21100` (21150 on Linux); `b64() { printf "$1" | base64 -w0 | sed 's/+/%2B/g; s/\//%2F/g; s/=/%3D/g'; }`; `$H/raw?b=<b64>` replies with exactly those bytes (`&keep=1` keeps the connection).
- *(WSL, `python3 linux/srv.py 21150 21151 &`):* 
  `~/curlnet/curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:21199/ 2>/dev/full; echo $?`. Also `~/curlnet/curl http://127.0.0.1:21150/ok 2>/dev/full >/dev/null` (progress meter), `-v ... 2>/dev/full`, `--badopt 2>/dev/full`, `-w '%{stderr}x' -o /dev/null -s .../ok 2>/dev/full`. Script: `linux/abort.sh`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
~/curlnet/curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:21199/ 2>/dev/full; echo $?
~/curlnet/curl http://127.0.0.1:21150/ok 2>/dev/full >/dev/null
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- ignores the failed stderr write and exits with the transfer's code: 7, 0, 0, 2, 0.

**Actual (Curl)**

- bash prints `Aborted`, exit 134. Closed stderr (`2>&-`) and an EPIPE stderr do not crash.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Console/UnhandledExceptionGuard.cs:31-38`. The catch block writes `curl: (2) ...` to standardError with no protection. That second IOException escapes Main, and the runtime then fails while printing the crash to the same full stderr.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-009: An empty dotted label in no_proxy / NO_PROXY / --noproxy (e.g. `.1`, `.0.0.1`, `foo,.x`) crashes the port with exit 2 when the URL host is an IPv4 literal

- **Severity:** Critical (crash; one environment variable breaks every transfer to an IP host)
- **Area:** environment
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (reproduced by the verifier on Windows and Linux).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (environment):* EV = `SCR\evidence\environment`. Windows: `dotnet run EV\server.cs 21200` (echo server: returns the raw request as the body; `/bin` returns bytes 0..255) and `dotnet run EV\s2\server2.cs 21201` (same, used as a proxy). `EV\verify_windows.ps1` runs each case in isolated `aref`/`port` directories with HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA at an empty directory. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` and `EV\linux\vtls.sh` (echo on 21210, proxy on 21211, `openssl s_server` on 21213).
- *(Windows):* 
  - `set http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21201` then `set no_proxy=.0.0.1` then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`
  - No proxy is needed to trigger it: `curl -s --noproxy .1 http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo` and `curl -s --noproxy foo,.x http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`
  - Verifier cases: `verify_windows.ps1` v-np-dot, v-np-opt and v-np-opt2.
- *(Linux):* 
  - `no_proxy=.1 ~/curlnet/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21210/echo`
  - `http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21211 no_proxy=.0.0.1 ~/curlnet/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21210/echo`
  - `linux/verify.sh` covers these as v-np-dot, v-np-dot2 and v-np-opt.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
set http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21201
set no_proxy=.0.0.1
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
curl -s --noproxy .1 http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
curl -s --noproxy foo,.x http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
no_proxy=.1 ~/curlnet/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21210/echo
http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:21211 no_proxy=.0.0.1 ~/curlnet/curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21210/echo
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- The entry does not match. The request is sent through the proxy, or direct with `--noproxy`. Exit 0 and the body is written.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Prints `curl: (2) Index was outside the bounds of the array.` with a bare LF line ending even on Windows. Exits 2 and sends nothing.

**Notes**

- *Not affected:* `--noproxy .1` with a `localhost` URL (v-np-loc gives the same result as REF).

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary\NoProxyMatcher.cs:242-247`. In `TryParseOctet`, `digits.Length <= 3 && (digits.Length == 1 || digits[0] != '0')` reads `digits[0]` when the span is empty. The empty span is a label produced by `text.Split('.')` in `TryParseIPv4` (line 227).

<a id="cgr-011"></a>
### CGR-011: A CR, LF or NUL in an HTTP/2 response header value goes into the HTTP/1 header parser, so a server can inject header lines such as Set-Cookie

- **Severity:** Critical (header and cookie injection across the HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 boundary; RFC 9113 8.2.1 requires treating such a field as malformed)
- **Area:** http2-linux
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Both. PORT-LINUX and PORT-WIN behave identically. REF was checked on Linux only.
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (reproduced by the tester and the verifier, and on PORT-WIN; the REF behaviour is an RFC 9113 check inside nghttp2, so it does not depend on the curl version).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `http2-linux H2L-1`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http2-linux):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http2-linux`. The Windows REF has no HTTP/2, so REF here is REF-LINUX 8.18.0 (nghttp2 1.68). Scripted HTTP/2 server (WSL, needs `libnghttp2.so.14`): `python3 EV/h2srv.py --port P --mode auto|tls|h1 --scen <SCEN> --log s.log [--alpn h2,http/1.1 --cert cert.pem --key key.pem] --life 25`. Harness `EV\run.sh <casefile>` (lines `name|scen|mode|args`); verifier `EV\verify\vrun.sh EV\verify\c_verify.txt` (ports 21612/21613); PORT-WIN: `WINPORT=<port> bash EV\winrun.sh <case>` (one port per case).
- Script: `EV\inject_repro.sh` (output `EV\inject_repro.out`; verifier output `EV\verify\inject_repro.out`).
- Server (WSL): `python3 h2srv.py --port 21640 --scen inject --log inj.log`. It answers with `x-inj: a\r\nset-cookie: evil=1; Path=/` as a single literal HPACK field.
- Command: `curl -sS --http2-prior-knowledge -c jar.txt -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:21640/x http://127.0.0.1:21640/y`
- Variant cases:
  - `r2_inject`, `x_inject_tls` (`-k -c jar.txt -D hdr.txt https://...`)
  - `r_crlfvalue` (`a\r\nb`)
  - `r2_lfvalue`, `x_lf_tls` (`a\nb`)
  - `r2_nulvalue` (`a\0b`)
  - `r2_loccrlf` (a 302 Location containing CRLF, with `-L`)

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
EV\inject_repro.sh
python3 h2srv.py --port 21640 --scen inject --log inj.log
curl -sS --http2-prior-knowledge -c jar.txt -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:21640/x http://127.0.0.1:21640/y
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- nghttp2 rejects the field and curl ignores it without a message. No `x-inj` or `set-cookie` line is written, the jar is empty, request 2 carries no cookie, the body is delivered and the exit code is 0. `%{num_headers}` is 2.

**Actual (Curl)**

- `-D` prints `x-inj: a` and then `set-cookie: evil=1; Path=/`.
- The jar contains `127.0.0.1	FALSE	/	FALSE	0	evil	1`, and request 2 sends `cookie: evil=1` (seen on the wire, over both h2c and TLS).
- `%{num_headers}` is 4.
- `a\r\nb` and `a\nb` fail with `curl: (8) Header without colon` and no body is written.
- NUL fails with `curl: (8) Nul byte in header`.
- The `loccrlf` 302 case exits 8 where REF exits 0.
- PORT-WIN gives the same output (`EV\win\r2_inject`, `r2_lfvalue`, `r2_nulvalue`).

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary\Http2ResponseHead.cs:52-53` (`HeaderLines` joins `name: value\r\n` for every non-pseudo field and does not check the field).

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF-LINUX's (the Windows REF has no HTTP/2), for both PORT-LINUX and PORT-WIN (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-012"></a>
### CGR-012: curl_multi_cleanup called from inside a transfer callback never returns in PORT, and the multi handle is destroyed under the caller (REF refuses with CURLM_RECURSIVE_API_CALL)

- **Severity:** Critical (hang: the callback thread deadlocks)
- **Area:** libcurl-multi-callbacks
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Windows, Linux
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (Windows 2/2, Linux 1/1)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `libcurl-multi-callbacks LMC-1`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (libcurl-multi-callbacks):* EV = `SCR\evidence\libcurl-multi-callbacks`. A C# probe (`EV\probe\`) runs one driver per case against REF `libcurl-4.dll` (P/Invoke) and PORT `Libcurl.dll` (its C# API), with a built-in recording server: 127.0.0.1:21700 answers `200 hello`, 21701 answers `200 other`, 21799 is closed. Run `EV\probe\out\probe.exe <cases> 2` or `powershell -File EV\run.ps1 -Filter <cases> -Out <name> -Reps 2` (`LIBONLY=REF` or `LIBONLY=PORT` runs one side). Linux: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "<EV as /mnt/c path>/linux.sh" <cases> 1 <name>`.
- case `C_93_multi_cleanup_in_callback` (`probe\CasesRecursive.cs:64`).
  1. Multi `m` holds one easy handle for `http://127.0.0.1:21700/`.
  2. On its first call, the WRITEFUNCTION calls `curl_multi_cleanup(m)` and records what it returns.
  3. The loop drives the transfer with `curl_multi_perform` + `curl_multi_poll(100)` for up to 3 s, then calls `curl_multi_cleanup(m)`.

  Command: `EV\probe\out\probe.exe C_93 2`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
EV\probe\out\probe.exe C_93 2
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- prints `multi_cleanup=8 msgs 0` / `final multi_cleanup=0`. The call inside the callback returns CURLM_RECURSIVE_API_CALL and does nothing; the transfer completes.

**Actual (Curl)**

- `multi_cleanup=` is never recorded, because the call inside the callback never returns. The application's next `curl_multi_perform` throws `ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object.`, and no CURLMSG_DONE is delivered.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary\ManagedMultiTransfer.cs:289-308`. `DisposeAsync` sets `disposed`, then runs `await Task.WhenAll(performs)`, and that list includes the perform task the callback is running on. `Libcurl\Multi\Core\CurlMulti.cs` has no check for a call made from inside a callback.

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

- **Severity:** Critical (security: credentials sent in clear although TLS was required)
- **Area:** tls-protocols-revocation
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (verifier reproduced it on Windows and Linux; the Windows result is from REF 8.22.0)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `tls-protocols-revocation TPR-01`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- *(Windows):* `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ldap 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx tls=starttls`. This is a scripted LDAP server that logs every BER message and answers the StartTLS extended operation. Then run `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -u cn=admin:secret ldap://localhost:21900/dc=test`. Verifier cases: `v_ldap_reqd_u`, `v_ldap_ssl_u` (`E\v.ps1 -Only ldap`). Original cases: `b4_ldap_sslreqd`, `b5_ldap_reqd_u`, `b5_ldap_reqd_2`, `b5_ldap_ftpsslreqd`.
- *(Linux):* `~/tpr/srv/tsrv ldap <p> pfx=~/tpr/tp/srv.pfx tls=starttls`, then the same command with `/usr/bin/curl` and `~/curlnet/curl`. Verifier cases: `V_ldap_reqd_u`, `V_ldap_ssl_u` (`E\linux\lv.sh`).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ldap 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx tls=starttls
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd -u cn=admin:secret ldap://localhost:21900/dc=test
E\v.ps1 -Only ldap
~/curlnet/curl
E\linux\lv.sh
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- On Windows (WinLDAP build) with `--ssl-reqd`: exit 4 `curl: (4) LDAP local: explicit TLS not supported`. It connects but sends nothing. On Linux (OpenLDAP build) with `--ssl-reqd` or `--ssl`, it first sends the StartTLS extended request `1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.20037` in plaintext (`77188016312E332E362E312E342E312E313436362E3230303337`), completes the TLS handshake, and then sends the bind, search and unbind inside TLS (`Cs:` lines).

**Actual (Curl)**

- On both platforms it never starts TLS. The first plaintext message is the bind `…60150201030408636E3D61646D696E8006736563726574`: a simple bind for DN `cn=admin` with password `secret`, in clear (`C:` lines). The search and unbind follow, and it exits 0 with the entry printed. The required-TLS level is not consulted at all.

**Notes**

- *Note (verifier):* On Windows with plain `--ssl` (TLS optional), REF also binds in plaintext, so that variant is not a difference on Windows. It differs only on Linux, where REF upgrades with StartTLS.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ldap.UnitLibrary\LdapProtocolHandler.cs:189-195` (`TargetOf`). `useTls` is set only for the `ldaps` scheme. The library has no StartTLS operation, and no UseSslFailed or "explicit TLS not supported" path.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-014: Windows: stapled OCSP responses are ignored. A revoked staple is accepted under `--ssl-revoke-best-effort`, and a good staple still fails with "revocation status is unknown"

- **Severity:** Critical (security: the transfer succeeds against a server whose own staple says its certificate is revoked)
- **Area:** tls-protocols-revocation
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (verifier reproduced it with new certificates ocg11/ocg12/ocr11/ocr12)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `tls-protocols-revocation TPR-02`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- `"C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\bin\openssl.exe" s_server -accept 21900 -cert E\pki\certs\ocr11R.crt -key E\pki\srv.key -cert_chain E\pki\rca.crt -WWW -status_file E\pki\certs\ocr11R.ocsp`, run from a directory that contains `index.txt`. Then run `curl -sS --cacert E\pki\rca.crt --ssl-revoke-best-effort https://localhost:21900/index.txt`. For a good staple, use `ocg11R.crt` / `ocg11R.ocsp` without `--ssl-revoke-best-effort`. Each side gets its own fresh certificate (`…R` for REF, `…P` for PORT), so the Windows URL cache cannot leak between them. Verifier cases: `v_st_good_default`, `v_st_good_default_2`, `v_st_rev_best`, `v_st_rev_default` (`E\v.ps1 -Only staple`). Original cases: `b3_st_*`, `b5_st_*`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -sS --cacert E\pki\rca.crt --ssl-revoke-best-effort https://localhost:21900/index.txt
E\v.ps1 -Only staple
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- Schannel uses the staple. Good staple, default checking: exit 0 with `hello rev`. Revoked staple, default or best-effort checking: exit 60 `curl: (60) schannel: trust for this certificate or one of the certificates in the certificate chain has been revoked`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- It never uses the staple. Good staple, default checking: exit 60 `curl: (60) schannel: the revocation status is unknown`. Revoked staple with `--ssl-revoke-best-effort`: exit 0, and it prints `hello rev`. Revoked staple, default checking: exit 60 with the "revocation status is unknown" text. `--cert-status` is a no-op on both sides on Windows.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Networking.UnitLibrary\ServerCertificateVerification.cs:108-126` (`ReadChainAnchors`). It builds its own `X509ChainPolicy` with `RevocationMode.Online` and never gives it the stapled response. Lines 386-392 (`RevocationBestEffortTolerates`) then mask the resulting RevocationStatusUnknown/OfflineRevocation.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-015"></a>
### CGR-015: Windows: non-ASCII command-line text is sent as UTF-8 for bodies, URLs, `--data-urlencode`, `--url-query`, `-w` and several non-HTTP protocols, while header-like options use the ANSI code page; REF uses the ANSI code page for all of them

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** cli-options, url-parsing, http-requests, writeout-verbose, other-protocols, environment, upstream-cases
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [cli-options CLIO-01] Confirmed (reproduced by the finder and re-run by the verifier); [http-requests HR-4] Confirmed: reproduced 2/2 on Windows.; [writeout-verbose WV-19] Confirmed against the designated REF (the Git ucrt64 build). Note that this depends on how curl was built (ANSI argv vs wmain/UTF-8), so a differently built curl.exe may behave like PORT. A `-w @file` with UTF-8 bytes matches.; [other-protocols OP-8] Confirmed (verifier re-ran this on Windows).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0021
- **Source findings:** `cli-options CLIO-01`, `url-parsing UP-06`, `http-requests HR-4`, `writeout-verbose WV-19`, `other-protocols OP-8`, `environment ENV-07`, `upstream-cases UC-5`

Build note from the verifiers: REF is a non-UNICODE (ANSI argv) build. A UNICODE Windows curl (for example `C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe` 8.21, used only as a cross-check) converts every argument to UTF-8, headers included. The port matches neither build: it mixes UTF-8 and ANSI within one request. The fix must at least make the port consistent with itself; matching the designated oracle means using the ANSI code page everywhere REF does.

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (cli-options):* Evidence `SCR\evidence\cli-options`. Windows: start the echo server `pwsh -NoProfile -File SCR\evidence\cli-options\echoserver.ps1 -Port 20000` (replies 200 with the raw request bytes as the body); `@U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20000/`; port 20002 is left closed. Harness: `SCR\evidence\cli-options\h.sh <name> <args>` runs REF and PORT and stores exit code, stdout, stderr and files. Linux: `python3 linux/echo.py 20001` (in the evidence folder); `URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:20001/`. Verifier scripts: `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v4_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (url-parsing):* E = `SCR\evidence\url-parsing`. Windows server: `E\srvbin\server.exe 20200 E\rec` (or `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20200 E\rec`); it records raw requests and replies `200 ok`, except that a request target containing `__loc=X` gets a 302 with `Location:` = URL-decoded X. Linux: `python3 lharness.py vcases.py` (or `vcases2.py`) from `E\wsl` (server on 20210). Re-run every case: `pwsh -File E\verify.ps1` (outputs `E\cases\v*`).
- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- *Setup (writeout-verbose):* EV = `SCR\evidence\writeout-verbose`. Windows server: `cd EV\srv && dotnet run wvsrv.cs -- 20700 EV\resp EV\req.log` (HTTP on 127.0.0.1/::1:20700, a mini FTP server on 20701, TLS on 20702; `/raw/<name>` serves `EV\resp\<name>.txt`; other routes `/code/N`, `/redir/N`, `/hang/ms`, `/close` (empty reply), `/ka`, `/echo`, `/p`). Linux: `EV\linux\srv.py` on 20710. One-line repros for every finding: `EV\repro_findings.sh` (Windows) and `EV\linux\verify_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (other-protocols):* EV = `SCR\evidence\other-protocols`. Scripted per-protocol loopback servers and runner in `EV\bench\Program.cs`; Windows `pwsh -File EV\run.ps1 <file>.cases [filter]`, Linux `bash EV/run.sh <file>.cases` (set `FILTER=`) or `EV/verify-linux.sh [filter]`. Each `.cases` line is `name | server-mode | server options | curl args`. - *Setup (environment):* EV = `SCR\evidence\environment`. Windows: `dotnet run EV\server.cs 21200` (echo server: returns the raw request as the body; `/bin` returns bytes 0..255) and `dotnet run EV\s2\server2.cs 21201` (same, used as a proxy). `EV\verify_windows.ps1` runs each case in isolated `aref`/`port` directories with HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA at an empty directory. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` and `EV\linux\vtls.sh` (echo on 21210, proxy on 21211, `openssl s_server` on 21213).

Cross-platform runs: `EV\verify\diff.sh`, driven in WSL by `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "/mnt/c/Users/Stewart Rogers/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/Z--repos-Curl-ThirdPartyReview/3796612b-55d9-44ec-9722-80e35c3282a1/scratchpad/evidence/upstream-cases/verify/sync.sh" vN.sh` (N = 1..4), against the canned recording server `EV\verify\srv.py` (configs in `EV\verify\conf\`). Windows-native runs: `EV\verify\vwin.ps1` (wraps `harness\Diff-Curl.ps1` and `Record-CurlExchange.ps1`).
- **[cli-options CLIO-01]** Non-ASCII arguments on Windows: PORT sends bodies, URLs and -w output as UTF-8; REF converts argv to the ANSI code page
  - *(echo server on 20000):* `curl -s -d "é" @U`; `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:20000/é"`; `curl -s -o NUL -w "é" @U`; `curl -s --data-urlencode "é" @U`; `curl -s -d "中" @U`; `curl -s -o "中.txt" @U`; `curl --sílent @U`; `curl -sS "http://中文.localhost:20000/"`. Scripts: `repro/r01_unicode_win.sh`, `verify/v1_win.sh`.
- **[url-parsing UP-06]** Windows: non-ASCII command-line arguments are taken as UTF-8, where the reference build reads them in the ANSI code page
  - `curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:20200/café"` (v06_argv_ansi)
  - `curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:2020<U+FF10>/a"`, where U+FF10 is the full-width digit zero (v06b_port_fw)
- **[http-requests HR-4]** On Windows, request bodies and URLs built from command-line text use UTF-8, while REF uses the ANSI code page (cp1252). Header options use ANSI in both, so the port is inconsistent with itself.
  - On a cp1252 system:
    - `curl -sS -d é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
    - `curl -sS --data-urlencode é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
    - `curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:20335/é`
    - `curl -sS --url-query q=é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`

    The cases are v4_* in `E\verify.json`. The finder's cases are in `E\c4.json`, `E\c19.json` and `E\c24.json`, which also cover `--json`, `--request-target`, `-T ü.txt` and CJK file names.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-19]** Non-ASCII literal text in -w on Windows is written as UTF-8; REF writes ANSI code page bytes
  - `curl -s -o NUL -w 'café ü €\n' http://127.0.0.1:20700/`, run from Git Bash.
- **[other-protocols OP-8]** On Windows, non-ASCII command-line text reaches the wire as UTF-8 in several places where curl sends ANSI (cp1252) bytes
  - `EV\enc.cases` and `EV\enc2.cases`. Commands:
    - `curl -s -S -d "héllo" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t` (also with `--data-binary` and `--data-raw`)
    - `curl -s -S --data-urlencode "héllo" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t`
    - `curl -s -S "gopher://127.0.0.1:21001/0/é"`
    - `curl -s -S "dict://127.0.0.1:21001/d:é"`
    - `curl -s -S -u u:p -X "XFOO é" pop3://127.0.0.1:21001/` (also with `€`)
    - `curl -s -S -d "€" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t`
- **[environment ENV-07]** Non-ASCII argument text is sent as UTF-8 for `-d`/`--data-urlencode`/URL path/`-w` (and `--json`, `--data-raw`, `--data-binary`, `--variable`), but as ANSI for `-H`/`-A`/`-b`/`-e`/`-X`/`-F`/`-u`
  - `curl -s -d x=é http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`
  - `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21200/é`
  - `curl -s --data-urlencode x=é ...`
  - `curl -s -o NUL -w é ...`
  - Compare with `curl -s -H "X-U: é" ...`
  - Verifier cases: v-d-latin, v-url-latin, v-urlenc-latin, v-w-latin and v-H-latin.
- **[upstream-cases UC-5]** Windows: non-ASCII command-line text is sent as UTF-8 in the URL, -d, --data-urlencode, --url-query and -w, where REF-WIN uses the ANSI code page. PORT still uses ANSI for -H
  - `verify\vwin.ps1` (cases `v_cp_*`, port 21370, canned 200 reply). Each command is run natively on Windows:
    - `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:21370/“é"`
    - `curl -s -H "X-A: café" -d "v=é" http://127.0.0.1:21370/x`
    - `curl -s --data-urlencode v=é --url-query q=é http://127.0.0.1:21370/x`
    - `curl -s -o NUL -w "[é]" http://127.0.0.1:21370/x`

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [cli-options CLIO-01]
curl -s -d "é" @U
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:20000/é"
curl -s -o NUL -w "é" @U
curl -s --data-urlencode "é" @U
curl -s -d "中" @U
curl -s -o "中.txt" @U
curl --sílent @U
curl -sS "http://中文.localhost:20000/"
# [url-parsing UP-06]
curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:20200/café"
curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:2020<U+FF10>/a"
# [http-requests HR-4]
curl -sS -d é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
curl -sS --data-urlencode é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:20335/é
curl -sS --url-query q=é http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
# [writeout-verbose WV-19]
curl -s -o NUL -w 'café ü €\n' http://127.0.0.1:20700/
# [other-protocols OP-8]
curl -s -S -d "héllo" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t
curl -s -S --data-urlencode "héllo" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t
curl -s -S "gopher://127.0.0.1:21001/0/é"
curl -s -S "dict://127.0.0.1:21001/d:é"
curl -s -S -u u:p -X "XFOO é" pop3://127.0.0.1:21001/
curl -s -S -d "€" mqtt://127.0.0.1:21001/t
# [environment ENV-07]
curl -s -d x=é http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21200/é
curl -s --data-urlencode x=é ...
curl -s -o NUL -w é ...
curl -s -H "X-U: é" ...
# [upstream-cases UC-5]
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:21370/“é"
curl -s -H "X-A: café" -d "v=é" http://127.0.0.1:21370/x
curl -s --data-urlencode v=é --url-query q=é http://127.0.0.1:21370/x
curl -s -o NUL -w "[é]" http://127.0.0.1:21370/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[cli-options CLIO-01]** everything goes through code page 1252. `-d é` sends 0xE9 with Content-Length 1. The URL is sent as `/%E9`. `-w` writes 0xE9 and `--data-urlencode` gives `%E9`. `-d 中` sends `?`, and `-o 中.txt` creates `_.txt`. The unknown-option message echoes the ANSI byte. `http://中文.localhost` gives exit 3 "URL rejected: No host present".
- **[url-parsing UP-06]** 
  - Sends `GET /caf%E9`. `%{url_effective}` is written as CP1252 bytes.
  - The full-width digit is best-fit mapped to `0`, so the request connects to port 20200 and exits 0.
- **[http-requests HR-4]** 
  - `-d é` sends body `\xe9` with `Content-Length: 1`
  - `--data-urlencode é` sends `%E9`
  - the URL path becomes `/%E9`
  - `--url-query` gives `?q=%E9`
- **[writeout-verbose WV-19]** `63 61 66 E9 20 FC 20 80 0D 0A` (cp1252)
- **[other-protocols OP-8]** *REF behaviour (cp1252 bytes):* 
  - MQTT payload `68 E9 6C 6C 6F`
  - `--data-urlencode` payload `h%E9llo`
  - gopher selector `/\xE9`
  - dict `DEFINE ! \xE9`
  - POP3 `XFOO \xE9` and `XFOO \x80`
  - MQTT `€` sent as `80`
- **[environment ENV-07]** cp1252 everywhere:
  - `-d` sends body `x=` E9 (Content-Length 3).
  - The URL request line is `GET /%E9`.
  - `--data-urlencode` sends `x=%E9`.
  - `-w` writes E9.
  - `-H` sends E9.
- **[upstream-cases UC-5]** 
  - URL: `GET /%93%E9`
  - Body: `v=\xE9` with Content-Length: 3
  - Query: `?q=%E9`, and the urlencoded body is `v=%E9`
  - -w writes byte E9
  - -H sends E9

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[cli-options CLIO-01]** the `-H` header value matches REF (ANSI), but bodies, URLs and `-w` are UTF-8. `-d é` sends C3 A9 with Content-Length 2, the URL becomes `/%C3%A9`, `-w` writes C3 A9 and `--data-urlencode` gives `%C3%A9`. `-d 中` sends E4 B8 AD, `-o 中.txt` creates `中.txt`, and the message reads `--sílent` in UTF-8. The IDN URL succeeds with `Host: xn--fiq228c.localhost:20000`. The same argv is therefore encoded two ways depending on the option.
- **[url-parsing UP-06]** 
  - Sends `GET /caf%C3%A9`, and `%{url_effective}` is written in UTF-8.
  - The full-width digit gives exit 3, `Port number was not a decimal number between 0 and 65535`.
- **[http-requests HR-4]** 
  - `-d é` sends `\xc3\xa9` with `Content-Length: 2`
  - `--data-urlencode é` sends `%C3%A9`
  - the URL path becomes `/%C3%A9`
  - `--url-query` gives `?q=%C3%A9`
  - The control case `-H "X: é"` sends `\xe9` in both binaries.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-19]** `63 61 66 C3 A9 20 C3 BC 20 E2 82 AC 0D 0A` (UTF-8)
- **[other-protocols OP-8]** *PORT behaviour (UTF-8 bytes):* 
  - `68 C3 A9 6C 6C 6F`
  - `h%C3%A9llo`
  - `/\xC3\xA9`
  - `DEFINE ! \xC3\xA9`
  - `XFOO \xC3\xA9` and `XFOO \xE2\x82\xAC`
  - `E2 82 AC`
  - The PORT is not consistent with itself: SMTP `-d`, `-u` and SMTP `-X` use cp1252 and match REF.
- **[environment ENV-07]** 
  - `-d` sends `x=` C3 A9 (4).
  - The URL request line is `GET /%C3%A9`.
  - `--data-urlencode` sends `x=%C3%A9`.
  - `-w` writes C3 A9.
  - `-H` sends E9, the same as REF.
- **[upstream-cases UC-5]** 
  - URL: `GET /%E2%80%9C%C3%A9`
  - Body: `v=\xC3\xA9` with Content-Length: 4
  - Query: `?q=%C3%A9`, and the urlencoded body is `v=%C3%A9`
  - -w writes C3 A9
  - -H sends E9, the same as REF. PORT is therefore inconsistent with itself.

**Notes**

- **[url-parsing UP-06]** *Verifier note:* the Microsoft-shipped `C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe` is a UNICODE build. Checked for information only, not as the oracle, it sends `GET /caf%C3%A9` like PORT. The difference therefore comes from the non-UNICODE mingw REF build. It is a mismatch with the designated oracle, but arguably not a defect.
- **[http-requests HR-4]** *Note:* REF here is the MSYS2 ucrt64 (ANSI) build. Unicode builds of curl for Windows convert argv to UTF-8 and would send what the port sends. Even so, the port does not match the REF oracle, and it mixes the two encodings within one request.
- **[environment ENV-07]** *Build note:* REF is a non-UNICODE build. A UNICODE build (`C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe` 8.21) sends UTF-8 for both `-d` and `-H`. The port therefore matches neither build: it uses UTF-8 for data, URL and write-out, and ANSI for headers.
- **[upstream-cases UC-5]** *Verifier note:* This difference depends on how curl was built. REF-WIN (Git for Windows ucrt64) is an ANSI build. A Unicode Windows build of curl converts every argument to UTF-8, -H included. PORT matches neither build completely.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[cli-options CLIO-01]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/CommandLineOptions.cs:2377` (`AppendPostData` uses `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes`); `CommandLineOptionTable.cs` (the data-urlencode and json rows).
- **[url-parsing UP-06]** `Curl.Console` entry point (the arguments are encoded as UTF-8).
- **[http-requests HR-4]** 
  - `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/CommandLineOptions.cs:2377` (`AppendPostData` uses `Encoding.UTF8`)
  - `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/CommandLineOptionTable.cs:836`, `:972` and `:979`
  - `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpUrlText.cs:26`
  - `HttpRequestHeadFormatter.cs:228`
- **[writeout-verbose WV-19]** `Curl.Output.UnitLibrary/WriteOutTemplateRenderer.cs:101`
- **[other-protocols OP-8]** the per-protocol conversion from argument to bytes: the MQTT payload, `GopherSelector`, the DICT request and the POP3 control channel.
- **[environment ENV-07]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary` `CommandLineOptions.AsWireText` (ANSI) is applied only to the header-like options.
- **[upstream-cases UC-5]** argument decoding in Curl.Console / Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-016"></a>
### CGR-016: Linux: invalid UTF-8 bytes in arguments are replaced with U+FFFD before use

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** cli-options
- **Platform(s):** Linux
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. curl never re-encodes argv, so this does not depend on the REF version.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `cli-options CLIO-02`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (cli-options):* Evidence `SCR\evidence\cli-options`. Windows: start the echo server `pwsh -NoProfile -File SCR\evidence\cli-options\echoserver.ps1 -Port 20000` (replies 200 with the raw request bytes as the body); `@U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20000/`; port 20002 is left closed. Harness: `SCR\evidence\cli-options\h.sh <name> <args>` runs REF and PORT and stores exit code, stdout, stderr and files. Linux: `python3 linux/echo.py 20001` (in the evidence folder); `URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:20001/`. Verifier scripts: `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v4_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- *(WSL, echo.py on 20001):* `curl -s -d $'\xff' URL`; `-H $'X-A: \xff'`; `$'http://127.0.0.1:20001/\xff'`; `-o $'\xff.txt'`; `-o /dev/null -w $'\xfe'`; `--data-urlencode $'\xff'`; `-b $'a=\xff'`. Scripts: `linux/t3.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -s -d $'\xff' URL
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- the raw bytes are sent. Body 0xFF, header `X-A: \xff`, `GET /%FF`, file `\xff.txt`, `-w` writes 0xFE, `%FF`, `Cookie: a=\xff`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- every invalid byte becomes EF BF BD. Body EF BF BD (Content-Length 3), the header value EF BF BD, `GET /%EF%BF%BD`, file `EF BF BD.txt`, `-w` writes EF BF BD, `%EF%BF%BD`. The cookie value becomes `?`.

**Suspected location in source**

- argv reaches .NET already decoded as UTF-8 (Curl.Console Program entry) and is re-encoded per option, e.g. `CommandLineOptions.cs:2377`.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.
