<a id="cgr-017"></a>
### CGR-017: Reading stdin twice in one command line (two `@-` consumers, `-K -` plus `@-`, or `@-` across `--next`) aborts with exit 2 and a .NET "Cannot access a closed Stream" message before sending anything

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** config-glob-output, cli-options, http-requests, parallel-multi-transfer
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [config-glob-output CGO-01] Confirmed. The verifier reproduced it on Windows (8.22) and Linux (8.18 agrees with 8.22).; [http-requests HR-1] Confirmed: reproduced 2/2 on Windows and 2/2 on Linux.; [parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1] Confirmed (Windows reproduced in the verifier run, Linux too)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0007, GF-0082
- **Source findings:** `config-glob-output CGO-01`, `cli-options CLIO-03`, `http-requests HR-1`, `parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1`

All four areas trace this to one root cause: `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/DiskDataFileReader.cs` (`ReadStandardInput`, about lines 98-104) opens the process stdin with `using Stream standardInput = openStandardInput();`, so the first reader disposes it. curl reads stdin once and gives every later reader EOF (empty data).

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (config-glob-output):* E = `SCR\evidence\config-glob-output`. Windows server: `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20102 E\verify\log.txt` (listens on 127.0.0.1 and [::1], logs raw requests, replies `200 OK` with body `path=<request target>`; query keys `lm=` adds Last-Modified, `cd=`/`cdhex=` add Content-Disposition, `size=n` body of n `A`, `short=n` over-declares Content-Length, `status=n`). Linux: `python3 E/linux/server.py 20103 log`. `$U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20102` (20103 on Linux). Run each case in a fresh directory with HOME, USERPROFILE and APPDATA pointing at it and CURL_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset. Verifier scripts: `E\verify\v1_stdin.ps1`, `v2_misc.ps1`, `v3_misc.ps1`, `v4_maxpath.ps1`, `E\verify\linux\vl.sh`.
- *Setup (cli-options):* Evidence `SCR\evidence\cli-options`. Windows: start the echo server `pwsh -NoProfile -File SCR\evidence\cli-options\echoserver.ps1 -Port 20000` (replies 200 with the raw request bytes as the body); `@U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20000/`; port 20002 is left closed. Harness: `SCR\evidence\cli-options\h.sh <name> <args>` runs REF and PORT and stores exit code, stdout, stderr and files. Linux: `python3 linux/echo.py 20001` (in the evidence folder); `URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:20001/`. Verifier scripts: `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v4_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- *Setup (parallel-multi-transfer):* EV = `SCR\evidence\parallel-multi-transfer`. Server: `dotnet run EV\srv\server.cs -- 22000,22001 EV\srv\log` (listens on 127.0.0.1:22000 and :22001; query `d=` delay in ms, `s=` status, `n=` body size, `p=`/`pd=` send the body in parts with a delay, `close=1` adds Connection: close; other paths return `body /<path>`); port 22099 is closed. Linux: `EV/linux/srv.py 22000,22001 /tmp/pmt_srv` (started by `EV/linux/lt.sh`). Harness `EV\dt.ps1`; verifier `EV\v1.ps1` and `EV/linux/vl.sh`.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-01]** A second read of stdin makes the port abort with exit 2 and a .NET "Cannot access a closed Stream" message
  - each command below is run with the given text piped to stdin.
    - stdin `url = $U/s\n`:
      - `curl -sS -K - -d @-`
      - `curl -sS -K - -H @-`
      - `curl -sS -K - -K -`
    - stdin `X-H: 1\n`:
      - `curl -sS -d @- -H @- $U/s6`
      - `curl -sS -H @- -H @- $U/s7`
      - `curl -sS -d @- -d @- $U/s8`
      - `curl -sS -d @- $U/a --next -d @- $U/b`
    - Scripts: `E\verify\v1_stdin.ps1` (Windows) and `E\verify\linux\vl.sh` cases s1, s4 and s7 (Linux). The originals are `E\b_stdin.ps1` and `E\b_rc.ps1` (ks03, ks04).
- **[cli-options CLIO-03]** Reading stdin twice (two `@-` arguments) fails with .NET "Cannot access a closed Stream" and exit 2
  - `curl -s -d @- --data-binary @- @U < linux/stdin1.bin`; `curl -s -H @- -d @- @U < linux/stdin1.bin`. Scripts: `repro/r03_stdin_twice_win.sh`, `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- **[http-requests HR-1]** A second read of standard input makes Curl fail with exit 2 and print a .NET exception message
  - Any loopback server that answers 200, for example the harness. Run each of these:
    - `printf 'abc\n' | curl -sS -d @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
    - `printf 'X-A: 1\n' | curl -sS -H @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
    - `printf 'header = "X-K: 1"\n' | curl -sS -K - -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
    - `printf abc | curl -sS -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/b`
    - `printf 'X-A: 1\n' | curl -sS -H @- -T - http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`

    The cases are v1_* in `E\verify.json`.
- **[parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1]** Reading stdin twice in one command line makes PORT fail with exit 2 and a .NET exception before it sends anything
  - start the server. Pipe `STDIN-DATA-123` (no newline) into each command:
    - `curl -s -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b` (also the same command with `-Z`)
    - `curl -s -d @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a`
    - `curl -s --json @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next --json @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b`
    - `curl -s -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -T - http://127.0.0.1:22000/b`
    - `curl -s -T - http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b`

    Scripts: `v1.ps1` (v_d_twice, v_d_twice_Z, v_dd_same, v_json_next, v_d_then_T, v_T_then_d), `linux/vl.sh` (vl_d_twice). Older runs: `b9.ps1` and `b10.ps1`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [config-glob-output CGO-01]
curl -sS -K - -d @-
curl -sS -K - -H @-
curl -sS -K - -K -
curl -sS -d @- -H @- $U/s6
curl -sS -H @- -H @- $U/s7
curl -sS -d @- -d @- $U/s8
curl -sS -d @- $U/a --next -d @- $U/b
E\verify\v1_stdin.ps1
E\verify\linux\vl.sh
E\b_stdin.ps1
E\b_rc.ps1
# [cli-options CLIO-03]
curl -s -d @- --data-binary @- @U < linux/stdin1.bin
curl -s -H @- -d @- @U < linux/stdin1.bin
# [http-requests HR-1]
printf 'abc\n' | curl -sS -d @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
printf 'X-A: 1\n' | curl -sS -H @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
printf 'header = "X-K: 1"\n' | curl -sS -K - -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
printf abc | curl -sS -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:20335/b
printf 'X-A: 1\n' | curl -sS -H @- -T - http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
# [parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1]
curl -s -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b
curl -s -d @- -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a
curl -s --json @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next --json @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b
curl -s -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -T - http://127.0.0.1:22000/b
curl -s -T - http://127.0.0.1:22000/a --next -d @- http://127.0.0.1:22000/b
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-01]** 
  - curl reads stdin once. Every later read gets EOF, which is empty data.
  - The transfer goes ahead with exit 0. Examples:
    - `-K - -d @-` sends `POST /s` with `Content-Length: 0`.
    - `-d @- -H @-` sends a POST whose body is `X-H: 1` and adds no extra header.
    - The `--next` case sends `POST /a` with the body, then `POST /b` with `Content-Length: 0`.
- **[cli-options CLIO-03]** exit 0. The first `@-` gets all of stdin and the second gets nothing. The body is `line1line2bin&` (Content-Length 14), and `-H @- -d @-` sends Content-Length 0.
- **[http-requests HR-1]** Exits 0 and sends the request. The first `@-` gets the stdin bytes and later reads get an empty string. `-d @- -d @-` sends `Content-Length: 4` with body `abc&`. `-H @- -d @-` sends `X-A: 1` with `Content-Length: 0`. `--next` sends POST /a with `abc`, then POST /b with an empty body. `-H @- -T -` sends `PUT` chunked with `0\r\n\r\n`.
- **[parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1]** exit 0. The first `@-` reads the 14 bytes and later reads get an empty body (POST /b with Content-Length: 0). stdout is `body /a\nbody /b\n`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-01]** 
  - No request is sent, not even the first transfer of a `--next` chain.
  - Exit 2, with this on stderr:
    ```
    curl: (2) Cannot access a closed Stream.
    Object name: 'WindowsConsoleStream'.
    ```
    On Linux the object name is `'UnixConsoleStream'`.
  - The original tester found two combinations that do not fail: `-T -` given twice, and `-F` with both `@-` and `<-`.
- **[cli-options CLIO-03]** exit 2 and no request is sent. stderr reads `curl: (2) Cannot access a closed Stream.` followed by `Object name: 'WindowsConsoleStream'.` (`'UnixConsoleStream'` on Linux).
- **[http-requests HR-1]** Exits 2, stdout is empty, and no request is sent. stderr is `curl: (2) Cannot access a closed Stream.` followed by `Object name: 'WindowsConsoleStream'.` (on Linux the object name is `'UnixConsoleStream'`). With `-H @- -T -` the port sends the request head with no body or terminating chunk, then prints `curl: (2) Stream does not support reading.` A single `-d @-` works and matches REF.
- **[parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1]** exit 2 and no request is sent. stderr is `curl: (2) Cannot access a closed Stream.` followed by `Object name: 'WindowsConsoleStream'.` (`'UnixConsoleStream'` on Linux). The `-d @-` / `-T -` combinations give `curl: (2) Stream does not support reading.` instead. For `-d @- … --next -T -`, the first transfer completes (`body /a`) before the failure.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-01]** 
  - `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/DiskDataFileReader.cs:98-104`: `ReadStandardInput` opens stdin with `using Stream standardInput = openStandardInput();`, so the process stdin stream is disposed after the first read.
  - The exception is turned into `curl: (2) <message>` at `Curl.Console/UnhandledExceptionGuard.cs:31-37`.
- **[cli-options CLIO-03]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/DiskDataFileReader.cs:100` (`using Stream standardInput = openStandardInput();` disposes the process stdin).
- **[http-requests HR-1]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/DiskDataFileReader.cs:98-103`. `ReadStandardInput` wraps the stream in `using Stream standardInput = openStandardInput();`, which disposes the process-wide stdin stream opened in `Curl.Console/Program.cs:19`. The next reader gets a closed stream.
- **[parallel-multi-transfer PMT-1]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/DiskDataFileReader.cs:98-103`. `ReadStandardInput` opens and disposes `Console.OpenStandardInput()` on every call. It is called from `CommandLineOptionTable.cs:716/887/1055`, so a second read hits the disposed console stream.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-018: A redirect to `localhost:20200/x` (scheme-like text with no `//`) is followed as http to a different host, where curl refuses it as an unsupported scheme

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** url-parsing
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. Reproduced by the original tester and by the verifier, on Windows (8.22) and on Linux.

- **Source findings:** `url-parsing UP-01`

**Reproduction**

Windows server: `E\srvbin\server.exe 20200 E\rec` (or `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20200 E\rec`); it records raw requests and replies `200 ok`, except that a request target containing `__loc=X` gets a 302 with `Location:` = URL-decoded X. Linux: `python3 lharness.py vcases.py` (or `vcases2.py`) from `E\wsl` (server on 20210). Re-run every case: `pwsh -File E\verify.ps1` (outputs `E\cases\v*`).
- `curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=localhost:20200/x" -w "[%{url_effective}]"`
  - Windows case: v01_redir_noscheme.
  - Linux case: lv01_redir_noscheme (port 20210).

```sh
curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=localhost:20200/x" -w "[%{url_effective}]"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- Exit 1, with stderr `curl: (1) The redirect target URL could not be parsed: Unsupported URL scheme`.
- Only the first request is sent.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Exit 0.
- Sends a second request, `GET /x HTTP/1.1` with `Host: localhost:20200`, and prints `ok`.

### CGR-019: IDN hosts get no UTS#46 mapping, so a different punycode host is contacted

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** url-parsing
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. The Windows cases ran against REF 8.22, and the Linux results agree with them.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0028
- **Source findings:** `url-parsing UP-02`

**Reproduction**

Windows server: `E\srvbin\server.exe 20200 E\rec` (or `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20200 E\rec`); it records raw requests and replies `200 ok`, except that a request target containing `__loc=X` gets a 302 with `Location:` = URL-decoded X. Linux: `python3 lharness.py vcases.py` (or `vcases2.py`) from `E\wsl` (server on 20210). Re-run every case: `pwsh -File E\verify.ps1` (outputs `E\cases\v*`).

  - `curl -sS "http://BÜCHER.example:20200/a" --connect-to ::127.0.0.1:20200` (v02_idn_upper_raw)
  - `curl -sS "http://École.example:20200/a" --connect-to ::127.0.0.1:20200` (v02b_idn_E_raw)
- *, Linux:* the same command with each of these hosts: ΣΣ, İstanbul, Ａb (full-width A), ﬁle, a+U+00AD+b, a+U+200D+b, e+U+0301+cole. These are cases lv02_idn_* in `E\wsl\vcases.py`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh

```

**Expected (real curl)**

- *REF behaviour (Host header):* 

  | Input host | REF sends |
  |---|---|
  | BÜCHER | `xn--bcher-kva` |
  | École | `xn--cole-9oa` |
  | ΣΣ | `xn--4xaa` |
  | İstanbul | `xn--istanbul-o0e` |
  | Ａb | `ab` |
  | ﬁle | `file` |
  | a+soft hyphen+b, a+ZWJ+b | `ab` |
  | e+combining acute+cole | `xn--cole-9oa` |

**Actual (Curl)**

- sends `xn--bcher-2pa`, `xn--cole-pka`, `xn--7waa`, `xn--stanbul-ifb`, `xn--b-4o0i`, `xn--le-1b1n`, `xn--ab-5da`, `xn--ab-m1t` and `xn--ecole-6ed`, all with exit 0. The request goes to a different host name from the one curl uses.

<a id="cgr-020"></a>
### CGR-020: Header text read from a file (`-H @file`, `--proxy-header @file`, `-F ...;headers=@file`, and `-K` cookie/request values) is decoded and re-encoded instead of sent byte for byte

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** http-requests, environment
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: [http-requests HR-2] Both (the symptoms differ by platform)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [http-requests HR-2] Confirmed: reproduced 2/2 on Windows and 2/2 on Linux.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `http-requests HR-2`, `environment ENV-02`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- *Setup (environment):* EV = `SCR\evidence\environment`. Windows: `dotnet run EV\server.cs 21200` (echo server: returns the raw request as the body; `/bin` returns bytes 0..255) and `dotnet run EV\s2\server2.cs 21201` (same, used as a proxy). `EV\verify_windows.ps1` runs each case in isolated `aref`/`port` directories with HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA at an empty directory. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` and `EV\linux\vtls.sh` (echo on 21210, proxy on 21211, `openssl s_server` on 21213).
- **[http-requests HR-2]** Header text read from a file is decoded and re-encoded instead of sent byte for byte (-H @file, --proxy-header @file, -F ...;headers=@file, and -K cookie/request values)
  - Run `curl -sS -H @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:20335/a` with each of these h.txt files:
    - h.txt = bytes `X: \xc3\xa9\xe4\xb8\xad\n`
    - h.txt = bytes `X: \xe9\xff\n`

    Then run `curl -sS -K k.txt http://127.0.0.1:20335/a` with each of these k.txt files:
    - k.txt = `cookie = "c=\xc3\xa9"`
    - k.txt = `request = "\xc3\xa9"`

    The cases are v2_* in `E\verify.json`. The finder's cases are in `E\c20.json`, which also covers `--proxy-header @file` and `-F a=b;headers=@file`.
- **[environment ENV-02]** `-H @file`, `--proxy-header @file` and `-F "x;headers=@file"` re-encode the file's bytes to the ANSI code page, so non-cp1252 bytes become `?`
  - Create `h.txt` holding the UTF-8 text `X-C: 日本` followed by LF.
    - `curl -s -H @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`
    - `curl -s -x 127.0.0.1:21201 --proxy-header @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`
    - `curl -s -F "a=b;headers=@h.txt" http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo`, with `h.txt` = `X-C: é日本`
    - A file holding the raw bytes `X-C: ` FF 80 C3 28 behaves the same way.
    - Verifier cases: v-Hfile, v-Hfile-bin, v-pxhfile and v-Ffile.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-requests HR-2]
curl -sS -H @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
curl -sS -K k.txt http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
# [environment ENV-02]
curl -s -H @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
curl -s -x 127.0.0.1:21201 --proxy-header @h.txt http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
curl -s -F "a=b;headers=@h.txt" http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-requests HR-2]** Copies the file bytes unchanged:
  - the UTF-8 file sends `X: \xc3\xa9\xe4\xb8\xad`
  - the Latin-1 file sends `X: \xe9\xff`
  - the -K cookie sends `Cookie: c=\xc3\xa9`
  - the -K request sends the request line `\xc3\xa9 /a HTTP/1.1`
- **[environment ENV-02]** Sends the file's bytes unchanged: `X-C: E6 97 A5 E6 9C AC`. The raw bytes go out as FF 80 C3 28.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-requests HR-2]** 
  - Windows: the UTF-8 file sends `X: \xe9?` (re-encoded to cp1252, and the CJK character becomes `?`). The Latin-1 file sends `X: ??`. The -K cookie sends `Cookie: c=\xe9` and the -K request sends `\xe9 /a`.
  - Linux: the UTF-8 header file matches REF. The Latin-1 file sends `X: \xef\xbf\xbd\xef\xbf\xbd` (two U+FFFD characters). The -K cookie sends `c=\xe9` and the -K request sends `\xe9 /a`.
  - The -K `header = "X: \xc3\xa9"` case matches REF on both platforms.
- **[environment ENV-02]** 
  - `-H` and `--proxy-header` send `X-C: ??`. The raw bytes go out as `???(`.
  - `-F` sends `X-C: E9 3F 3F`.
  - The header grows shorter and the original bytes are lost.

**Notes**

- **[environment ENV-02]** *Why this is not build-dependent:* upstream curl never transcodes file content, so a UNICODE curl build sends the raw bytes too.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-requests HR-2]** 
  - `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/CommandLineOptionTable.cs:1038` (`Encoding.UTF8.GetString(contents)` in the -H @file reader)
  - `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpRequestHeadFormatter.cs:158` (`Encoding.Latin1.GetBytes(head)`)
  - the method and cookie are appended raw (`HttpRequestHeadFormatter.cs:213` and `:150`)
- **[environment ENV-02]** 
  - `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary\CommandLineOptionTable.cs` (~1038) decodes the file to a string, which the HTTP formatter later encodes as ANSI.
  - The same pattern is in `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary\FormPartParameterReader.cs` (~185).

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

- **Source findings:** `writeout-verbose WV-03`, `http-responses HR-7`

Linux: `EV\linux\server.py` serves the same fixtures (verifier: port 20460 via `EV\verify\linux\vrun.sh`; port 20450 in the original runs).
- **[writeout-verbose WV-03]** Header-derived -w values are re-encoded Latin-1 to UTF-8, corrupting bytes 0x80 and above
  - `resp/hibit.txt` contains `X-Hi: caf\xc3\xa9 \xff\xfe end` and `Content-Type: text/\xe9`.
    - `curl -s -o NUL -w '%{content_type}|%header{x-hi}|%{header_json}\n' http://127.0.0.1:20700/raw/hibit`
- **[http-responses HR-7]** -w %header{}, %{header_json} and %{content_type} re-encode header bytes as UTF-8, double-encoding UTF-8 values
  - `m_hdr_w_high.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-A: caf\xe9 \xc3\xa9\r\nContent-Type: t/\xe9\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nok`.
    Command: `curl -s -S -o NUL -w "[%header{x-a}][%{content_type}]" http://127.0.0.1:20400/m_hdr_w_high`
  - `m_hdr_json_utf8v` (`X-A: caf\xc3\xa9`), run with `-w %{header_json}`.
  - `m_hdr_utf8_name` (header name `X-\xc3\xa9`), run with `-w %{header_json}`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh

curl -s -o NUL -w '%{content_type}|%header{x-hi}|%{header_json}\n' http://127.0.0.1:20700/raw/hibit
# [http-responses HR-7]
curl -s -S -o NUL -w "[%header{x-a}][%{content_type}]" http://127.0.0.1:20400/m_hdr_w_high
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-03]** Writes the raw bytes: `text/\xe9|caf\xc3\xa9 \xff\xfe end`. `%{header_json}` and `%{json}` carry the same raw bytes.
- **[http-responses HR-7]** writes the raw bytes: `[caf\xe9 \xc3\xa9][t/\xe9]`. header_json gives `"caf\xc3\xa9"`, and the name gives `"x-\xc3\xa9"`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-03]** `text/\xc3\xa9|caf\xc3\x83\xc2\xa9 \xc3\xbf\xc3\xbe end`. Every byte at or above 0x80 is UTF-8 encoded, so UTF-8 header values come out double-encoded (mojibake). This also affects `%header{location}`. `-v` and `-D` output match REF.
- **[http-responses HR-7]** treats the bytes as Latin-1 and writes them as UTF-8: `[caf\xc3\xa9 \xc3\x83\xc2\xa9][t/\xc3\xa9]`. header_json gives `"caf\xc3\x83\xc2\xa9"` (shown as `cafÃ©`), and the name is mangled to `x-\xc3\xa3\xc2\xa9`. Same on Linux.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-03]** `Curl.Output.UnitLibrary/WriteOutTemplateRenderer.cs:101`, where `Encode()` uses `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` on text whose header values were decoded as Latin-1.
- **[http-responses HR-7]** `Curl.Output.UnitLibrary\TransferWriteOutVariables.cs` / `WriteOutJson.cs`. Head bytes are held as Latin-1 strings (`HttpResponseHeadBuilder`) and encoded as UTF-8 on output.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-022"></a>
### CGR-022: `--ciphers` / `--proxy-ciphers` with Schannel ALG_ID names (CALG_*, USE_STRONG_CRYPTO) is rejected with exit 59

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** tls
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `tls TLS-03`

**Reproduction**

Harnesses `E\tlsdiff.ps1`, `E\linux\tlsdiff.sh`; verifier `E\verify\vwin1.ps1`, `vwin2.ps1`, `vlin.sh` (cases `E\cases\V_*`, `E\linux\cases\V_L_*`).

The same happens with `USE_STRONG_CRYPTO` and `CALG_AES_256` (also against a TLS 1.3 server), and with `CALG_3DES`. Cases: `V_calg_aes128`, `V_calg_strong`, `V_calg_tls13`, `V_calg_3des`. **Actual (Curl)**

**Suspected location in source**

Default servers: SMTP answers 250 and offers AUTH PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5 XOAUTH2 OAUTHBEARER; POP3 offers SASL PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5; IMAP offers AUTH=PLAIN AUTH=LOGIN AUTH=CRAM-MD5 SASL-IR.

  - e20: `curl -s -S -u u:p -X "XFOO €" imap://127.0.0.1:21001/`
  - e22: `curl -s -S -u "u€:p" "imap://127.0.0.1:21001/INBOX;UID=1"`

```sh
curl -s -S -u u:p -X 'XFOO é' imap://127.0.0.1:21084/
curl -s -S -u u:p -X "XFOO €" imap://127.0.0.1:21001/
curl -s -S -u "u€:p" "imap://127.0.0.1:21001/INBOX;UID=1"
```

- sends the argument bytes unchanged.
  - Linux: `A002 LOGIN us\xC3\xA9r p\xC3\xA4ss` and `A003 XFOO \xC3\xA9`
  - Windows (ANSI cp1252): `A002 LOGIN u\x80 p` and `A003 XFOO \x80`

**Actual (Curl)**

- Linux: `A002 LOGIN us\xE9r p\xE4ss` and `A003 XFOO \xE9`. UTF-8 credentials become Latin-1, so a real server rejects the login.
- Windows: `A002 LOGIN u? p` and `A003 XFOO ?`.
- SMTP and POP3 send the same strings correctly on Linux.

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Imap.UnitLibrary\ImapControlChannel.cs:188`: `Encoding.Latin1.GetBytes(text + "\r\n")`.

### CGR-026: A write error on an output, header, trace, cookie or `%output` file (ENOSPC, `/dev/full`) gives exit 2 with an exception message instead of exit 23, and `-w` output is lost

- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `network-robustness NR-2`, `config-glob-output CGO-09`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (network-robustness):* EV = `SCR\evidence\network-robustness`. Windows server: `EV\srvbin\server.exe 21100 21101` (source `EV\srv\server.cs`); repro script `EV\repro_findings.sh` (uses the `d.sh` diff harness). Linux: `python3 EV/linux/srv.py 21150 21151`; repro `EV/linux/verify_lin.sh`. `H=http://127.0.0.1:21100` (21150 on Linux); `b64() { printf "$1" | base64 -w0 | sed 's/+/%2B/g; s/\//%2F/g; s/=/%3D/g'; }`; `$H/raw?b=<b64>` replies with exactly those bytes (`&keep=1` keeps the connection).
- *Setup (config-glob-output):* E = `SCR\evidence\config-glob-output`. Windows server: `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20102 E\verify\log.txt` (listens on 127.0.0.1 and [::1], logs raw requests, replies `200 OK` with body `path=<request target>`; query keys `lm=` adds Last-Modified, `cd=`/`cdhex=` add Content-Disposition, `size=n` body of n `A`, `short=n` over-declares Content-Length, `status=n`). Linux: `python3 E/linux/server.py 20103 log`. `$U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20102` (20103 on Linux). Run each case in a fresh directory with HOME, USERPROFILE and APPDATA pointing at it and CURL_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset. Verifier scripts: `E\verify\v1_stdin.ps1`, `v2_misc.ps1`, `v3_misc.ps1`, `v4_maxpath.ps1`, `E\verify\linux\vl.sh`.
- **[network-robustness NR-2]** ENOSPC on an output file gives exit 2 instead of 23; a failed --trace/-c/%output write fails the run
  - *(WSL server 21150, H=http://127.0.0.1:21150):* `curl -sS -o /dev/full $H/ok`; `-D /dev/full -o /dev/null $H/ok`; `--trace /dev/full -o /dev/null $H/ok`; `-c /dev/full -o /dev/null $H/ok`; `-o /dev/null -w '%output{/dev/full}x' $H/ok`; `--stderr /dev/full http://127.0.0.1:21199/`; `-o /dev/full "$H/gen?size=20000"`. Script: `linux/run2.sh` + `linux/cases2.sh`.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-09]** A write error when the output file is closed (/dev/full, ENOSPC) gives exit 2 and an exception message instead of exit 23, and -w output is lost
  - in WSL, run `python3 E/linux/server.py 20103 log`, then:
    - `curl -sS -o /dev/full $U/x`
    - `curl -sS $U/x -o /dev/full -w '%{exitcode} %{errormsg}\n'`
    - `curl -sS --remove-on-error -o /dev/full $U/x`
    - Script: `vl.sh` df1/df3/df5.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [network-robustness NR-2]
curl -sS -o /dev/full $H/ok
# [config-glob-output CGO-09]
python3 E/linux/server.py 20103 log
curl -sS -o /dev/full $U/x
curl -sS $U/x -o /dev/full -w '%{exitcode} %{errormsg}\n'
curl -sS --remove-on-error -o /dev/full $U/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[network-robustness NR-2]** `curl: (23) Failed writing body` (23); `-D`: `Failed writing headers to /dev/full` + `(23) client returned ERROR on write of 17 bytes`; trace/-c/%output: exit 0 with no message; `--stderr /dev/full`: exit 7; for a body of 16 KiB or more: `(23) Failure writing output to destination, passed 16384 returned 0`.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-09]** *REF behaviour (8.18):* 
  - stderr `curl: curl: (23) Failed writing body`, exit 23.
  - `-w` prints `23 Failed writing received data to disk/application`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[network-robustness NR-2]** `curl: (2) No space left on device : '/dev/full'` with exit 2 for -o, -D, --trace, -c, %output and --stderr. For a body of 16 KiB or more it gives exit 23, but the message says `passed 16342` where curl says 16384.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-09]** 
  - stderr `curl: (2) No space left on device : '/dev/full'`, exit 2.
  - `-w` prints nothing.
  - With a 200 KB body, the failure happens during a write and both exit 23 (df2).

**Suspected location in source**

- **[network-robustness NR-2]** the IOException from the buffered flush/close is not turned into CURLE_WRITE_ERROR and falls to `Curl.Console/UnhandledExceptionGuard.cs:31`. See also `Curl.Console/DeferredOutputFileStream.cs`, `DumpHeaderOutputStream.cs`.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-09]** the `IOException` from flushing or disposing the output stream (`Curl.Console/DeferredOutputFileStream.cs`) is not mapped to CURLE_WRITE_ERROR. It reaches `Curl.Console/UnhandledExceptionGuard.cs:31-37`, which returns exit 2.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Linux: `dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained -o EV\verify\outlinux`, then `EV\verify\linux_verify.sh`.
- run `EV\probe\out\probe.exe repro` (section `CURLOPT_PUT=1 + INFILESIZE 15 + READFUNCTION`). The C equivalent is `curl_easy_setopt(h,CURLOPT_URL,"http://127.0.0.1:21410/f"); curl_easy_setopt(h,CURLOPT_PUT,1L); curl_easy_setopt(h,CURLOPT_INFILESIZE_LARGE,(curl_off_t)15); /* READFUNCTION supplying 15 bytes */ curl_easy_perform(h);`. The every-value sweep is `probe.exe sweep` (`EV\verify\sweep_v.txt`).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
EV\probe\out\probe.exe repro
CURLOPT_PUT=1 + INFILESIZE 15 + READFUNCTION
probe.exe sweep
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- setopt returns 0. The wire shows `PUT /f HTTP/1.1` with `Content-Length: 15` and the body. EFFECTIVE_METHOD=PUT, SIZE_UPLOAD_T=15.

**Actual (Curl)**

- setopt returns 4 for every value from -3 to 40 and for the edge values. The wire shows `GET /f HTTP/1.1` with no body. EFFECTIVE_METHOD=GET, SIZE_UPLOAD_T=0. Code that ignores the setopt result silently sends the wrong method.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Libcurl\Options\EasyOptionDispatch.cs:40`. No setter is registered for `CurlOption.Put`, so the dispatch falls back to `CurlCode.NotBuiltIn`.

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

<a id="cgr-031"></a>
### CGR-031: REFUSED_STREAM, and GOAWAY with a last-stream-id below the request, are not retried on a new connection; REF retries and succeeds

- **Severity:** High (servers commonly send GOAWAY or REFUSED_STREAM during graceful shutdown or overload, and curl hides this from the user)
- **Area:** http2-linux
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Both (PORT-WIN matches: `EV\win\x_rst7first`, `EV\win\x_gafirst`)
- **Confidence:** Probable. Detail: Probable (reproduced by the tester and the verifier on Linux and PORT-WIN; the REF retry logic lives in curl's own code, which can only be checked against 8.18)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `http2-linux H2L-5`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http2-linux):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http2-linux`. The Windows REF has no HTTP/2, so REF here is REF-LINUX 8.18.0 (nghttp2 1.68). Scripted HTTP/2 server (WSL, needs `libnghttp2.so.14`): `python3 EV/h2srv.py --port P --mode auto|tls|h1 --scen <SCEN> --log s.log [--alpn h2,http/1.1 --cert cert.pem --key key.pem] --life 25`. Harness `EV\run.sh <casefile>` (lines `name|scen|mode|args`); verifier `EV\verify\vrun.sh EV\verify\c_verify.txt` (ports 21612/21613); PORT-WIN: `WINPORT=<port> bash EV\winrun.sh <case>` (one port per case).
- Server scens, which act on connection 1 only:
  - `rst7first`: RST_STREAM REFUSED_STREAM.
  - `gafirst`: GOAWAY with last=0 and NO_ERROR, then close.
  - `gafirstia`: the same with INTERNAL_ERROR.
- Command: `curl -sS --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.1:P/x -w '\n[%{http_version} %{response_code} %{num_connects}]\n'`. TLS form: `curl -sSk https://127.0.0.1:P/x`.
- Cases: `x_rst7first`, `x_rst7first_tls`, `x_gafirst`, `x_gafirstia`, `x_gafirst_tls`.
- Always-refusing variants (`rst7`, `gabefore0`): REF gives up after 5 retries.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -sS --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.1:P/x -w '\n[%{http_version} %{response_code} %{num_connects}]\n'
curl -sSk https://127.0.0.1:P/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- opens a second connection, re-sends the request, prints `hello h2` and exits 0 with `[2 200 2]`. If the server always refuses, REF exits 56 with `curl: (56) Connection died, tried 5 times before giving up`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- no retry, `[0 000 1]`.
  - REFUSED_STREAM: exit 92, `curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly: REFUSED_STREAM (err 7)`.
  - GOAWAY: exit 56, `curl: (56) Failure when receiving data from the peer`.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary\Http2StreamConnection.cs:375` (every `Http2StreamResetException` becomes exit 92, and `Http2GoAwayException` becomes 56). `Http3StreamConnection.cs:300` has a request-rejected retry, but HTTP/2 does not.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF-LINUX's (the Windows REF has no HTTP/2), for both PORT-LINUX and PORT-WIN (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match. Re-check the expected behaviour against a curl 8.22.0 build first (the evidence is from REF-LINUX 8.18.0).

<a id="cgr-033"></a>
### CGR-033: Callbacks of multi-driven transfers run on background threads, outside curl_multi_perform

- **Severity:** High
- **Area:** libcurl-multi-callbacks
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Windows, Linux
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `libcurl-multi-callbacks LMC-2`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (libcurl-multi-callbacks):* EV = `SCR\evidence\libcurl-multi-callbacks`. A C# probe (`EV\probe\`) runs one driver per case against REF `libcurl-4.dll` (P/Invoke) and PORT `Libcurl.dll` (its C# API), with a built-in recording server: 127.0.0.1:21700 answers `200 hello`, 21701 answers `200 other`, 21799 is closed. Run `EV\probe\out\probe.exe <cases> 2` or `powershell -File EV\run.ps1 -Filter <cases> -Out <name> -Reps 2` (`LIBONLY=REF` or `LIBONLY=PORT` runs one side). Linux: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "<EV as /mnt/c path>/linux.sh" <cases> 1 <name>`.
- case `C_69_callback_thread`.
  1. The server sends the 200 head and the first 100000 body bytes, then the other 100000 bytes 200 ms later.
  2. A multi holds one easy handle. Its WRITEFUNCTION and HEADERFUNCTION record the thread id and whether the main thread is inside `curl_multi_perform`.
  3. The loop is `perform`, then `Sleep(30)`, with no poll.

  Command: `probe.exe C_69 2`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
probe.exe C_69 2
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- `header:caller-thread:inside-perform write:caller-thread:inside-perform`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- `header:other-thread:OUTSIDE-perform write:other-thread:OUTSIDE-perform`. Each added transfer runs as a background Task, and its callbacks run at the same time as the application's own code. C code that relies on libcurl's single-thread callback contract (no locking) gets data races.

**Notes**

- *Side effect (intermittent):* in `C_70_running_counts`, a handle removed right after the first perform still had its request sent (PORT `[GET /1] | [GET /2]`, REF `[GET /2]`). This happened in both Windows runs but not in the Linux run.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary\ManagedMultiTransfer.cs:824-830`. `Start` returns `Transfer.PerformAsync(...)` as a Task that runs on its own.

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

<a id="cgr-034"></a>
### CGR-034: curl_multi_socket_action reports synthetic socket numbers, never CURL_POLL_OUT, and a 10 ms polling timer instead of libcurl's timeouts

- **Severity:** High (applications that run their own event loop, such as libuv, libevent or epoll, cannot drive transfers)
- **Area:** libcurl-multi-callbacks
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux). Detail: Windows, Linux
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `libcurl-multi-callbacks LMC-3`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (libcurl-multi-callbacks):* EV = `SCR\evidence\libcurl-multi-callbacks`. A C# probe (`EV\probe\`) runs one driver per case against REF `libcurl-4.dll` (P/Invoke) and PORT `Libcurl.dll` (its C# API), with a built-in recording server: 127.0.0.1:21700 answers `200 hello`, 21701 answers `200 other`, 21799 is closed. Run `EV\probe\out\probe.exe <cases> 2` or `powershell -File EV\run.ps1 -Filter <cases> -Out <name> -Reps 2` (`LIBONLY=REF` or `LIBONLY=PORT` runs one side). Linux: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "<EV as /mnt/c path>/linux.sh" <cases> 1 <name>`.
- cases `C_20_sockaction_one`, `C_21_sockaction_three_assign`, `C_65_sockaction_refused`, `C_74_timer_only_perform` and `C_75_sockaction_timeout_transfer`.
  1. The application sets SOCKETFUNCTION and TIMERFUNCTION and adds 1 or 3 easy handles.
  2. It runs a standard event loop: WSAPoll or poll() on the sockets it was given; `curl_multi_socket_action(fd, ev)` on each event; `curl_multi_socket_action(CURL_SOCKET_TIMEOUT)` when the timer expires.
  3. It checks every socket with `getsockopt(SO_TYPE)`.

  Command: `probe.exe C_20,C_21,C_65,C_74,C_75 2`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
probe.exe C_20,C_21,C_65,C_74,C_75 2
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- Sockets are real and poll() drives the transfer: `real: S1:real`, `pollErrors>0=False socketEvents>0=True`.
- Callback sequence: `add T0 kick S1=2 T-1 S1=1 S1=4`.
- TIMEOUT_MS=600 against a silent server: `T0 S=2 T400+ S=1 S=4 T-1 results=28`.
- Refused connect: `T0 S=2 T-1 S=4 results 7`.
- TIMERFUNCTION only, driven by perform: `T0 T-1`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Sockets are engine numbers from 0x40000000 upward, so poll() fails on them and no socket event ever fires: `real: S1:NOT-A-SOCKET`, `pollErrors>0=True socketEvents>0=False`.
- Callback sequence: `add T0 kick S1=1 T+ S1=4 T-1`. The socket is registered for CURL_POLL_IN at once and never for CURL_POLL_OUT.
- While anything is running, the timer is re-armed every 10 ms (`T+*`, `T0*`) instead of getting -1 or the transfer's real timeout.
- Transfers finish only because the application busy-polls through the timer.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary\ManagedMultiTransfer.cs`:
  - `:71` `FirstTransferSocket`;
  - `:769-786` `TellSocketCallback` always passes `CurlPoll.In`;
  - `:812-822` `TimerMilliseconds` uses `RunningTransferCheckInterval` (10 ms, defined at `:92`).

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

- the DoH sub-transfers use the proxy from the environment. The proxy receives `POST http://127.0.0.1:21800/dns-query HTTP/1.1` twice, or `CONNECT 127.0.0.1:21801` twice for HTTPS DoH. The test proxy answers CONNECT with 403, so REF exits 6 with `Could not resolve host: foo.test`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- the DoH POSTs go straight to the DoH server and the proxy sees nothing. In the HTTPS/CONNECT case PORT exits 0 and fetches the page, while REF exits 6.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary/EngineComposition.Dns.cs:133-155` (CreateDohConnector: "No --resolve, --connect-to, proxy or -4/-6 applies to it", ADR-0152).

Reverse check: `srv doh=21800 web=21802 rr=foo.test:A:127.0.0.1`, then `curl -sS -m 5 --doh-url 127.0.0.1:21800/dns-query http://foo.test:21802/x`. Cases: `cases\v_f2_*.txt`, `linux\cases\vl_f2_noscheme.txt`.

```sh
curl -sS --doh-insecure --doh-url 127.0.0.1:21801/dns-query http://foo.test:21802/x
srv doh=21800 web=21802 rr=foo.test:A:127.0.0.1
curl -sS -m 5 --doh-url 127.0.0.1:21800/dns-query http://foo.test:21802/x
```


- **[proxy-connect PC-17]** exit 2, `curl: option --dns-ipv4-addr: the installed libcurl version does not support this`, then the "try curl --help" line.

  - n4: sends `X-Next:1`.

- **[config-glob-output CGO-06]** `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary/ConfigFileSyntax.cs:33`. Its doc comment says "Not modelled: a NUL byte ending a line early".
- **[environment ENV-13]** not located.

  - `j_high.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Disposition: attachment; filename="caf\xe9.txt"\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello`. Command (in an empty directory): `curl -s -S -OJ http://127.0.0.1:20400/j_high`


**Expected (real curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-08]** 
  - Windows reads the bytes in the ANSI code page: the UTF-8 name gives `cafÃ©.txt`, and 0xE9 gives `café.txt`.
  - Linux writes the raw bytes: `caf\351.txt`.
- **[http-responses HR-8]** creates `café.txt` from byte 0xE9 (CP1252), and `cafÃ©.txt` from the bytes C3 A9.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-08]** 
  - Windows: `café.txt` from the UTF-8 name, and `caf\uFFFD.txt` from 0xE9.
  - Linux: valid UTF-8 matches REF, but 0xE9 becomes `caf\357\277\275.txt` (U+FFFD), so the original byte is lost.
- **[http-responses HR-8]** creates `caf\uFFFD.txt` (replacement character) from 0xE9, and `café.txt` from C3 A9. Both saved names differ from REF's.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-08]** `Curl.Console/ContentDispositionFileName.cs:113` (`Encoding.UTF8.GetString`).
- **[http-responses HR-8]** `Curl.Console\ContentDispositionFileName.cs:113` (`Encoding.UTF8.GetString`)

Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- *Setup (other-protocols):* EV = `SCR\evidence\other-protocols`. Scripted per-protocol loopback servers and runner in `EV\bench\Program.cs`; Windows `pwsh -File EV\run.ps1 <file>.cases [filter]`, Linux `bash EV/run.sh <file>.cases` (set `FILTER=`) or `EV/verify-linux.sh [filter]`. Each `.cases` line is `name | server-mode | server options | curl args`. Default servers: SMTP answers 250 and offers AUTH PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5 XOAUTH2 OAUTHBEARER; POP3 offers SASL PLAIN LOGIN CRAM-MD5; IMAP offers AUTH=PLAIN AUTH=LOGIN AUTH=CRAM-MD5 SASL-IR.
- *Setup (http-stateful):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-stateful`. Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Replay a case: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 <case>`; ad hoc: `EV\vrun.ps1 <routesdir> <curl args>`. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` with `EV\linux\vpat.txt`.
- **[url-parsing UP-05]** Lower-case percent escapes in the URL path are not upper-cased on the wire
  - `curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:20200/a%2fb%7e"` (v05_path_lowerhex)
  - `curl -sS --path-as-is "http://127.0.0.1:20200/a/%2e%2e/b"` (v05b_pai_lower)
- **[config-glob-output CGO-03]** The port keeps percent-encoded hex digits in the URL path as typed; curl 8.22 sends them in upper case
  - `curl -sS "$U/%7euser/%e2%82%ac"`
  - `curl -sS -O "$U/%2e%2e%2fevil"`
  - Script: `E\verify\v2_misc.ps1` p1/p2. The originals are `E\b_out0.ps1` (o09, o10, o42) and `E\b_misc.ps1` (s18, s19).
- **[http-requests HR-5]** Lower-case percent escapes in the URL path are not upper-cased (curl 8.22.0 sends /a%2fb as /a%2Fb)
  - Run `curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:20335/a%2fb`, case v5_pct_lower. The finder's cases are in `E\c10.json`.
- **[other-protocols OP-12]** WebSocket and HTTP request paths keep lower-case percent-escapes where curl 8.22 upper-cases them
  - `EV\pct.cases` pc01/pc02 and `EV\confirm.cases` C18. Commands:
    - `curl -s -S "ws://127.0.0.1:21001/a%2fb%3d"`
    - `curl -s -S "http://127.0.0.1:21001/a%0d%0ab%2fc"`
- **[http-stateful HS-18]** Lower-case percent-escapes in the URL path are sent as given; curl 8.22 upper-cases them, which also changes SigV4 signatures
  - `curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:20500/a%2fb%c3%bc?x=%2f'`, and `curl -sS --aws-sigv4 aws:amz:us-east-1:s3 -u AKID:SECRET -H 'X-Amz-Date: 20250101T000000Z' http://127.0.0.1:20500/a%2fb%c3%bc`. Cases: `EV\cases\pct-lower-plain`, `svx-lower-v`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [url-parsing UP-05]
curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:20200/a%2fb%7e"
curl -sS --path-as-is "http://127.0.0.1:20200/a/%2e%2e/b"
# [config-glob-output CGO-03]
curl -sS "$U/%7euser/%e2%82%ac"
curl -sS -O "$U/%2e%2e%2fevil"
E\verify\v2_misc.ps1
E\b_out0.ps1
E\b_misc.ps1
# [http-requests HR-5]
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:20335/a%2fb
# [other-protocols OP-12]
curl -s -S "ws://127.0.0.1:21001/a%2fb%3d"
curl -s -S "http://127.0.0.1:21001/a%0d%0ab%2fc"
# [http-stateful HS-18]
curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:20500/a%2fb%c3%bc?x=%2f'
curl -sS --aws-sigv4 aws:amz:us-east-1:s3 -u AKID:SECRET -H 'X-Amz-Date: 20250101T000000Z' http://127.0.0.1:20500/a%2fb%c3%bc
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-05]** `GET /a%2Fb%7E` and `GET /a/%2E%2E/b`. `%{url_effective}` keeps the lower case.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-03]** 
  - Sends `GET /%7Euser/%E2%82%AC HTTP/1.1`, and likewise `GET /%2E%2E%2Fevil`.
  - The `-O` file name keeps the typed form `%2e%2e%2fevil`.
- **[http-requests HR-5]** Sends `GET /a%2Fb HTTP/1.1`. Lower-case escapes in the query are left alone, and the port matches that (control case v5_pct_query).
- **[other-protocols OP-12]** `GET /a%2Fb%3D HTTP/1.1` and `GET /a%0D%0Ab%2Fc HTTP/1.1`
- **[http-stateful HS-18]** sends `GET /a%2Fb%C3%BC?x=%2f`. The path is upper-cased and the query is left alone. Signature `de9fa8b6...`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-05]** `GET /a%2fb%7e` and `GET /a/%2e%2e/b`.
- **[config-glob-output CGO-03]** 
  - Sends `GET /%7euser/%e2%82%ac HTTP/1.1` unchanged.
  - The request line therefore differs, and so does any server output that echoes the path.
  - The `-O` file name matches REF.
- **[http-requests HR-5]** Sends `GET /a%2fb HTTP/1.1`.
- **[other-protocols OP-12]** `GET /a%2fb%3d HTTP/1.1` and `GET /a%0d%0ab%2fc HTTP/1.1`. The query string, gopher, RTSP, IMAP, SMTP, DICT and MQTT paths match.
- **[http-stateful HS-18]** sends `GET /a%2fb%c3%bc?x=%2f`. Signature `ec301c3d...`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[url-parsing UP-05]** `Curl.Protocol.Abstractions.UnitLibrary/CurlUrlParser.cs` (Build, around :271).
- **[config-glob-output CGO-03]** the port's URL path normalisation (not located).
- **[http-requests HR-5]** `Curl.Protocol.Abstractions.UnitLibrary/CurlUrlParser.cs:289-293`. The path gets dot-segment removal only, with no escape upper-casing. Compare `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary/UrlPartText.cs`, which does this for redirect URLs.
- **[other-protocols OP-12]** URL path normalisation in the URL parser; not specific to these protocols.
- **[http-stateful HS-18]** the CurlUrl path normalisation in `Curl.Protocol.Abstractions.UnitLibrary`. Overlaps the url-parsing area.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

```sh
# [url-parsing UP-10]

# [proxy-connect PC-08]
srv 20600 log 'H;OK'
curl -s -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 "http://[fe80::1%25eth0]:8080/x"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-10]** `GET http://[::1%25lo]:8080/a HTTP/1.1`
- **[proxy-connect PC-08]** `GET http://[fe80::1%25eth0]:8080/x HTTP/1.1`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-10]** `GET http://[::1]:8080/a HTTP/1.1`
- **[proxy-connect PC-08]** `GET http://[fe80::1]:8080/x HTTP/1.1`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[url-parsing UP-10]** `CurlUrlHost.cs:209-213` (`normalized` is built without the zone id) and the proxy request-target formatter.

- **Source findings:** `url-parsing UP-19`, `http-stateful HS-8`

- *Setup (url-parsing):* E = `SCR\evidence\url-parsing`. Windows server: `E\srvbin\server.exe 20200 E\rec` (or `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20200 E\rec`); it records raw requests and replies `200 ok`, except that a request target containing `__loc=X` gets a 302 with `Location:` = URL-decoded X. Linux: `python3 lharness.py vcases.py` (or `vcases2.py`) from `E\wsl` (server on 20210). Re-run every case: `pwsh -File E\verify.ps1` (outputs `E\cases\v*`).
- *Setup (http-stateful):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-stateful`. Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Replay a case: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 <case>`; ad hoc: `EV\vrun.ps1 <routesdir> <curl args>`. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` with `EV\linux\vpat.txt`.
- **[url-parsing UP-19]** A redirect Location that contains a control character (TAB, 0x01) is rejected
  - PORT reports `Bad hostname` with exit 3, where curl percent-encodes the character and follows the redirect.
  - `curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=/a%09b"` (v19_redir_tab; the server sends `Location: /a<TAB>b`)
  - `curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=/a%01b"` (v19b_redir_ctrl)
  - Linux cases: lv19_*.
- **[http-stateful HS-8]** Control characters in a Location header: a relative Location fails with exit 3 where curl percent-encodes and follows it; DEL in an absolute Location is followed where curl refuses
  - Relative: `/a/b` returns `302` with `Location: /b<TAB>c` (bytes 0x01-0x1F behave the same). Run `curl -sSL -w '%{http_code} %{num_redirects} %{url_effective} %{redirect_url}\n' http://127.0.0.1:20500/a/b`, and the same without -L.
  - Absolute: `/a` returns `Location: http://127.0.0.1:20500/b<0x7F>c`.
  - Cases: `EV\cases\loc-tab`, `loc-tab-noL`, `locc-1..31`, `locc-abs-*`, `locc-abs-127`, `locc-tab-query`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [url-parsing UP-19]
curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=/a%09b"
curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=/a%01b"
# [http-stateful HS-8]
curl -sSL -w '%{http_code} %{num_redirects} %{url_effective} %{redirect_url}\n' http://127.0.0.1:20500/a/b
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-19]** follows with `GET /a%09b` (or `GET /a%01b`) and exits 0.
- **[http-stateful HS-8]** 
  - Relative: follows to `GET /b%09c`. Stdout `final\n200 1 http://127.0.0.1:20500/b%09c`, exit 0. Without -L, redirect_url is `.../b%09c`.
  - Absolute with a C0 byte or DEL: exit 3 `The redirect target URL could not be parsed: Malformed input to a URL function`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[url-parsing UP-19]** `curl: (3) The redirect target URL could not be parsed: Bad hostname`. The second request is not sent.
- **[http-stateful HS-8]** 
  - Relative: exit 3 `curl: (3) The redirect target URL could not be parsed: Bad hostname`, and the redirect is not followed. Without -L, redirect_url contains the raw TAB byte.
  - Absolute with a C0 byte: exit 3 `Bad hostname`.
  - Absolute with DEL: follows to `GET /b%7Fc` and exits 0.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[url-parsing UP-19]** `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary/RedirectFollower.cs:401` (`EncodedForFollow` does not encode bytes below 0x20).
- **[http-stateful HS-8]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpRedirectLocation.cs`: `Resolve` (line 58), `Encode` (line 197), `NormalizeAbsolute` (line 91).

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

  - Linux cases: lv20_*.
- **[http-stateful HS-9]** %{redirect_url} and %{url_effective} differ for unusual absolute Location values
  - `/a/b` returns `302` with `Location: X`. Run `curl -sS[L] -w '%{http_code} %{num_redirects} %{url_effective} %{redirect_url}\n' http://127.0.0.1:20500/a/b`.
  - Try X = `http:/b`, `file:///c:/windows/win.ini`, `http://\xE9.invalid/b` (a raw E9 byte) and `http:`.

```sh
curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:20200/__loc=/a/%252e%252e/b" -w "%{url_effective}"
# [http-stateful HS-9]
```

- **[http-stateful HS-9]**

  - The file Location becomes `file://c:/windows/win.ini`.
  - The host byte E9 is written back as the single byte E9. Linux 8.18 fails with exit 3 instead.
  - `http:` fails with `Unsupported number of slashes following scheme`.

**Actual (Curl)**

  - `http:/b` is reported unchanged as `http:/b` (both exit 6 with -L).
  - The file Location stays `file:///c:/windows/win.ini`. On Linux this case matches REF.
  - The host byte E9 is reported as UTF-8 `C3 A9`.
  - `http:` fails with `Port number was not a decimal number between 0 and 65535`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[url-parsing UP-20]** `Curl.Core.UnitLibrary/RedirectFollower.cs` (url_effective comes from the target string, not from the parsed CurlUrl).

### CGR-067: While waiting for 100 Continue, an early final 2xx response makes Curl drop the request body. curl sends the body anyway.

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** http-requests
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed: reproduced 2/2 on Windows and 2/2 on Linux.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0025
- **Source findings:** `http-requests HR-7`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- Use a server that sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\n\r\nok\n` as soon as the request head arrives and keeps reading (harness `"early":true`). Run:
  - `printf abcde | curl -sS -T - http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`
  - `curl -sS -H "Expect: 100-continue" -d abcde http://127.0.0.1:20335/a`

  These are cases v7_*. The finder's cases are in `E\c18.json`, which includes a 1 MiB+1 `--data-binary` and `-T` where REF sends 1048770 bytes and PORT sends 193.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh

```

**Expected (real curl)**

- After the 200 it still sends the body: `5\r\nabcde\r\n0\r\n\r\n` for `-T -`, and `abcde` for the `-d` case. Exits 0 with stdout `ok`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Sends only the request head and no body bytes, even though it declared `Content-Length: 5` or chunked. Exits 0 with stdout `ok`.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpContinueWaitConnection.cs:64-74`. `WaitForContinueAsync` returns false when a final status arrives first, so the body is skipped. The same class's `StopsSending` (line 90) says that a 2xx should let the body go on.

- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- WSL: run `mkdir sub`, then:
  - `curl -sS -T sub http://127.0.0.1:20355/a`
  - `curl -sS -F f=@sub http://127.0.0.1:20355/a`
  - `curl -sS -d @sub http://127.0.0.1:20355/a`


  - `-T sub` sends `PUT /a` chunked with only `0\r\n\r\n` and exits 0.

<a id="cgr-070"></a>
### CGR-070: An unsolicited `101 Switching Protocols` is treated as an interim 1xx response, so the body is not written and the transfer fails with exit 8

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** http-responses, network-robustness
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0083
- **Source findings:** `http-responses HR-3`, `network-robustness NR-4`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-responses):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-responses`. Canned-response server: `dotnet run EV\server\server.cs -- 20400 EV\resp EV\logs`; `GET /NAME` returns the bytes of `EV\resp\NAME.bin` (if `EV\resp\NAME.opts` contains `keep`, the connection stays open). Differential: `EV\diff.ps1 -Name NAME -CArgs ... [-Opts keep]`; verifier `EV\verify\vdiff.ps1` (port 20420) driven by `EV\verify\vcases.ps1`. Linux: `EV\linux\server.py` serves the same fixtures (verifier: port 20460 via `EV\verify\linux\vrun.sh`; port 20450 in the original runs).
- *Setup (network-robustness):* EV = `SCR\evidence\network-robustness`. Windows server: `EV\srvbin\server.exe 21100 21101` (source `EV\srv\server.cs`); repro script `EV\repro_findings.sh` (uses the `d.sh` diff harness). Linux: `python3 EV/linux/srv.py 21150 21151`; repro `EV/linux/verify_lin.sh`. `H=http://127.0.0.1:21100` (21150 on Linux); `b64() { printf "$1" | base64 -w0 | sed 's/+/%2B/g; s/\//%2F/g; s/=/%3D/g'; }`; `$H/raw?b=<b64>` replies with exactly those bytes (`&keep=1` keeps the connection).
- **[http-responses HR-3]** Unsolicited 101 Switching Protocols is treated as an interim 1xx, so the body fails with exit 8
  - `x101b.bin` = `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching\r\n\r\nhello`, then the server closes. Command: `curl -s -S http://127.0.0.1:20400/x101b`
  - Variants: `x101` (`Upgrade: foo`, run with `-i`), `x101c` (`Content-Length: 2`), `x101_10` (`HTTP/1.0 101`).
- **[network-robustness NR-4]** Unsolicited `101 Switching Protocols` fails with exit 8 `Invalid status line`
  - `curl -sSi "$H/raw?b=$(b64 'HTTP/1.1 101 Switching\r\n\r\nabc')"`; add `-w '%{http_code} %{exitcode}'`. Also with `Upgrade: h2c`/`Connection: Upgrade` headers (Linux l_101b).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-responses HR-3]
curl -s -S http://127.0.0.1:20400/x101b
# [network-robustness NR-4]
curl -sSi "$H/raw?b=$(b64 'HTTP/1.1 101 Switching\r\n\r\nabc')"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-3]** exit 0. stdout is `hello`. With `-i`, the 101 head is followed by `hello`.
- **[network-robustness NR-4]** exit 0, stdout `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching\r\n\r\nabc`; -w `101 0`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-3]** exit 8 `curl: (8) Invalid status line`, and no body is written. With `-i` only the 101 head is written. Same on Linux.
- **[network-robustness NR-4]** exit 8 `curl: (8) Invalid status line`; the body is not written; -w `101 8`.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-responses HR-3]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary\HttpResponseHeadReader.cs` around line 470-517: 101 is treated as an interim response (`SwitchedProtocols |= StatusCode == 101` at line 517).
- **[network-robustness NR-4]** `HttpResponseHeadReader.cs` treats 101 as informational and expects another status line

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-077: Windows Digest (server and proxy) does not match the SSPI reference: challenges REF refuses with exit 94 are answered, and answer bytes differ for userhash, escaping, case, charset, white space, long nonces, `DOMAIN\user`, empty and non-ASCII user names

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** http-stateful, upstream-cases, proxy-connect
- **Platform(s):** Windows. Detail: [http-stateful HS-14] Windows (the Linux part depends on the curl version); [proxy-connect PC-10] Windows. On Linux the port matches 8.18 for userhash (VL20).
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0003, GF-0034, GF-0006
- **Source findings:** `http-stateful HS-12`, `http-stateful HS-13`, `http-stateful HS-14`, `upstream-cases UC-6`, `proxy-connect PC-10`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (http-stateful):* EV = `SCR\evidence\http-stateful`. Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Replay a case: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 <case>`; ad hoc: `EV\vrun.ps1 <routesdir> <curl args>`. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` with `EV\linux\vpat.txt`.
- *Setup (upstream-cases):* EV = `SCR\evidence\upstream-cases`. Cross-platform runs: `EV\verify\diff.sh`, driven in WSL by `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "/mnt/c/Users/Stewart Rogers/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/Z--repos-Curl-ThirdPartyReview/3796612b-55d9-44ec-9722-80e35c3282a1/scratchpad/evidence/upstream-cases/verify/sync.sh" vN.sh` (N = 1..4), against the canned recording server `EV\verify\srv.py` (configs in `EV\verify\conf\`). Windows-native runs: `EV\verify\vwin.ps1` (wraps `harness\Diff-Curl.ps1` and `Record-CurlExchange.ps1`).
- *Setup (proxy-connect):* EV = `SCR\evidence\proxy-connect`. Scripted recording server: `EV\srv\out\srv.exe <port> <log> '<script for conn 1>' ['<script for conn 2>' ...]` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`); steps are `;`-separated: `H` read a request head, `HN` read a head and answer nothing yet, `OK`/`CE`/`403`/`403B`/`407B` canned replies, `W:<bytes>` write literal bytes, `S4`/`S5G`/`S5U`/`S5R` read SOCKS messages, `E` record raw bytes until EOF. In repros `srv` means this binary. Harnesses `EV\harness.ps1` and `EV\lharness.sh`; verifier `EV\v_win*.ps1`, `EV\v_linux.sh`, `EV\v_l3.sh`.
- **[http-stateful HS-12]** Windows Digest: the SSPI build's refusals (exit 94) are missing, and PORT answers unusual challenges
  - `/p` returns 401 with the challenge below, then 200 `authed`.
  - Commands: `curl -sS --digest -u user:pass 'http://127.0.0.1:20500/p?x=1'`, and the same with `-X PATCH -d zz`.
  - Challenges: `algorithm=FOO`; `qop="auth-int"`; `qop="foo"`; no nonce; a trailing comma.
  - Cases: `EV\cases\dg-unknown-alg`, `dg-auth-int`, `dg-qop-unknown`, `dg-nononce`, `dg-trailing-comma`, `dg-X`. Script: `EV\c08_digest.ps1`.
- **[http-stateful HS-13]** Windows Digest answer bytes differ from the SSPI build for several challenge forms
  - the same setup as HS-12. Challenges:
    - (a) `userhash=true` (MD5)
    - (b) `realm="te\"st", nonce="a\\bc"`
    - (c) `DIGEST REALM=... ALGORITHM=md5`
    - (d) `charset=UTF-8`
    - (e) `Digest    realm = "testrealm" ,  nonce = "abc123" ,qop="auth"`
    - (f) a 3000-character nonce
    - Cases: `EV\cases\dg-userhash-md5`, `dg-escaped`, `dg-case`, `dg-charset`, `dg-extra-ws`, `dg-long-nonce`.
- **[http-stateful HS-14]** Windows Digest with a "DOMAIN\user", empty or non-ASCII user name does not match SSPI
  - `/p` returns 401 `Digest realm="testrealm", nonce="abc123", qop="auth"`, then 200.
  - Commands: `curl -sS --digest -u 'dom\user:pass' http://127.0.0.1:20500/p`, then the same with `-u ':pass'` and with `-u 'usér:pass'`.
  - Cases: `EV\cases\dgu-dom_user_pass`, `dgu-us_er_pass`, `dgu-_pass`, `dgu-us_r_pass`.
- **[upstream-cases UC-6]** Windows Digest auth does not match REF-WIN's SSPI digest (URI quoting, backslash in user name, duplicated challenge parameters, CR/LF in the user name)
  - `verify\vwin.ps1` (cases `v_dg*`, port 21371). The server answers with two connections: first `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Digest realm="testrealm", nonce="1053604145"`, then `200`.
    - (a) `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:21371/64\"" -u testuser:testpass --digest`
    - (b) `curl -s "http://%5cuser%22:password@127.0.0.1:21371/1229" --digest`
    - (c) Challenge `Digest realm="testrealm", algorithm=MD5, algorithm=MD5, nonce="1", nonce="2"`, then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21371/1437 -u testuser:testpass --digest`
    - (d) `curl -s -S http://127.0.0.1:21371/3221 -u "hello<LF><CR>:pass" --digest`
- **[proxy-connect PC-10]** Windows: Digest challenges with userhash=true or qop="auth-int" are answered differently from the Schannel/SSPI reference
  - run `srv 20600 log 'H;W:HTTP/1.1 407 X\r\nProxy-Authenticate: Digest realm="p", nonce="n1", userhash=true\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n;H;OK'`, then `curl -s -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 --proxy-digest -U us:pw http://example.test/x`. For the second case use `qop="auth-int"` instead of `userhash=true`. Verifier cases: v16 and v17.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-stateful HS-12]
curl -sS --digest -u user:pass 'http://127.0.0.1:20500/p?x=1'
EV\c08_digest.ps1
# [http-stateful HS-14]
curl -sS --digest -u 'dom\user:pass' http://127.0.0.1:20500/p
# [upstream-cases UC-6]
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:21371/64\"" -u testuser:testpass --digest
curl -s "http://%5cuser%22:password@127.0.0.1:21371/1229" --digest
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:21371/1437 -u testuser:testpass --digest
curl -s -S http://127.0.0.1:21371/3221 -u "hello<LF><CR>:pass" --digest
# [proxy-connect PC-10]
srv 20600 log 'H;W:HTTP/1.1 407 X\r\nProxy-Authenticate: Digest realm="p", nonce="n1", userhash=true\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n;H;OK'
curl -s -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 --proxy-digest -U us:pw http://example.test/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-stateful HS-12]** prints `curl: (94) An authentication function returned an error` and exits 94.
- **[http-stateful HS-13]** 
  - (a) `username="user"` with no userhash; the server check passes.
  - (b) `nonce="a\bc"`.
  - (c) `algorithm=MD5`.
  - (d) appends `,charset=utf-8`.
  - (e) answers with `realm=""` and gets the 200.
  - (f) keeps cnonce, nc and `qop="auth"`.
- **[http-stateful HS-14]** 
  - `dom\user` gives `username="user",realm="dom"`.
  - `:pass` gives `curl: (67) Login denied` and exit 67.
  - `usér` sends the raw byte E9.
- **[upstream-cases UC-6]** 
  - (a) `uri="/64""` (the quote is sent raw).
  - (b) `username="user\""` (SSPI drops the leading `\`), response=ed551b...
  - (c) Exit 94 and no second request.
  - (d) Exit 94, `curl: (94) An authentication function returned an error`.
- **[proxy-connect PC-10]** for userhash it sends `username="us"` with no userhash parameter. For an auth-int-only challenge it exits 94 and sends no second request.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-stateful HS-12]** exits 0.
  - For auth-int, an unknown qop, a trailing comma and PATCH, it answers with Digest and prints `authed`.
  - For an unknown algorithm or a missing nonce, it prints the 401 body `denied`.
- **[http-stateful HS-13]** 
  - (a) `username="f7b4a687..."` with `userhash=true`; the server check fails.
  - (b) `nonce="a\\bc"`.
  - (c) `algorithm=md5`.
  - (d) no charset.
  - (e) sends no Authorization header and prints `denied`.
  - (f) drops qop, cnonce and nc, which makes it an RFC 2069 answer.
- **[http-stateful HS-14]** 
  - `dom\user` gives `username="dom\\user",realm="testrealm"`.
  - `:pass` sends `username=""` and exits 0 (`authed`).
  - `usér` sends `username="us%E9r"`.
- **[upstream-cases UC-6]** 
  - (a) `uri="/64\""` (escaped).
  - (b) `username="\\user\""`, response=f2694d...
  - (c) Sends the retry with nonce="2" and exits 0, printing the body.
  - (d) Sends `username="hello%0A%0D"` and exits 0.
- **[proxy-connect PC-10]** for userhash it sends `username="e6585ea998f7e371f4493fd74d84b791",...,userhash=true`. For auth-int it sends `qop="auth-int"` and exits 0 with `hello`.

**Notes**

- **[http-stateful HS-14]** *Linux:* PORT sends `us%C3%A9r` where REF 8.18 sends raw UTF-8. The port says it copies 8.21's quoting, so this part depends on the curl version and is not claimed.
- **[upstream-cases UC-6]** *Verifier note:* PORT's values in (b), (c) and (d) match upstream's non-SSPI expectations, but its header layout (no space after commas) copies SSPI. The result is a hybrid that no real curl build produces, and it differs from REF-WIN.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-stateful HS-12]** `Curl.Authentication.UnitLibrary/DigestAuthenticator.cs:70` refuses only the algorithms that SSPI does not answer. See also `DigestChallengeParameters.cs`.
- **[http-stateful HS-13]** `Curl.Authentication.UnitLibrary/DigestAuthenticator.cs:146` (`FormatSspiValue`); `DigestChallengeParameters.cs`.
- **[http-stateful HS-14]** `Curl.Authentication.UnitLibrary/DigestQuoting.cs:22-31`; `DigestAuthenticator.cs:120`.
- **[upstream-cases UC-6]** `Curl.Authentication.UnitLibrary` (Digest on Windows).
- **[proxy-connect PC-10]** `Curl.Authentication.UnitLibrary\DigestAuthenticator.cs`

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Replay a case: `pwsh EV\verify.ps1 <case>`; ad hoc: `EV\vrun.ps1 <routesdir> <curl args>`. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` with `EV\linux\vpat.txt`.
- `curl -sS -g --aws-sigv4 aws:amz:us-east-1:s3 -u AKID:SECRET -H 'X-Amz-Date: 20250101T000000Z' 'http://127.0.0.1:20500/p?k=ä'`, and the same with the path `/ü`. Cases: `EV\cases\svq-k__-396`, `svp-__-299`.


- the request line is `GET /p?k=\xE4` (an ANSI byte) with `Signature=251a1c08...`. Path case: `GET /%FC` with `Signature=3ff4f5d1...`.

- *Note:* the argv code-page part overlaps the url-parsing area.

<a id="cgr-079"></a>
### CGR-079: Proxy credentials in the proxy URL lose to -U/--proxy-user; curl lets the URL's user info win

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** proxy-connect
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed. Reproduced by the tester and again by the verifier, on both platforms.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `proxy-connect PC-01`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (proxy-connect):* EV = `SCR\evidence\proxy-connect`. Scripted recording server: `EV\srv\out\srv.exe <port> <log> '<script for conn 1>' ['<script for conn 2>' ...]` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`); steps are `;`-separated: `H` read a request head, `HN` read a head and answer nothing yet, `OK`/`CE`/`403`/`403B`/`407B` canned replies, `W:<bytes>` write literal bytes, `S4`/`S5G`/`S5U`/`S5R` read SOCKS messages, `E` record raw bytes until EOF. In repros `srv` means this binary. Harnesses `EV\harness.ps1` and `EV\lharness.sh`; verifier `EV\v_win*.ps1`, `EV\v_linux.sh`, `EV\v_l3.sh`.
- run `srv 20600 log 'H;OK'`, then `curl -s -x http://a:b@127.0.0.1:20600 -U c:d http://example.test/`.
  - Variants: `http_proxy=http://a:b@127.0.0.1:20600 curl -s -U c:d http://example.test/`, and `-x http://a@127.0.0.1:20600 -U c:d`.
  - SOCKS5 variant: `-x socks5://a:b@127.0.0.1:20600 -U c:d http://127.0.0.1:8080/x` with server script `S5G;S5UP;S5U;S5AOK;S5R;S5ROK;H;OK`.
  - SOCKS4 variant: `-x socks4://a@127.0.0.1:20600 -U c:d http://127.0.0.1:8080/x` with script `S4;S4OK;H;OK`.
  - Verifier cases: v01-v05 and VL01-VL04.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
srv 20600 log 'H;OK'
curl -s -x http://a:b@127.0.0.1:20600 -U c:d http://example.test/
http_proxy=http://a:b@127.0.0.1:20600 curl -s -U c:d http://example.test/
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- *REF (Windows 8.22.0 and Linux 8.18.0):* sends `Proxy-Authorization: Basic YTpi` (a:b). With a user-only URL it sends `YTo=` (a:). SOCKS5 sends `\x01\x01a\x01b` and the SOCKS4 USERID is `a`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- sends `Proxy-Authorization: Basic Yzpk` (c:d) in every variant. SOCKS5 sends `\x01\x01c\x01d` and the SOCKS4 USERID is `c`.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary\ManagedEasyTransfer.Context.cs:222-237` (`ProxyCredentialsOf`). Its doc comment says -U and --proxy-user "replace the proxy URL's own user information" (BL-2660, ADR-0677), which does not match curl 8.22.0 CLI behaviour.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-088"></a>
### CGR-088: `-v`/`--trace` do not echo error messages as `* <message>` info lines (curl's failf echo) for HTTP, FTP, CONNECT and SOCKS failures

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** writeout-verbose, ftp-file-tftp, proxy-connect
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [writeout-verbose WV-06] Confirmed (Windows and Linux).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** AF-0085
- **Source findings:** `writeout-verbose WV-06`, `ftp-file-tftp FTP-12`, `proxy-connect PC-11`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (writeout-verbose):* EV = `SCR\evidence\writeout-verbose`. Windows server: `cd EV\srv && dotnet run wvsrv.cs -- 20700 EV\resp EV\req.log` (HTTP on 127.0.0.1/::1:20700, a mini FTP server on 20701, TLS on 20702; `/raw/<name>` serves `EV\resp\<name>.txt`; other routes `/code/N`, `/redir/N`, `/hang/ms`, `/close` (empty reply), `/ka`, `/echo`, `/p`). Linux: `EV\linux\srv.py` on 20710. One-line repros for every finding: `EV\repro_findings.sh` (Windows) and `EV\linux\verify_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (ftp-file-tftp):* EV = `SCR\evidence\ftp-file-tftp`. Scripted FTP/TFTP stub: `EV\stub\win3\stub.exe` (Linux `EV/stub/linux/stub`, source `EV\stub\Program.cs`) with fixture root `EV\fixture\root` (file.txt is 18 bytes). Differential harness `EV\dt.sh NAME 'script' curl-args`, where `@U@` = `ftp://127.0.0.1:$CPORT`, script lines are `CMD=reply` or `OPT key=value` separated by `;;`, and `STUBEXTRA=EV\tls.pfx` enables FTPS. Verifier: `EV\v1.sh`, `EV\v2.sh` (Windows), `EV\vl.sh` (Linux).
- *Setup (proxy-connect):* EV = `SCR\evidence\proxy-connect`. Scripted recording server: `EV\srv\out\srv.exe <port> <log> '<script for conn 1>' ['<script for conn 2>' ...]` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`); steps are `;`-separated: `H` read a request head, `HN` read a head and answer nothing yet, `OK`/`CE`/`403`/`403B`/`407B` canned replies, `W:<bytes>` write literal bytes, `S4`/`S5G`/`S5U`/`S5R` read SOCKS messages, `E` record raw bytes until EOF. In repros `srv` means this binary. Harnesses `EV\harness.ps1` and `EV\lharness.sh`; verifier `EV\v_win*.ps1`, `EV\v_linux.sh`, `EV\v_l3.sh`.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-06]** -v does not echo error messages as "* <message>" info lines (curl's failf echo)
  - `curl -s -v -f http://127.0.0.1:20700/code/404`
  - `curl -s -v http://127.0.0.1:20700/close` (empty reply)
  - `curl -s -v -u bad:x ftp://127.0.0.1:20701/file.txt` (the server answers 530)
  - The same gap applies to `--trace` and to every failure path the original tester listed: `--max-redirs`, `--max-filesize`, bad gzip, bad chunk, `-m`, a bad `-o` path, a short body, FTP CWD/STOR/RETR/REST errors, and a bad SOCKS5 reply.
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-12]** `-v` FTP failures are not echoed as `* <message>` info lines, and `* shutting down / closing connection #0` is missing
  - `curl -sSv ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/nope.txt`
  - `curl -sSv -Q BOGUS ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt`
  - Other cases: `EV\cases\vf_*` (PASS 530, EPSV+PASV 500, --max-filesize, greeting 500, 226 replaced by 451).

  Verification cases: `v_vf_missing`, `v_vf_q` (Windows); `v_vf_missing` (Linux).
- **[proxy-connect PC-11]** -v does not print the failure as a "* " trace line for CONNECT and SOCKS failures
  - *(CONNECT):* run `srv 20600 log 'HN;403B'`, then `curl -sv -p -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 http://example.test/`.
  - *(SOCKS4):* run with script `S4;S4REJ`, then `curl -sv -x socks4://127.0.0.1:20600 http://127.0.0.1:8080/x`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [writeout-verbose WV-06]
curl -s -v -f http://127.0.0.1:20700/code/404
curl -s -v http://127.0.0.1:20700/close
curl -s -v -u bad:x ftp://127.0.0.1:20701/file.txt
# [ftp-file-tftp FTP-12]
curl -sSv ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/nope.txt
curl -sSv -Q BOGUS ftp://127.0.0.1:20960/file.txt
# [proxy-connect PC-11]
srv 20600 log 'HN;403B'
curl -sv -p -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 http://example.test/
curl -sv -x socks4://127.0.0.1:20600 http://127.0.0.1:8080/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-06]** Prints the error as an info line before ending, for example `* The requested URL returned error: 404`, `* Empty reply from server` followed by `* shutting down connection #0`, and `* Access denied: 530`. These come from libcurl `failf()`, which echoes to the verbose stream in release builds too. REF-LINUX 8.18 (a release build) prints them.
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-12]** `* The file does not exist`; `* QUOT command failed with 500` followed by `* shutting down connection #0`, and similar lines for the other failures.
- **[proxy-connect PC-11]** `* CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` or `* [SOCKS] cannot complete SOCKS4 connection to 0.0.0.0:0. (91), request rejected or failed.` before `* closing connection #0`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-06]** None of these lines appear; only the final `curl: (N)` line is printed. For an empty reply it prints `* closing connection #0` where REF prints `* shutting down connection #0`.
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-12]** These lines are missing. The final `curl: (N) ...` line matches. file:// and TFTP verbose failures match.
- **[proxy-connect PC-11]** that line is missing.

**Notes**

- **[proxy-connect PC-11]** *Verifier cases:* v18, v18b and VL14.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-06]** There is no general failf-style verbose echo. `Curl.Console/CurlCommandRunner.cs` writes only the final line; only `SchannelFailureEcho.cs` exists, for TLS.
- **[ftp-file-tftp FTP-12]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary/FtpSession.cs` `QuitAndFailAsync` / `EndAndFailAsync` do not report the failure message as an info event.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (writeout-verbose):* EV = `SCR\evidence\writeout-verbose`. Linux: `EV\linux\srv.py` on 20710. One-line repros for every finding: `EV\repro_findings.sh` (Windows) and `EV\linux\verify_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (url-parsing):* E = `SCR\evidence\url-parsing`. Windows server: `E\srvbin\server.exe 20200 E\rec` (or `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20200 E\rec`); it records raw requests and replies `200 ok`, except that a request target containing `__loc=X` gets a 302 with `Location:` = URL-decoded X. Linux: `python3 lharness.py vcases.py` (or `vcases2.py`) from `E\wsl` (server on 20210). Re-run every case: `pwsh -File E\verify.ps1` (outputs `E\cases\v*`).
- **[writeout-verbose WV-08]** %{url} / %{url.query} ignore the query that -G -d or --url-query add
  - `curl -s -o NUL -w '%{url}|%{url.query}\n' -G -d a=b http://127.0.0.1:20700/p`
  - `curl -s -o NUL -w '%{url}|%{url.query}\n' --url-query x=1 'http://127.0.0.1:20700/p?y=2'`

  - `curl -sS -G -d a=b "http://127.0.0.1:20200/x" -w "%{url}"` (v07_G_url)
  - `curl -sS --url-query a=b "http://127.0.0.1:20200/x" -w "%{url}"` (v07b_uq_url)
  - Linux cases: lv07_*.

