**Reproduction**

- *Setup (parallel-multi-transfer):* EV = `SCR\evidence\parallel-multi-transfer`. Server: `dotnet run EV\srv\server.cs -- 22000,22001 EV\srv\log` (listens on 127.0.0.1:22000 and :22001; query `d=` delay in ms, `s=` status, `n=` body size, `p=`/`pd=` send the body in parts with a delay, `close=1` adds Connection: close; other paths return `body /<path>`); port 22099 is closed. Linux: `EV/linux/srv.py 22000,22001 /tmp/pmt_srv` (started by `EV/linux/lt.sh`). Harness `EV\dt.ps1`; verifier `EV\v1.ps1` and `EV/linux/vl.sh`.
- `curl -Z --parallel-immediate -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{url}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok1?d=200" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok2?d=100" "http://[::1"`
- `curl -Z --parallel-immediate -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -T u1.txt "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=200" -T nope.txt http://127.0.0.1:22000/b`. Here u1.txt exists and nope.txt does not.
- `curl -Z --parallel-max 1 -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{url}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok1?d=200" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok2?d=100" "http://[::1"`

Scripts: `v1.ps1` (v_badglob, v_badglob_r, v_upmiss, v_badglob_pmax1, v_badglob_ser), `linux/vl.sh` (vl_badglob, vl_upmiss).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -Z --parallel-immediate -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{url}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok1?d=200" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok2?d=100" "http://[::1"
curl -Z --parallel-immediate -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -T u1.txt "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=200" -T nope.txt http://127.0.0.1:22000/b
curl -Z --parallel-max 1 -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{url}\n" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok1?d=200" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/ok2?d=100" "http://[::1"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- no request goes out for ok1, ok2 or a. Each transfer already queued is reported with the setup error. stdout is `0 3 …ok1?d=200\n1 3 …ok2?d=100\n`. stderr has the glob error and then two `curl: (3) URL using bad/illegal format or missing URL` lines. In the -T case, stdout is `0 26 000\n1 26 000\n` and `curl: (26) Failed to open/read local data from file/application` appears twice. Exit is 3 or 26. With `--parallel-max 1`, ok1 and ok2 run, and then REF prints `2 3 http://[::1` and `curl: (3) URL rejected: Bad IPv6 address`. Serial mode is the same in REF and PORT.

**Actual (Curl)**

- prints the glob or cannot-open error once, then performs the other transfers and reports them. stdout is `body /ok2\n1 0 …\nbody /ok1\n0 0 …\n`, and in the -T case u1.txt is uploaded (`1 26 000\nbody /a\n0 0 200\n`). The exit code is the same as REF's. With `--parallel-max 1`, PORT prints no -w line and no `URL rejected` line for the bad URL.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Console/CurlCommandRunner.cs` ~1993-2002, the -Z path that records "a failure that ends the run before its transfer starts", and `WriteGlobFailureLinesAsync` at :1713. Neither aborts nor re-reports transfers that are already queued.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-171"></a>
### CGR-171: Under -Z, when a host's first transfer closes its connection (Connection: close or a -f error), PORT runs the waiting transfers one at a time, starting with the last; REF starts them all at once

- **Severity:** Medium (the order of -w lines, bodies and error lines differs, and the transfers no longer run concurrently)
- **Area:** parallel-multi-transfer
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (Windows x3, Linux)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `parallel-multi-transfer PMT-3`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (parallel-multi-transfer):* EV = `SCR\evidence\parallel-multi-transfer`. Server: `dotnet run EV\srv\server.cs -- 22000,22001 EV\srv\log` (listens on 127.0.0.1:22000 and :22001; query `d=` delay in ms, `s=` status, `n=` body size, `p=`/`pd=` send the body in parts with a delay, `close=1` adds Connection: close; other paths return `body /<path>`); port 22099 is closed. Linux: `EV/linux/srv.py 22000,22001 /tmp/pmt_srv` (started by `EV/linux/lt.sh`). Harness `EV\dt.ps1`; verifier `EV\v1.ps1` and `EV/linux/vl.sh`.
- `curl -Z -s -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -o NUL -o NUL -o NUL "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=600&close=1" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/b?d=100" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/c?d=300"`
- The same command with `-f` and the first URL `a?d=600&s=500`.

Scripts: `v1.ps1` (v_p2_close, v_p2_close_r, v_p1_f500), `linux/vl.sh` (vl_p2_close). The server's per-connection timeline is in `runs\v_p2_close\{ref,port}\meta`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
curl -Z -s -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -o NUL -o NUL -o NUL "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=600&close=1" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/b?d=100" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/c?d=300"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- at t=606 ms, REF opens two new connections in the same millisecond and runs b and c concurrently. stdout is `0 0 200\n1 0 200\n2 0 200\n` (`0 22 500\n1 0 200\n2 0 200\n` with -f), and the run ends at about 920 ms.

**Actual (Curl)**

- at t=617 ms PORT opens one connection for c only. b starts on a new connection at t=930, after c has finished. stdout is `0 0 200\n2 0 200\n1 0 200\n` (`0 22 500\n2 0 200\n1 0 200\n` with -f). The run ends at about 1040 ms.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Console/ParallelHostQueue.cs` ~84-160. `Leave` passes the first waiter as `pending`, `FreeWaiting` moves it behind the others, and `StartReleased` starts the released transfers one after another. ADR-0768 is cited in the source.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Server: `dotnet run EV\srv\server.cs -- 22000,22001 EV\srv\log` (listens on 127.0.0.1:22000 and :22001; query `d=` delay in ms, `s=` status, `n=` body size, `p=`/`pd=` send the body in parts with a delay, `close=1` adds Connection: close; other paths return `body /<path>`); port 22099 is closed. Linux: `EV/linux/srv.py 22000,22001 /tmp/pmt_srv` (started by `EV/linux/lt.sh`). Harness `EV\dt.ps1`; verifier `EV\v1.ps1` and `EV/linux/vl.sh`.
- `curl -Z -s -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -o NUL -o NUL -o NUL "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=600" "http://127.0.0.1:22001/q?d=100" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/c?d=300"`
- `curl -Z -s -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -o NUL -o NUL -o NUL "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=600" http://127.0.0.1:22099/x "http://127.0.0.1:22000/c?d=200"`. Port 22099 refuses the connection.

```sh
curl -Z -s -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code}\n" -o NUL -o NUL -o NUL "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=600" http://127.0.0.1:22099/x "http://127.0.0.1:22000/c?d=200"
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- c starts on a second connection as soon as q ends (t=116 ms), or right after the refused connect, and finishes before a. stdout is `1 0 200\n2 0 200\n0 0 200\n`; in the refused case it is `1 7 000\n2 0 200\n0 0 200\n`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- c waits until a ends at about 605 ms and then reuses a's connection. stdout is `1 0 200\n0 0 200\n2 0 200\n`; in the refused case it is `1 7 000\n0 0 200\n2 0 200\n`.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Console/ParallelHostQueue.cs` ~80-95. `Leave` frees only the waiters of the same host:port, so a transfer that ends at another host, or that fails to connect, frees none of them.

  - Serial: `curl -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code} %{size_upload}\n" -F "f=@-" http://127.0.0.1:22000/a http://127.0.0.1:22000/b`

  Scripts: `v1.ps1` (v_F_ser, v_F_par), `linux/vl.sh` (vl_F_ser, vl_F_par).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh

curl -Z --parallel-immediate -sS -w "%{urlnum} %{exitcode} %{http_code} %{size_upload}\n" -F "f=@-" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/a?d=200" "http://127.0.0.1:22000/b?d=100"
```

- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [http-requests HR-11] Confirmed: reproduced 2/2 on Windows and 2/2 on Linux.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** GF-0078
- **Source findings:** `cli-options CLIO-13`, `http-requests HR-11`, `environment ENV-11`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (cli-options):* Evidence `SCR\evidence\cli-options`. Windows: start the echo server `pwsh -NoProfile -File SCR\evidence\cli-options\echoserver.ps1 -Port 20000` (replies 200 with the raw request bytes as the body); `@U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20000/`; port 20002 is left closed. Harness: `SCR\evidence\cli-options\h.sh <name> <args>` runs REF and PORT and stores exit code, stdout, stderr and files. Linux: `python3 linux/echo.py 20001` (in the evidence folder); `URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:20001/`. Verifier scripts: `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v4_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (http-requests):* E = `SCR\evidence\http-requests`. Recording loopback server + differential runner: `dotnet run E\diff.cs -- E\verify.json E\vout1 20335` (Windows, port 20335) and `E/vlinux.sh` (WSL, port 20355; runs `python3 -I E/diff.py E/verify.json ~/hr_verify/v1 20355`). The server answers `200 OK` with body `ok\n` after reading the whole request; in `early` mode it answers right after the request head and keeps reading.
- *Setup (environment):* EV = `SCR\evidence\environment`. Windows: `dotnet run EV\server.cs 21200` (echo server: returns the raw request as the body; `/bin` returns bytes 0..255) and `dotnet run EV\s2\server2.cs 21201` (same, used as a proxy). `EV\verify_windows.ps1` runs each case in isolated `aref`/`port` directories with HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA at an empty directory. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` and `EV\linux\vtls.sh` (echo on 21210, proxy on 21211, `openssl s_server` on 21213).
- **[cli-options CLIO-13]** -s -T . : REF still draws the progress meter; PORT prints nothing
  - `curl -s -T . -o NUL @U < linux/stdin1.bin` (and on Linux with `-o /dev/null`, with or without stdin). Scripts: `repro/r12_Tdot_win.sh`, `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`.
- **[http-requests HR-11]** -T . with -s (or -sS) still writes the progress meter in curl, but Curl stays silent
  - Run `printf 'hello dot\n' | curl -s -T . http://127.0.0.1:20335/a` (case v11_Tdot_s). The control case `-s -T -` matches.
- **[environment ENV-11]** `-s -T .` (upload from stdin, non-blocking) prints no progress meter; REF prints it even with `-s`
  - Windows: `echo a | curl -s -T . http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo` (v-Tdot)
  - Linux: the same command with port 21210 (v-Tdot)

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [cli-options CLIO-13]
curl -s -T . -o NUL @U < linux/stdin1.bin
# [http-requests HR-11]
printf 'hello dot\n' | curl -s -T . http://127.0.0.1:20335/a
# [environment ENV-11]
echo a | curl -s -T . http://127.0.0.1:21200/echo
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[cli-options CLIO-13]** stderr contains progress-meter rows despite `-s`.
- **[http-requests HR-11]** Even with `-s`, stderr gets the meter header lines (`  % Total    % Received % Xferd ...`) and CR-separated progress rows. This happens on both 8.22.0 (Windows) and 8.18.0 (Linux).
- **[environment ENV-11]** stderr gets the `% Total % Received ...` header and the progress lines. REF 8.22 and REF-LINUX 8.18 both do this.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[cli-options CLIO-13]** stderr is empty.
- **[http-requests HR-11]** stderr is empty. The request bytes are identical.
- **[environment ENV-11]** stderr is empty. stdout and the exit code are the same as REF.

**Notes**

- **[http-requests HR-11]** *Note:* REF's behaviour contradicts the `-s` documentation and is probably a curl quirk. Strict drop-in parity still differs.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-requests HR-11]** the progress-meter enablement in `Curl.Cli.UnitLibrary`. Exact line not located.
- **[environment ENV-11]** not located.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-188"></a>
### CGR-188: Windows: `--create-dirs` for an output path longer than MAX_PATH succeeds in PORT; REF fails with exit 23 before sending the request

- **Severity:** Low
- **Area:** config-glob-output, environment
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: [config-glob-output CGO-10] Confirmed on Windows.
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `config-glob-output CGO-10`, `environment ENV-14`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (config-glob-output):* E = `SCR\evidence\config-glob-output`. Windows server: `dotnet run E\srv\server.cs -- 20102 E\verify\log.txt` (listens on 127.0.0.1 and [::1], logs raw requests, replies `200 OK` with body `path=<request target>`; query keys `lm=` adds Last-Modified, `cd=`/`cdhex=` add Content-Disposition, `size=n` body of n `A`, `short=n` over-declares Content-Length, `status=n`). Linux: `python3 E/linux/server.py 20103 log`. `$U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20102` (20103 on Linux). Run each case in a fresh directory with HOME, USERPROFILE and APPDATA pointing at it and CURL_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset. Verifier scripts: `E\verify\v1_stdin.ps1`, `v2_misc.ps1`, `v3_misc.ps1`, `v4_maxpath.ps1`, `E\verify\linux\vl.sh`.
- *Setup (environment):* EV = `SCR\evidence\environment`. Windows: `dotnet run EV\server.cs 21200` (echo server: returns the raw request as the body; `/bin` returns bytes 0..255) and `dotnet run EV\s2\server2.cs 21201` (same, used as a proxy). `EV\verify_windows.ps1` runs each case in isolated `aref`/`port` directories with HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA at an empty directory. Linux: `EV\linux\verify.sh` and `EV\linux\vtls.sh` (echo on 21210, proxy on 21211, `openssl s_server` on 21213).
- **[config-glob-output CGO-10]** --create-dirs succeeds past MAX_PATH where curl fails before sending the request (Windows)
  - from a working directory whose full path is 190 characters long, run `curl -sS --create-dirs -o "D/D/D/D/D/D/f" $U/x`, where each D is 50 `d` characters.
    - Script: `E\verify\v4_maxpath.ps1`. It runs the command twice; the result is the same both times.
- **[environment ENV-14]** `--create-dirs` for an output path longer than MAX_PATH succeeds in the port and fails with exit 23 in REF
  - `curl -sS --create-dirs -o aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\bbbb(40).bin http://127.0.0.1:21200/bin`. That is five nested directories with 50-character names and a 40-character file name, about 470 characters as an absolute path. Verifier case: v-long-create.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [config-glob-output CGO-10]
curl -sS --create-dirs -o "D/D/D/D/D/D/f" $U/x
E\verify\v4_maxpath.ps1
# [environment ENV-14]
curl -sS --create-dirs -o aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\aaaa(50)\bbbb(40).bin http://127.0.0.1:21200/bin
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-10]** 
  - Creates only the first directory.
  - stderr: `curl: Error creating directory dddd.../dddd...` (wrapped over several lines), then `curl: (23) Failed writing received data to disk/application`, exit 23.
  - No request is sent.
- **[environment ENV-14]** `curl: Error creating directory ...` then `curl: (23) Failed writing received data to disk/application`. Exit 23 and no file is written.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-10]** creates all six directories, sends `GET /x`, writes `f` and exits 0.
- **[environment ENV-14]** Creates the directories and writes the 256-byte file, exit 0.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[config-glob-output CGO-10]** `Curl.Console/PhysicalOutputPaths.cs:24`. `Directory.CreateDirectory` handles long paths.
- **[environment ENV-14]** not located.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Windows server: `EV\srvbin\server.exe 21100 21101` (source `EV\srv\server.cs`); repro script `EV\repro_findings.sh` (uses the `d.sh` diff harness). Linux: `python3 EV/linux/srv.py 21150 21151`; repro `EV/linux/verify_lin.sh`. `H=http://127.0.0.1:21100` (21150 on Linux); `b64() { printf "$1" | base64 -w0 | sed 's/+/%2B/g; s/\//%2F/g; s/=/%3D/g'; }`; `$H/raw?b=<b64>` replies with exactly those bytes (`&keep=1` keeps the connection).
- *Setup (upstream-cases):* EV = `SCR\evidence\upstream-cases`. Cross-platform runs: `EV\verify\diff.sh`, driven in WSL by `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "/mnt/c/Users/Stewart Rogers/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/Z--repos-Curl-ThirdPartyReview/3796612b-55d9-44ec-9722-80e35c3282a1/scratchpad/evidence/upstream-cases/verify/sync.sh" vN.sh` (N = 1..4), against the canned recording server `EV\verify\srv.py` (configs in `EV\verify\conf\`). Windows-native runs: `EV\verify\vwin.ps1` (wraps `harness\Diff-Curl.ps1` and `Record-CurlExchange.ps1`).
- **[http-responses HR-16]** Response-header size limit: PORT writes one extra header line to -D/-i, and %{num_headers} is 0
  - `h_many.bin` = a status line plus 4000 headers `X-H<n>: ` + 70 x `v`, then `Content-Length: 2` (about 320 KB).
  - Commands: `curl -s -S -D - -o NUL http://127.0.0.1:20400/h_many` and `curl -s -S -o NUL -w "%{http_code} %{num_headers} %{size_header}" http://127.0.0.1:20400/h_many`
- **[network-robustness NR-10]** %{size_header} after a `Too large response headers` (56) failure counts the last header twice
  - `curl -sS -o NUL -w '%{size_header}\n' "$H/bighdrs?n=4&size=100000"`; also `n=10&size=40000`.
- **[upstream-cases UC-12]** Response-header size limit: PORT writes one more header line to the -i output than curl before failing with exit 56
  - `verify\v3.sh`, server `verify\conf\hdr497.py` (test497 data: 9 headers, then 1750 repeated 178-byte headers, LF line ends). Run `curl -s -S -i -o o.txt http://127.0.0.1:21360/497`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [http-responses HR-16]
curl -s -S -D - -o NUL http://127.0.0.1:20400/h_many
curl -s -S -o NUL -w "%{http_code} %{num_headers} %{size_header}" http://127.0.0.1:20400/h_many
# [network-robustness NR-10]
curl -sS -o NUL -w '%{size_header}\n' "$H/bighdrs?n=4&size=100000"
# [upstream-cases UC-12]
curl -s -S -i -o o.txt http://127.0.0.1:21360/497
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-16]** exit 56 `Too large response headers: 307277 > 307200`. -D writes 307277 bytes. -w prints `200 3807 307277`.
- **[network-robustness NR-10]** exit 56 `Too large response headers: 400057 > 307200`; -w `400057` (n=10: `320097`).
- **[upstream-cases UC-12]** Exit 56, `curl: (56) Too large response headers: 307325 > 307200`. o.txt has 1744 lines (307325 bytes).

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[http-responses HR-16]** same exit and message. -D writes 307358 bytes (one extra header line). -w prints `200 0 307358`. Same on Linux.
- **[network-robustness NR-10]** the same exit and message, but -w `500067` (n=10: `360107`), exactly one header line too many.
- **[upstream-cases UC-12]** Exit 56 with the same message. o.txt has 1745 lines (307502 bytes): it writes the header that crossed the limit.

**Notes**

- **[upstream-cases UC-12]** *Verifier note:* The original line counts (1741/1742) came from different data; the off-by-one holds.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[http-responses HR-16]** `HttpResponseHeadBuilder.cs:137` (`HeadBytesWithPendingHeader`) also writes the pending header after `Append` throws.
- **[network-robustness NR-10]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary/HttpResponseHeadBuilder.cs` (size accounting after the overflow).
- **[upstream-cases UC-12]** `Curl.Original.Protocol.Http.UnitLibrary\HttpResponseHeadBuilder.cs` (MaximumHeadSize check after the write).

Scriptable server: `dotnet EV\srv\out\srv.dll EV\srv.log 20500 20501 20502s` (20502 is TLS, self-signed); route files in a case's `routes\` folder, `p.1.http` answers the first hit on `/p`, `p.2.http` the second. Windows: start the echo server `pwsh -NoProfile -File SCR\evidence\cli-options\echoserver.ps1 -Port 20000` (replies 200 with the raw request bytes as the body); `@U` = `http://127.0.0.1:20000/`; port 20002 is left closed. Harness: `SCR\evidence\cli-options\h.sh <name> <args>` runs REF and PORT and stores exit code, stdout, stderr and files. Linux: `python3 linux/echo.py 20001` (in the evidence folder); `URL` = `http://127.0.0.1:20001/`. Verifier scripts: `verify/v1_win.sh`, `verify/v4_win.sh`, `verify/v2_linux.sh`, `verify/v3_linux.sh`.
- *Setup (proxy-connect):* EV = `SCR\evidence\proxy-connect`. Scripted recording server: `EV\srv\out\srv.exe <port> <log> '<script for conn 1>' ['<script for conn 2>' ...]` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`); steps are `;`-separated: `H` read a request head, `HN` read a head and answer nothing yet, `OK`/`CE`/`403`/`403B`/`407B` canned replies, `W:<bytes>` write literal bytes, `S4`/`S5G`/`S5U`/`S5R` read SOCKS messages, `E` record raw bytes until EOF. In repros `srv` means this binary. Harnesses `EV\harness.ps1` and `EV\lharness.sh`; verifier `EV\v_win*.ps1`, `EV\v_linux.sh`, `EV\v_l3.sh`.
- *Setup (doh-ipfs-resolution):* EV = `SCR\evidence\doh-ipfs-resolution`. Test server `EV\srv\out\srv.exe` (Linux `EV/srv/outlinux/srv`, source `EV\srv\Program.cs`); in repros `srv` means this binary. Options: `doh=<port>` plain-HTTP DoH responder, `dohs=<port>` TLS DoH (`selfsigned=1` or `pfx=`), `web=`/`webs=` web targets, `web2=` recording proxy, `rr=name:TYPE:addr` records, `mangle=http10|hang` faults, `webstatus=`/`weblocation=`. Harness `EV\harness.ps1`; verifier `EV\v1.ps1`, `EV\v2.ps1` (outputs `EV\cases\v_*.txt`); Linux `EV\linux\run1.sh vl.py`.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-17]** The connect-failure verbose line says "port 0" instead of the bound local port
  - `curl -s -v http://127.0.0.1:20799/` (nothing is listening).
- **[cli-options CLIO-19]** Verbose output for a failed connect reports local port 0
  - `curl -v http://127.0.0.1:20002/`.
- **[proxy-connect PC-15]** -v "connect to ... from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed" shows port 0 instead of the local port that was used
  - with no server on the port, run `curl -sv http://127.0.0.1:20699/`. Verifier cases: v22 and VL17.
- **[doh-ipfs-resolution DOH-17]** -v prints "connect to ... from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed" when moving to the next address
  - `srv web=21802`, then `curl -v -sS --resolve foo.test:21802:127.0.0.9,127.0.0.1 http://foo.test:21802/x`. Cases: `cases\v_f17_multi_resolve_v.txt`, `linux\cases\vl_f17_multi.txt`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [writeout-verbose WV-17]
curl -s -v http://127.0.0.1:20799/
# [cli-options CLIO-19]
curl -v http://127.0.0.1:20002/
# [proxy-connect PC-15]
curl -sv http://127.0.0.1:20699/
# [doh-ipfs-resolution DOH-17]
srv web=21802
curl -v -sS --resolve foo.test:21802:127.0.0.9,127.0.0.1 http://foo.test:21802/x
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-17]** 
  - Windows: `* connect to 127.0.0.1 port 20799 from 0.0.0.0 port 65138 failed: Connection refused`
  - Linux: `... from 127.0.0.1 port NNNNN ...`
- **[cli-options CLIO-19]** `* connect to 127.0.0.1 port 20002 from 0.0.0.0 port <ephemeral> failed: Connection refused`.
- **[proxy-connect PC-15]** `* connect to 127.0.0.1 port 20699 from 0.0.0.0 port 54415 failed: Connection refused`. Linux 8.18 prints `from 127.0.0.1 port N`.
- **[doh-ipfs-resolution DOH-17]** on Windows there is no `connect to ... failed` line between the two `Trying` lines. On Linux it prints `connect to 127.0.0.9 port 21802 from 127.0.0.1 port <n> failed: Connection refused`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-17]** `... from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed: Connection refused`
- **[cli-options CLIO-19]** `... from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed: Connection refused`.
- **[proxy-connect PC-15]** `... from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed: Connection refused` on both platforms.
- **[doh-ipfs-resolution DOH-17]** `* connect to 127.0.0.9 port 21802 from 0.0.0.0 port 0 failed: Connection refused` on both platforms.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[writeout-verbose WV-17]** `Curl.Networking.UnitLibrary/TcpConnector.cs` does not read the local endpoint after a failed connect.
- **[doh-ipfs-resolution DOH-17]** `Curl.Networking.UnitLibrary/TcpConnector.cs`.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Windows server: `cd EV\srv && dotnet run wvsrv.cs -- 20700 EV\resp EV\req.log` (HTTP on 127.0.0.1/::1:20700, a mini FTP server on 20701, TLS on 20702; `/raw/<name>` serves `EV\resp\<name>.txt`; other routes `/code/N`, `/redir/N`, `/hang/ms`, `/close` (empty reply), `/ka`, `/echo`, `/p`). Linux: `EV\linux\srv.py` on 20710. One-line repros for every finding: `EV\repro_findings.sh` (Windows) and `EV\linux\verify_linux.sh`.
- **[upstream-cases UC-15]** The progress meter is printed on some early failures by REF but not by PORT
  - `verify\v2.sh`.
    - POP3 (`verify\conf\pop3.json`): `curl pop3://127.0.0.1:21361/9 -u user:secret`
    - SMTP (`smtp.json`): `curl smtp://127.0.0.1:21362/907 --mail-rcpt bad@example.com --mail-from sender@example.com -T upload`
- **[proxy-connect PC-16]** No progress meter is written when a CONNECT is refused
  - run `srv 20600 log 'HN;403'`, then run `curl -p -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 http://example.test/` without -s, with stdout redirected. Verifier cases: v23 and VL18.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-21]** Connection refused: no progress meter header or zero row before the error (Linux)
  - `curl -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:20799/`, run 2 more times by the verifier.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
# [upstream-cases UC-15]
curl pop3://127.0.0.1:21361/9 -u user:secret
curl smtp://127.0.0.1:21362/907 --mail-rcpt bad@example.com --mail-from sender@example.com -T upload
# [proxy-connect PC-16]
srv 20600 log 'HN;403'
curl -p -x http://127.0.0.1:20600 http://example.test/
# [writeout-verbose WV-21]
curl -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:20799/
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- **[upstream-cases UC-15]** The meter header and a zero line, then `curl: (8) Weird server reply` (POP3) or `curl: (55) ...` (SMTP).
- **[proxy-connect PC-16]** stderr has the meter header lines and a zero line, then `curl: (7) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-21]** *REF-LINUX 8.18:* The two meter header lines and a zero row, then `curl: (7) ...`

**Actual (Curl)**

- **[upstream-cases UC-15]** Only the `curl: (N) ...` line. Exit codes match (8 and 55).
- **[proxy-connect PC-16]** stderr has only `curl: (7) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`.
- **[writeout-verbose WV-21]** *PORT-LINUX:* Only the `curl: (7)` line.

**Notes**

- **[upstream-cases UC-15]** *Verifier note:* The reverse case (test2114, where PORT prints the meter and REF does not) and the test94 proxy case were not re-run.

**Suspected location in source**

- **[upstream-cases UC-15]** Curl.Output.UnitLibrary (progress meter start).
- **[writeout-verbose WV-21]** `Curl.Console/TransferProgressRecorder.cs`

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-253: curl_ws_recv delivers a large frame in 16 KiB pieces even when the caller's buffer holds the whole frame

- **Severity:** Low
- **Area:** libcurl-api
- **Platform(s):** Both (Windows and Linux)
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (Windows, Linux).
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `libcurl-api LA-20`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (libcurl-api):* EV = `SCR\evidence\libcurl-api`. Build the probe: `cd EV\probe && dotnet build -c Release -o out`. It calls REF libcurl (`C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\bin\libcurl-4.dll`) through P/Invoke and the port's managed `Libcurl.dll` (`SCR\Curl\Libcurl\bin\Release\net10.0`) in the same process against the same loopback server. `EV\probe\out\probe.exe repro` starts an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:21410 and prints REF and PORT side by side; other subcommands: `ws`, `sweep`, `multiids`, `cb`, `upload http10`, `form` (21411), `printf2`, `url1`, `lport`, `state`. Linux: `dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained -o EV\verify\outlinux`, then `EV\verify\linux_verify.sh`.
- run `probe.exe ws len64k`. The server sends one 70000-byte binary frame, and the client calls curl_ws_recv with a 100000-byte buffer.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
probe.exe ws len64k
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- a single call returns n=70000.

**Actual (Curl)**

- five calls return n=16374, 16384, 16384, 16384 and 4474, with offset and bytesleft metadata. The data is correct and partial delivery is allowed by the API, but code that assumes one call per frame when the buffer is large enough behaves differently.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Engine.UnitLibrary\ManagedEasyWebSocket.cs:32` (`ReadSize = 16 * 1024`).

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

**Suspected location in source**

- **Severity:** Low

- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `libcurl-multi-callbacks LMC-17`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (libcurl-multi-callbacks):* EV = `SCR\evidence\libcurl-multi-callbacks`. A C# probe (`EV\probe\`) runs one driver per case against REF `libcurl-4.dll` (P/Invoke) and PORT `Libcurl.dll` (its C# API), with a built-in recording server: 127.0.0.1:21700 answers `200 hello`, 21701 answers `200 other`, 21799 is closed. Run `EV\probe\out\probe.exe <cases> 2` or `powershell -File EV\run.ps1 -Filter <cases> -Out <name> -Reps 2` (`LIBONLY=REF` or `LIBONLY=PORT` runs one side). Linux: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash "<EV as /mnt/c path>/linux.sh" <cases> 1 <name>`.
- case `C_57_xferinfo_returns`, variant ret=0x10000001: NOPROGRESS=0, GET `http://127.0.0.1:21700/`. The probe compares stdout only, and that matches, so capture stderr for each side separately:
  1. `set LIBONLY=REF` then `probe.exe C_57 1 2> c57_REF.err`
  2. `set LIBONLY=PORT` then `probe.exe C_57 1 2> c57_PORT.err`

```sh
set LIBONLY=REF
probe.exe C_57 1 2> c57_REF.err
set LIBONLY=PORT
probe.exe C_57 1 2> c57_PORT.err
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- libcurl's meter is written to stderr (470 bytes, starting `  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed ...`). rc=0.

**Actual (Curl)**

- stderr is empty (0 bytes). rc=0, and the body matches.

**Suspected location in source**

- the PORT code that dispatches TransferInfoCallback does not map `ProgressCallbackResult.Continue` to the default meter. Exact line not located.

**Acceptance criterion:** Running the probe case(s) in the repro gives PORT return codes, callback sequences, CURLINFO values and bytes on the wire equal to REF's on Windows and REF-LINUX's on Linux (Expected).

- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- A persistent CRL server: `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe crl 21990 www=E\pki` (it serves `rev.crl` for every `*.crl` path). The server certificate `E\pki\certs\rev4R.pfx` (REF) / `rev4P.pfx` (PORT) has CDP `http://127.0.0.1:21990/rev4?.crl`. Run `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe http 21900 pfx=E\pki\certs\rev4R.pfx`, then `curl -sS --cacert E\pki\rca.crt https://localhost:21900/` (also with `--ssl-revoke-best-effort`, certificate `rev2`). Verifier cases: `v_crl_rev_default`, `v_crl_rev_best` (`E\v.ps1 -Only crl`). The CRL log `E\cases\v_crlserver.log` shows that both REF and PORT fetched their own CRL. For the staple variant, see TPR-02 (`v_st_rev_default`).

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe crl 21990 www=E\pki
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe http 21900 pfx=E\pki\certs\rev4R.pfx
curl -sS --cacert E\pki\rca.crt https://localhost:21900/
E\v.ps1 -Only crl
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- Exit 60 `curl: (60) schannel: trust for this certificate or one of the certificates in the certificate chain has been revoked`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- Exit 60. The CRL case prints `curl: (60) schannel: the certificate or certificate chain is based on an untrusted root`, and the staple case prints `curl: (60) schannel: the revocation status is unknown`. The exit code is right but the reason is wrong. The good, dead-CDP, no-CDP and `--ssl-no-revoke` CRL cases match.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Networking.UnitLibrary\TlsFailureMessages.cs:772-791` (`SchannelCaCertificateFileChainError`). It has no branch for `X509ChainStatusFlags.Revoked`, so revocation falls through to the "untrusted root" text.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

<a id="cgr-288"></a>
### CGR-288: Windows `--ftp-ssl-ccc`: curl's Schannel build often clears the control channel on a later connection and completes; PORT fails every URL with exit 81

- **Severity:** Low (CCC on Windows; REF itself fails the first attempt and is nondeterministic)
- **Area:** tls-protocols-revocation
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed. Detail: Confirmed (verifier reproduced it in two cases; REF's success is not deterministic)
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `tls-protocols-revocation TPR-11`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ftp 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx updir=E\up`. The server accepts CCC, sends close_notify, skips the client's TLS records and continues in plaintext. Then run `curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd --ftp-ssl-ccc ftp://localhost:21900/file.txt ftp://localhost:21900/file2.txt` (or three URLs). Verifier cases: `v_ccc_two`, `v_ccc_three`. With a single URL both exit 81.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ftp 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx updir=E\up
curl -sS -k --ssl-reqd --ftp-ssl-ccc ftp://localhost:21900/file.txt ftp://localhost:21900/file2.txt
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- The first connection fails with `curl: (81) Failed to clear the command channel (CCC)`. On the next connections the server logs `CCC down: skipped 1 TLS records from client`, then plaintext `PWD`/`EPSV`/`RETR`. The overall exit is 0 and the later files are printed (`hello ftp`). The original run `b5_ccc13_two_v4` shows that REF can also fail every attempt.

**Actual (Curl)**

- The server sees a reset right after `CCC` on every connection. Every URL fails with exit 81 (`Failed to clear the command channel (CCC)` once per URL), and nothing is printed.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ftp.UnitLibrary\FtpSession.cs:713-745` (`ClearControlTlsAsync`). Its comment says that CCC "never can" succeed on curl's Schannel build. Also `Connection.ClearTlsAsync`.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

### CGR-289: Windows `ldaps://`: PORT uses one connection with SNI `localhost` and honours `--cacert`; curl's WinLDAP makes a second connection with the machine name as SNI and uses the system store

- **Severity:** Low
- **Area:** tls-protocols-revocation
- **Platform(s):** Windows
- **Confidence:** Confirmed
- **Related existing finding (GF/AF):** none
- **Source findings:** `tls-protocols-revocation TPR-12`

**Reproduction**

- *Setup (tls-protocols-revocation):* E = `SCR\evidence\tls-protocols-revocation`; TP = `SCR\evidence\tls\pki` (srv.crt/srv.key/srv.pfx password `x`, ca.crt for CN localhost). Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Also `openssl s_server`. Revocation PKI `E\pki` (`rca.crt`; `ocg*` good, `ocr*` revoked with staples `certs\<tag>.ocsp`; `rev*` with CDP on port 21990). Harness `E\h.ps1`, `E\linux\lh.sh`; verifier `E\v.ps1`, `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ldap 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx` (implicit TLS), then `curl -sS -k ldaps://localhost:21900/dc=test`, and `curl -sS --cacert TP\ca.crt --ssl-no-revoke ldaps://localhost:21900/dc=test`. Verifier cases: `v_ldaps_k`, `v_ldaps_ca`.

Commands (run each with REF and with PORT):

```sh
E\srv\out\tsrv.exe ldap 21900 pfx=TP\srv.pfx
curl -sS -k ldaps://localhost:21900/dc=test
curl -sS --cacert TP\ca.crt --ssl-no-revoke ldaps://localhost:21900/dc=test
```

**Expected (real curl)**

- `-k`: one TLS connection with SNI `localhost` that is closed, then a second TLS connection with SNI = the machine host name, carrying 3 RootDSE searches, an NTLM bind and an unbind. It exits 38 `curl: (38) LDAP local: bind via ldap_win_bind Protocol Error`. With `--cacert`, the second handshake fails (system store, host-name SNI), and it exits 38 `curl: (38) LDAP local: bind via ldap_win_bind Server Down`.

**Actual (Curl)**

- A single TLS connection with SNI `localhost`. It sends the 3 searches and the NTLM bind twice (8 messages and an unbind; the NTLM flags also differ, `B7B208E2` vs `07B208A2`), then exits 38 `curl: (38) LDAP local: bind via ldap_win_bind Local Error` in both cases. With `--cacert` it trusts a server that WinLDAP does not. The exit codes match.

**Suspected location in source**

- `Curl.Original.Protocol.Ldap.UnitLibrary\LdapProtocolHandler.cs` and `WinLdapResultText.cs`. The emulated WinLDAP path does not reproduce WinLDAP's own TLS connection or trust store.

**Acceptance criterion:** For every repro command above, PORT's exit code, stdout bytes, stderr text, files written and bytes on the wire equal REF's on Windows (Expected); repro variants that already matched still match.

Server `E\srv\out\tsrv.exe <smtp|imap|pop3|ftp|ldap|http|proxy|crl> <port> pfx=<pfx> [tls=implicit|starttls|none] [tls12=1] [strict=1] [updir=<dir>] [mode=reneg|nonotify|closedelim] [www=<dir>]` (Linux `E\srv\outlinux\tsrv`; it logs every client message, `Cs:` = inside TLS). Then run `curl -sS --cacert pki/rca.crt https://localhost:<p>/index.txt` (no `--cert-status`), and the same with `-k`. Verifier cases: `V_st_req_nocs`, `V_st_req_nocs_k`.

## Appendix A. Tested and matching (coverage)

What each area exercised where PORT matched REF. Condensed from the area reports; nested lists are flattened into one line per topic. Counts of runs are approximate.

### A.1 cli-options

- A missing argument for every one of the 146 arg-taking options (`option --X: requires parameter`, exit 2).
- `--help <category>` for all categories, and `--help <option>` for all 335 option names. `--manual` and `-M` are byte-identical.
- Numeric options x 21 edge values for 18 options (380 Windows runs). The `--limit-rate`/`--max-filesize` unit suffixes, `--rate` forms, `-C`, `-r`, `-z`, `--proto*` specs, `--ftp-method`, `--ftp-ssl-ccc-mode`, `--ip-tos` names, `--parallel-max` and `--trace-config`.
- Short-option bundling, long-option forms (`--opt=value`, abbreviations refused, case, `---silent`, `--`, a lone `-`).
- `--no-` negation for all 128 boolean options and `--opt=x` on booleans. The `--no-`/`--expand-` variants.
- `-q`, `--disable`, `-:`/`--next` semantics, repeated options, option conflicts, empty arguments.
- A fuzz of 142 arg options x 10 odd values (about 1250 of the 1384 runs match; the differences are listed above).
- Config files (`-K`): 30 crafted files, `-K -`, and a missing file.
- `-w` format edge cases, `--variable`/`--expand-*`, URL globbing.
- Output naming and sanitising on Windows, `--output-dir`, `--create-dirs`.
- The binary stdin consumers (`--data-binary @-`, `--data-urlencode @-`, `--url-query @-`, `-H @-`, `-T -`, `-F f=@-`, `-b -`, `-K -`).
- `--libcurl file.c`, `-D -`, `-c -`, `--trace`/`--trace-ascii`, and the stderr CR/LF bytes.
- The options REF does not support that PORT also refuses (`--http3`, `--http3-only`, the TLS build options).
- `-V` output (apart from the library list, the Debug feature and the hidden smb), and the acceptance of 28 schemes (all except smb/smbs).
- The Linux subset (bundling, `--`, negation, `--next`, numerics, `-K`, help). Linux-only message differences that match Windows 8.22 were treated as 8.18 version differences.
- Headers (`-H`, `-A`, `-u`, `-b`, `-e`, `-X`) with non-ASCII values on Windows: both use the ANSI code page.
- The verifier's extra checks: on Windows, `--connect-timeout 0.01`/`0.001`, `-6` with an IPv4 literal, and `--keepalive-cnt 2147483648` (both exit 2) match.

### A.2 config-glob-output

- These are the original tester's results. The verifier did not re-run them.

### A.3 url-parsing

- **Harness:** the Windows harness is `E\harness.ps1` (function `D`), with batches `E\b01..b18.ps1` and `E\confirm*.ps1`. The Linux harness is `E\wsl\lharness.py` with `cases1.py` and `cases2.py`. The normalisations were the User-Agent value, `curl/8.x.y`, `after N ms` and the Debug-build WARNING line.
- **Schemes:**: Upper and mixed case (HTTP://, hTtP://, HTTPS, FILE, WSS).; Unknown schemes (foo, htt).; Scheme syntax: digits, `+`, `-` and `.`, a leading digit, 40/41 characters, empty.; 0, 1, 3 and 4 slashes, leading and trailing spaces, mailto:, data: and javascript:.
- **Scheme guessing:**: Prefixes ftp./FTP./dict./Dict./ldap./imap./smtp./pop3./www./mqtt./gopher./telnet./rtsp./tftp./scp./ws.; The bare names `ftp` and `ftp.`.; Userinfo before a guessed host, IPv6 without a scheme, and a lone `localhost`.
- **--proto-default:** https, ftp, FTP, bad, empty, with an explicit scheme, IPv6, ws, file, space, 100 characters.
- **--proto:** -http, =https, -all, `-all,+http`, =HTTP, xyz, empty, `,,,`, ` http`, =ws, and the option applied to guessed schemes.
- **--proto-redir:**: The defaults for 22 target schemes.; Lists with `+` and `-`.; `--proto -ftp` combined with `--proto-redir +ftp`.
- **Userinfo:**: user:pass, user only, an empty user or password.; The escapes %40, %3A, %2F, %23, %20, %00 and %zz.; A raw `@`, `;auth=` options and a raw `#`.; 300-character and 70000-character users.; `-u` overriding the URL, `-u` with non-ASCII, and `--disallow-username-in-url`.
- **Ports:** 0, 65535, 65536, junk, empty, leading zeros, -1, +N, 20 digits, hex, a fraction, two ports, a space, and the default ports.
- **IPv4 forms (32 cases):** decimal, octal, hex and short forms, overflow, trailing dots, empty labels, 08, 1e1, and 0x alone.
- **IPv6:**: ::1, the full form, leading zeros, upper-case hex (not mapped), a v4 tail.; Too long, garbage after `]`, an empty `[]`, vFuture, a missing `]`.; Zone ids %25lo, %251 and -._~, zone lengths 14/15/120/130, and `-g`.
- **Paths:**: Dot-segment removal (17 variants), `--path-as-is` and `--no-path-as-is`, double slashes.; Special characters and all printable ASCII, glob brackets with `-g`, backslashes in http paths.; Control characters and spaces rejected, bad `%` escapes, a 30000-character path, raw UTF-8 from `-K`.
- **Query and fragment:** all forms, including url.query and url.fragment write-out.
- **-G/-d:** request lines for 19 variants.
- **--url-query:** request lines for 18 variants.
- **--request-target:** *, /other?q, absolute, `a b`, empty, dots, CRLF, and through a proxy.
- **HTTP proxy absolute-form:**: Case of the host and scheme, userinfo, the default port, an empty port, `--path-as-is`.; IDN, an integer IP, compressed IPv6, a fragment, a trailing dot.; The proxy given without a scheme or with a path, a bad proxy scheme or port, an IPv6 proxy, proxy userinfo.
- **Redirects:**: Relative, `./`, `../`, deep `../`, an absolute path, query-only, fragment-only, empty, scheme-relative, absolute, upper case.; Spaces, a raw Latin-1 byte, %2f, backslashes, `;x`, userinfo, a bad port, IPv6, a trailing `..`, a 3000-character path, `#`, leading and trailing spaces, `--path-as-is`.
- **Write-out:** the url.\* and urle.\* parts for 12 URLs, and unknown write-out variables.
- **file:// URLs:** drive-letter forms, localhost, another host, `c|`, UNC, a query, %20, a real file, dots, user and port refused, `file://` alone, file:relative, and IP and IPv6 hosts.
- **-O names:** from URLs with a query or fragment, %20 and %2F, a trailing slash, dots, `-G`, no path, %41.
- **-K config URLs:** 60 kB and 1.1 MB (exit 100 for both), escapes, a 70000-character host (`Too long hostname`), a 70000-character user.

- **--json:** basic, several values, @file, @-, empty, with -d, with -G, with -X PUT, and Content-Type/Accept overrides.
- **-F:**: text, file, `;type=`, `;filename=` variants, `;headers=` (inline, @file, several), `;encoder=` variants; `<file`, @-, `<-`, comma lists, nested forms, --form-string, --form-escape; MIME type guessing (about 25 extensions), path forms, a custom multipart Content-Type and boundary, -X PUT, many parts, --next

(chunked with Expect), an empty file, a missing file, globs, -g, several URLs; -X POST, a chunked override, --http1.0 with -T -, -r, -C offset, --crlf, -a, Expect: off or custom, and --expect100-timeout

- **Chunked uploads:** -T - of 200 KB, -T file of 200 KB, -F @- of 200 KB, chunked with HTTP/1.0, the Trailer header, TE `gzip, chunked`, and CHUNKED in upper case.

### A.5 http-responses

- `-i`, `-D -`, `-D file`, `-I`: byte-identical output for a basic 200, and for HEAD with Content-Length, with a body or with no length.
- Header folding (obs-fold) in -i, -D, `%header{}` and header_json. Folded Location, Content-Type, Connection and Content-Length.
- Duplicate headers: in -i, in `%header{}` (takes the first) and in header_json (lists all). LF-only and mixed CR/LF heads, missing reason phrase, trailing blank in the reason, tab separator.
- Malformed header lines: CR-only line (exit 8), NUL in a header (8), header without colon (8), empty header name, space in the name, space before the colon.
- Message framing: HTTP/1.0 with no length (read to close), HTTP/1.1 with no length, HTTP/0.9 refused (exit 1) and allowed with `--http0.9`.
- Status-line variants: HTTP/1.2, HTTP/3, HTTP/1, negative code, two spaces, lower-case `http/`, `200OK`, RTSP/ICY, 2-digit code, garbage code, status line only (52), head with no blank line then close, status/header/chunk split across TCP writes.
- Content-Length: Larger than the body (18), smaller than the body, `--ignore-content-length` either way.; Invalid values `-1`, `abc`, `+5`, `0x5`, `5abc`, empty (exit 8).; Duplicates with the same and different values, `5, 5`, huge (overflow), 2^63-1, leading zeros, tab, space before the colon, lower-case name.
- Chunked: Chunk extensions (quoted, tab, 20KB), trailers in -i, -D and `%header{}`, `--raw`.; Bad, huge, negative, empty and `0x` sizes, 16-17 hex digits, leading zeros.; Truncated body, missing CRLF, LF-only.; Chunked plus CL, HTTP/1.0 chunked, TE gzip+chunked, `chunked,gzip` order, duplicate TE headers, identity, empty TE, 200 trailers, NUL in a trailer, data after the last chunk.
- `--compressed` with gzip, deflate (zlib and raw), br and zstd: Normal, chunked, no length, truncated, corrupted mid-stream, garbage, empty.; Trailing junk (23/61), `--raw`, HEAD.; x-gzip, upper-case name, identity, unknown (61), double gzip (good and bad), two CE headers, multi-member gzip (23), FNAME flag, missing trailer.; CE on 204/304/404 with `--fail-with-body`, `-w size_download`.
- 1xx responses: 100, 100 with headers in -D, 102+103, 199, 30 x 100.; 100 then close (52), 100 with a body (8), 100 with no blank line (8), HTTP/1.0 100.; 100 with -I, -f or TE, 103 in -D.
- 204/304/205 with a body, with no length, chunked. HTTP/1.0 204, `-z` with 304/412, HEAD 304 with CL.
- --fail: `--fail` (22) for 400/401/404/407/500/999; 399 passes.; `--fail-with-body` with -i, -o, -D and -O. `-f -O` writes no file.; `--fail-early` on 2 URLs. A 404 with a short body under -f vs `--fail-with-body` (22 vs 18). `-f` with `--retry`, `-f -C` with 416.
- -J: Quoted and unquoted names, `../` and `..\` traversal, absolute `/` and `C:\`, subdirectories.; `filename*` UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1, both forms together, %-encoding.; Semicolon, unterminated quote, case, inline, colon, wildcards, control characters, embedded quote, spaces, CON/nul.txt, trailing dot, 300-char name (Windows).; Existing file (23), `--no-clobber`, -i, -D, `-w filename_effective`, `--output-dir` with `--create-dirs` and with traversal, `-f` with 404, two CD headers.; -O without -J, URL-derived names, -O with no file part.
- Header limits: a single 100KB header around the boundary (ok), a single 200KB header (100), a folded line growing past the limit (100), 2000 headers (ok), a 5000-char reason phrase.
- Body handling: `-N`/`--no-buffer`, `--raw` with CL short, `--max-filesize` with CL, no length and chunked (63), `-m` on a stalled chunked body (28), RST mid-body (18) and RST with no length.
- Keep-alive: 2 URLs reused, `Connection: close`, HTTP/1.0 with and without keep-alive, HEAD with CL, 304 with CL, excess bytes arriving 300ms later (both open a new connection).
- Redirects: `-L` with -D, -i, and `-w` num_redirects/num_headers/size_header. 1xx before a 302, 303 with -I, `-L -f` to a 404, two different Location headers (8), the same Location twice.
- Write-out: `%{content_type}` with blanks and duplicates, `%{size_header}`/`%{num_headers}` for LF-only heads, `%{http_version}`, a missing `%header{}`, header_json with control characters.
- Binary body to a redirected stdout.
- On a Linux TTY (through script): the binary-output warning text, `-o -`, `-s` and `-w` match, apart from HR-9.
- Linux (REF-LINUX 8.18 vs PORT-LINUX), a subset of about 110 cases: matches as on Windows except for the findings above, and except for differences that depend on 8.18 (multi-member gzip message, trailer-fold exit 43).

### A.7 proxy-connect

- Harness: `evidence\proxy-connect\harness.ps1` (Windows) and `lharness.sh` (WSL). Server: `srv\Program.cs`, a scripted TCP/unix/TLS loopback server that records every byte. Normalised: curl/VERSION in the UA, the debug-build banner and DEBUG-only lines, ephemeral local ports, "after N ms", the digest cnonce/response, the NTLM type-3 blob, the HAProxy source port, and connection order in logs.
- About 420 differential cases on Windows (b1-b10) and about 95 on WSL (l1, l2). Batch logs are b1..b10.log, l1.log and l2.log, with per-case directories under `evidence\proxy-connect\cases\`.
- -x request line: absolute-form, a proxy with no scheme, an upper-case scheme, a proxy URL with a path, query, fragment or trailing slash, an IPv6 or localhost proxy, the default port 1080, a bad port (exit 5), an unknown scheme (exit 7), and a refused connect (exit 7, message text with -sS).
- Absolute-form target URL: dot segments, --path-as-is, query plus fragment, IDN, an explicit :80 or another port, an IPv6 literal, a trailing dot, ftp:// and ws:// through an HTTP proxy, -0, -I, a custom -X, --request-target, and POST/-T upload.
- Headers: the Proxy-Connection header and its removal via -H / --proxy-header, a Host override, an empty UA, --proxy-header vs -H separation (plain and tunnel), --proxy-header @file, empty `X;` headers, duplicate names, and removing UA/Host in CONNECT.
- Proxy auth: Basic from the URL, -U or --proxy-user, with empty and colon-bearing passwords and %-encoded credentials.; --proxy-digest: MD5, qop=auth, stale, opaque, SHA-256 (exit 94 in both), the tunnel uri form, and a repeated 407.; --proxy-anyauth with Basic, Digest, NTLM and unknown schemes. --proxy-ntlm type-1 bytes (tunnel and plain).; 407 replies with a body, -f, --fail-with-body, -i and -D. 407 with Connection: close and a reconnect. 407 followed by a 401 for server auth.
- CONNECT tunnel (-p, and https via a proxy): Request bytes, :port, an IPv6 authority, --proxy1.0, and an HTTP/1.0 200 reply.; Reply variants: 2xx codes (201, 299), reply headers, Content-Length, chunked and folded replies, a NUL in a header (exit 8), a split reply, and 100 Continue.; Failures: 302, 403 and 407 (exit 7), early close and a partial reply (exit 56), and a huge header.; Output and reuse: --suppress-connect-headers, -i/-D output, %{http_connect}, two URLs on one tunnel, two hosts, and ftp over a tunnel.
- HTTPS: https via CONNECT with -k (TLS end to end), an auth retry, socks4/socks5h plus TLS, an HTTPS proxy with --proxy-insecure (plain and tunnelled https), a proxy certificate failure (exit 60), %{proxy_ssl_verify_result}, and --preproxy socks plus https.
- SOCKS4/4a, byte-exact: IP, hostname and userid, a --resolve-mapped host, reject codes 91-93, a bad version, a short or closed reply, IPv6 target refusal, and long hostname/userid limits.
- SOCKS5/5h, byte-exact: Greeting methods with and without credentials, and GSSAPI selection.; RFC1929 sub-negotiation, including a 255-byte user/password and the refusal of anything over 255, auth failure, and no acceptable method.; Every reply code 1-9 and 255 (-sS messages), and BND as a domain, IPv6 or a bad atyp.; Split replies, 255- and 256-byte hostnames, an IPv6 target, --socks5-basic, --socks5-gssapi, and port 65535.
- --preproxy (socks4/4a/5/5h, the default scheme, with -p, with an https target), and socks flags vs -x precedence.
- Env vars: http_proxy/HTTP_PROXY, https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY, all_proxy/ALL_PROXY precedence, ftp_proxy, ws_proxy, socks via env, credentials in env, an empty value, no scheme and a bad scheme. On Linux, also the case rules (both cases set, mixed case, NO_PROXY vs no_proxy).
- no_proxy / --noproxy: Host patterns: exact host, domain and .domain, suffix non-match, case, trailing dots, `*` alone and in a list, and `*.domain`.; List syntax: spaces, tabs and empty entries.; IPv4 CIDR: /0, /8, /31, /32, /33, garbage, and host bits set.; IPv6: a literal, [::1], ::/64, ::1/128 and v4-mapped.; Interaction: the CLI overriding env, an empty --noproxy, applying to socks proxies, and a redirect to a no-proxy host.
- --connect-to (wildcards, host only, port only, first wins, bad syntax, IPv6, with a proxy, the proxy host mapped, a tunnel).
- --resolve (wildcard, +, multiple addresses, IPv6 with and without brackets, bad entries with exit 49, removal, proxy-name mapping including socks4).
- -4/-6 with localhost, literals, proxies and --resolve (exit 6/7). --interface with an IP, host! and if! (exit 45). --local-port single, range, bad, 0, 65536 and reversed.
- --unix-socket (http, a missing socket with exit 7, with -x ignored, https over the socket) and --abstract-unix-socket.
- --haproxy-protocol v1 bytes (IPv4, IPv6, proxy, tunnel, unix, https proxy, socks), --haproxy-clientip v4/v6/invalid/empty, and the header sent once per connection.
- --connect-timeout and -m during a stalled CONNECT and a stalled SOCKS handshake (exit 28), --retry after a CONNECT failure, -L through a proxy and a tunnel, %{proxy_used}, %{remote_ip}, %{url_effective} and %{errormsg}.
- Exit codes 5, 7 and 97 match in every scenario above, except the ones in the findings.

### A.8 writeout-verbose

- **-w variables on a plain GET:** http_code, response_code, http_connect, http_version, exitcode, errormsg, content_type, num_headers, num_connects, num_redirects, num_retries, redirect_url, scheme, method, local_ip, remote_ip, remote_port, ssl_verify_result, proxy_ssl_verify_result, filename_effective, url_effective, url, urlnum, onerror, size_*, speed_upload, proxy_used, certs, num_certs, ftp_entry_path, referer, xfer_id, tls_earlydata.

- **%{header_json}:** ASCII escapes, duplicates and order, and behaviour across `-L`.
- **%{json}:** on success and on error, apart from conn_id, timings and the library list.
- **Template parsing:** unknown variables, `%{}`, unclosed `%{` / `%header{` / `%output{`, `%%`, a trailing `%`, backslash escapes, an empty `-w`, two `--write-out` options, and whitespace or case inside `%{}`.
- **Template sources:** `-w @file`, `@-`, `@` alone (exit 26), and `@nonexistent`.
- **Output switching:** `%{stdout}` / `%{stderr}` (also with `--stderr`), and `%output{file}`, `%output{>>file}`, `%output{}` and a missing directory.
- **-w across several transfers:** multiple URLs, globbing, `-Z`, `--fail-early`, and `-f` with several URLs.
- **-w on failures:** connection refused, bad protocol, bad URL, `file://` and `ftp://`.
- **Line endings:** CRLF endings for `-w` and `-v` output on Windows.
- **curl: (N) text and exit codes:** codes 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28 (`-m`, `--connect-timeout` on http/ftp, `-Y`/`-y`), 30, 31, 33, 36, 37, 45, 47, 48, 49, 52, 56, 58, 59, 60, 61, 63, 64, 67, 78, 90, 97 and 100. Exit 2 was also checked for the Schannel-unsupported options.
- **Error display options:** `-s`, `-S`, `-sS` and the default for all of the above. Also `-f`, `--fail-early`, `-f -i`, `-f -L`, and codes 399, 400 and 401.
- **--retry warnings:** 503, 429, `--retry-connrefused` and `--retry-all-errors`.
- **Basic -v structure:** GET, POST, `-T`, `-F`, `--compressed`, `-u`, Digest, cookies, `-L` with 301/302/303/307, `--connect-to`, `-x`, `-p`, HTTP/1.0, chunked, `-H`/`-A` removal, `-0`, `--next`, keep-alive reuse, `-C -`, localhost, TLS with `-k`, and the ws:// refusal. Also the `-v` FTP session, apart from WV-06.
- **--trace and --trace-ascii:** file and stdout formats, `--trace-time`, `--trace-ids` on a single connection, combinations with `-v`, a trace into a missing directory, and the `--trace-config` variants.
- **Progress meter:** the on/off rules (`-o` vs stdout, `-s`, `--no-progress-meter`, `-v`, `-I`, several URLs, `-O`, `--stderr`), failure lines after the meter, and the final rows on success.
- **-# bar and -Z:** the `-#` bar for known and unknown size, a slow body, a failure, connection refused, several URLs, and its combinations with other options. The parallel `-Z` meter row format.
- **Header display:** `--styled-output` / `--no-styled-output` to a non-terminal. `-D -`, `-D file`, `-i`, and `-I -L` header output.
- **Error codes for other protocols:** SOCKS, FTP, file, dict, gopher, telnet, mqtt, rtsp, ipfs, tftp, scp and sftp in the tested setups.
- **Linux subset (REF-LINUX 8.18 vs PORT-LINUX):**: Basic `-w`, `%{json}` keys, escapes and unknown variables, `%{stderr}`/`%{stdout}`/`%output`.; `-v` with keep-alive and redirects, `--trace-ascii -`, `--no-progress-meter`, `--stderr`.; Exit codes 1, 2, 6, 18, 22, 23, 26, 56, 61 and 63.; The `-#` bar, and IPv6 with `-v` and `-w`.

### A.9 tls

- Windows: no CA gives 60 with the SEC_E_UNTRUSTED_ROOT text. `--cacert` without `--ssl-no-revoke` gives 60 'revocation status is unknown'. `--cacert` with `--ssl-no-revoke` or `--ssl-revoke-best-effort` gives 0 (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], -g).
- Windows and Linux: wrong-host, expired, not-yet-valid, untrusted-CA and self-signed certificates give exit 60 with the full message text; `-k` on each gives 0.
- Windows and Linux: `--cacert` missing (2), garbage (60 on Windows, 77 on Linux), a directory (77), leaf-only, chain file, wrong CA, and PKCS7/DER/empty/CRLF/two-cert bundle/text-dump CA files. `--capath` (Windows 60, Linux 0) and a missing `--capath`.
- Windows and Linux: `-w %{ssl_verify_result}` (0/18/20/10 per platform), `%{exitcode}`, `%{errormsg}`, `%{num_certs}` and `%{proxy_ssl_verify_result}`. On Windows, `%{certs}` including the chain, TLS 1.2 and EC certificates.
- Windows and Linux: `--pinnedpubkey` with a good or bad sha256, multiple hashes, `;` plus a space, missing padding, garbage base64, an empty hash, upper-case `SHA256//`, a PEM/DER public-key file, a wrong, missing or certificate file, an empty value (2), with `--cacert`/revocation, with an expired cert, on http:// URLs, and with an EC key.
- Windows: `--tlsv1`, `--tlsv1.0`/`1.1`/`1.2`/`1.3`, `-1`, `--sslv2`/`--sslv3`/`-2`/`-3`. `--tls-max` with 1.2, 1.3, default, 1.4, bogus and empty values; min above max (2). A TLS 1.2-only server against `--tlsv1.3` (35). A TLS 1.3-only server against `--tls-max 1.2` (35). Explicit `--tlsv1.0`/`1.1` against TLS 1.0/1.1 servers. The Linux equivalents, except TLS-08.
- Windows: OpenSSL-name `--ciphers` (all 59 in both). `--tls13-ciphers` with valid, invalid, CCM, empty (2), lowercase and mismatched values. `--curves` variants. Linux: literal suite names, NOPE (59), mixed lists, TLS 1.3 suites, curves including X25519MLKEM768 and ffdhe2048, nope (59), group mismatch (35).
- ALPN: an http/1.1 server, a server that offers only a foreign protocol (35), `--no-alpn`, `--http1.0`/`1.1`, Linux `--http2` against an h1 server.
- `--cert-status` (Windows 0, Linux 91), `--ca-native`, `--ca-native` with `--cacert`, `--ssl-allow-beast`, `--no-sessionid`, `--false-start`, `--tlsauthtype`/`--tlsuser`, `--egd-file`, `--random-file`, `--ssl-sessions`, `--tls-earlydata`, `--sigalgs`, `--crlfile`, `--engine list`, `--hsts`, `--doh-insecure`, `--no-verify-host`, `--ssl-auto-client-cert`, `--ssl-reqd` on https.
- Client certificates, Windows: PEM/DER/ENG, a bad type, an encrypted key and cert-store paths (all 58 with identical text); a wrong or missing p12 password (58); a missing p12 (58). Linux: PEM, combined PEM, an encrypted key with `--pass`, a wrong pass (43), DER with types, DER without a type (58), P12 (AES and 3DES), an empty-password P12, a wrong or missing password (58), a key mismatch (43), a bad type (43), a missing file (58), and no client cert to a server that requires one over TLS 1.2 (35).
- STARTTLS: SMTP/POP3/IMAP with `--ssl-reqd`/`--ssl`, a server that does not advertise it, a server that refuses it, `--cacert`, implicit smtps, VRFY, `--tls-max`, a bad pin (90), a name mismatch (60). FTP AUTH refused under `--ssl-reqd` (64) and under `--ssl` (plain fallback). Linux SMTP equivalents. Plain FTP without TLS.
- SNI: IPv4, IPv6, mapped, decimal and short IPv4 literals send no SNI in both. `--resolve` and `--connect-to` send the URL host. A custom Host: header does not change SNI. Verification against IP SANs. A trailing-dot host on Windows.
- HTTPS through an HTTP proxy (CONNECT) and through an HTTPS proxy: `-k`, `--cacert`, no CA, bad pins, 403, `-w http_connect`, `--proxy-insecure`, `--proxy-cacert`, `--proxy-capath`, an IP-literal proxy, `--proxy-tlsv1`, `--proxy-tls13-ciphers`, `--proxy-cert` P12, an http target through an HTTPS proxy (56).
- Environment: `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, and a missing or empty `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` (Windows ignores them in both; Linux honours them in both, and a missing file gives 77).
- Multiple URLs and `--next` connection reuse with TLS, `%{num_connects}`; http:// to a TLS port (52); https:// to a plain-TCP server (35); `--connect-timeout`/`-m` against a silent TLS server (28); `--proto =https`.

### A.10 ftp-file-tftp

- **Basic FTP download:** the command sequence is byte-exact (USER/PASS/PWD/EPSV/TYPE I/SIZE/RETR/QUIT) on Windows and Linux.
- **`--ftp-method`:** multicwd, singlecwd and nocwd for relative, absolute (`//`), %2F-prefixed, double-slash and deep (6-level) paths.
- **Listings:** directory LIST, NLST (`-l`), `-X 'LIST -la'`, `-X 'NLST -a'`, `;type=d`, and `-l` on a file URL. Byte-exact on Windows; Linux differs only by CRLF (FTP-3).
- **Missing targets:** missing file (78), missing directory with CWD failure (9), nocwd missing (78), SIZE 550 on a directory.
- **Files and credentials:** empty file, 100 KB binary, `%20` names, user:pass via `-u` and URL-encoded in the URL, `-u bob:`, `-u :pw`, a 300-character user.
- **Transfer types:** `;type=a`, `;type=i`, `;type=A`, `;type=x`, `-B`, `--crlf` on download, server-side ASCII conversion (Windows).
- **Passive mode:**: `--disable-epsv` (PASV), `--disable-eprt`, fallback to PASV when EPSV is refused, both refused (13).; Bad 229 reply (13), bad 227 reply (14), PASV port 0, out-of-range octet.; Unreachable or closed data port (7), `--ftp-skip-pasv-ip` on and off.
- **Active mode:**: `-P -`, `-P 127.0.0.1`, ip:port, ip:range, `--ftp-port`.; EPRT refused then PORT, both refused (30).; Active LIST and upload, bad interface (6).
- **Ranges and resume:**: `-r` ranges: open, suffix, beyond the end (36), inverted, multi, 0-0.; `-C` offset, `-C -`, `-C` beyond the end (36) and exact; REST refused (31).; `--max-filesize` with and without SIZE (63), `--ignore-content-length`.
- **Time conditions and `-I`:**: `-z` (newer, older, negative, MDTM failing), `-R` with good and bad MDTM.; `-I` output (Last-Modified/Content-Length/Accept-ranges), `-I` on a missing file (78) and on a directory.
- **Quote commands:**: `-Q` pre, post and prexfer (`+`, `-`), the `*` ignore-failure prefix, a failing quote (21) in every stage.; Multi-line replies, 3xx and 4xx quote replies, lowercase commands, an empty quote (21).; Quote-only URLs, `-I` with quotes, `-X NOOP` (19).
- **Login:**: 530 on USER or PASS (67), 230 on USER.; 332 with and without `--ftp-account`, ACCT 530 (11), `--ftp-alternative-to-user`.; Greeting 500 (8), greeting 421 (28), multi-line greeting, connection closed at greeting (56).
- **PWD:** PWD failing; odd, unquoted, VMS, doubled-quote and multi-line PWD replies; `%{ftp_entry_path}`.
- **Reply handling:** TYPE 504 (17), bad 3-digit code 999 (17), multi-line replies including a wrong terminator, SIZE overflow 2^63-1 (18), SIZE smaller or bigger than the data (18).
- **Transfer failures:**: RETR 550/450/425, 226 replaced by 451 or 550 (18), 125 preliminary reply.; Control connection closed at SIZE/PASS/RETR/226 (56), data connection hang (18).; Exit codes for `-m` and `--connect-timeout` timeouts (28).
- **Uploads:**: `-T` to a directory and to a named file, in multicwd, singlecwd and nocwd.; `--ftp-create-dirs` in all methods, including MKD failure (9).; `--append` (new and existing file), `--crlf` (LF and mixed), `-B` and `;type=a` upload.; `-C N` and `-C -` upload, including a new file and a smaller remote file.; stdin (`-` and `.`), a missing local file (26).; STOR 553/452 (25), APPE 550 (25), 226 failure (18).; Upload glob, empty file, `-I -T` (2), `--ftp-pret` (84).
- **Multiple URLs and retries:**: Several URLs on one connection: same directory, different directory, different user, `--next`, a failing first URL, `--fail-early`.; Globs `[1-2]` with `-o #1`, `-O`.; `--retry` on 450/550/421, `--skip-existing`, `--path-as-is`, `--limit-rate`, `--create-file-mode`.
- **FTPS:**: `--ftp-ssl-control`, AUTH refused with `--ssl-reqd` (64), `--ssl` (plain fallback), PROT refused (64).; Certificate not trusted (60), explicit and implicit.; With a server that starts data TLS at accept time: download, listing, implicit `ftps://` and `--ftp-ssl-ccc`. Linux upload also matches; Windows upload does not (FTP-2).
- **Wildcard-looking URLs:** the curl CLI has no wildcard matching, so both sides send SIZE/RETR of the literal name (78). A bad `[12]` range gives 3 on both.
- **file:// (general):**: Host forms: plain, localhost, 127.0.0.1, other host (3); missing file (37).; Directory listing with and without a trailing slash; `-I`/`-i` (body also written).; Ranges, including beyond the end (36) and inverted (33); `-C` beyond the end (36).; Escapes `%2520`, `%6C`, `%23`; raw `#`; a query string; `%00` (3).; `-T` to a new file, a directory, with append, `-C` and `--crlf`, to a missing directory (23), with `--create-dirs` (23).; `-o`/`-O`, `-w` variables, `-z`, `-R`, `--max-filesize` (63), two URLs, a glob, `..` and `%2e%2e`.; URL forms: `file:` with no slashes (3), `file:/`, `file:////`, `file://` (3), `file:///`.; `-X`/`-d`/`-H` ignored, `-f`, `-I -d` (2).
- **file:// on Windows:** drive letter with and without a leading slash, backslashes, `C|` (37), UNC localhost, `C$` share (37), NUL, CON (37), a directory, the `C:/` root, lowercase drive, ADS (37), trailing dot, pagefile (37), long path (37).
- **file:// on Linux:** `/etc/hostname`, `/dev/null`, `/dev/` (listing), `/etc/shadow` (37), `/sys` (37), the `/proc/self/` directory, `-T` to `/dev/null`, the `file:///` root listing.
- **TFTP:**: Downloads: basic, `//abs`, subdirectory, 100 KB, an exact multiple of 512, empty file (71), missing file (68).; blksize 8, 7, 512, 1024, 65464 and 65465; server OACK smaller, bigger (71) or absent; `--tftp-no-options` with and without blksize.; Error codes 0-9 (69/70/71/72/73/74/42/71/42).; Uploads: small, 3000 bytes, with blksize, with no options, to `/`.; Modes: netascii, octet, bad mode (68).; `-I` (8), `-w` variables including num_connects, range, resume, no path (71), `%20`, `-u`, server timeout (28).; RRQ option bytes are identical.
