### A.18 libcurl-multi-callbacks

- **Harness:** 69 cases, each run twice on Windows (REF 8.22.0 `libcurl-4.dll` vs PORT `Libcurl.dll`) and once on Linux (REF 8.18.0 vs PORT), against the loopback servers on 21700 and 21701.
- **Basic multi loop:** perform + poll with 200, 404 and refused handles. CURLMSG_DONE results 0/0/7, msgs_in_queue 2,1,0, info_read NULL after the queue is drained, and the response codes and bodies all match.
- **Message order:** info_read order follows completion order.
- **DONE results for bad input:** unsupported scheme 1, missing URL 3, malformed URL 3, unresolvable host 6.
- **Handle bookkeeping:**: perform on an empty multi;; curl_multi_timeout: -1, then 0 after add, then -1 after done and after remove;; adding the same handle twice (7), and adding it to a second multi (7);; removing a handle that was never added (0), and removing from the wrong multi (2).
- **Removing handles:**: remove_handle mid-transfer: no more write calls and no message. Re-adding starts a fresh request on a new connection.; Removing after done without reading the message, then re-adding: no stale message, and the connection is reused.
- **Connection limits and reuse:**: MAX_HOST_CONNECTIONS=1 and =2: queueing and reuse.; Unlimited parallelism.; MAXCONNECTS 0, 1 and 2: connection counts.; Reuse between easy handles in one multi.; FORBID_REUSE, FRESH_CONNECT, `Connection: close` and HTTP/1.0 responses.
- **Timeouts:** a per-handle TIMEOUT_MS inside a multi gives 28.
- **Cleanup with attached handles:**: curl_multi_cleanup with handles still attached returns 0, and the handles can be used again afterwards.; curl_easy_cleanup of an attached handle, then perform on the multi.
- **Wait, poll and wakeup:**: wait and poll on an empty multi;; wakeup before poll, double wakeup, and wakeup from another thread;; negative timeouts (10);; poll during an idle in-flight transfer.
- **curl_multi_assign:** unknown sockets give BAD_SOCKET; socketp is passed back in CURL_POLL_REMOVE.
- **Pausing from callbacks:**: CURL_WRITEFUNC_PAUSE from the write or header callback, then unpause: the data is re-delivered with nothing lost or duplicated.; CURL_READFUNC_PAUSE, then unpause: the upload bytes on the wire are identical.; pause and unpause from XFERINFOFUNCTION during curl_easy_perform.
- **PREREQFUNCTION:**: the values passed match;; an abort gives 42 and no request is sent;; it is called once per redirect hop and once per perform;; return values 2, -1 and 0x10000001 all abort.
- **RESOLVER_START:** return values 1, -1 and 2 abort with 42 for host names not seen before.
- **OPENSOCKETFUNCTION:** a socket the application creates without connecting works. CURLSOCKTYPE, the address fields and the close-callback counts match.
- **TRAILERFUNCTION:**: wire bytes match for chunked PUT, POST, HTTP/1.0, an entry with no colon, an empty list, and use in a multi;; with a non-chunked body it is not called;; an abort gives 42.
- **HSTSREADFUNCTION and HSTSWRITEFUNCTION:**: upgrade to https;; an expired entry;; CURLSTS_FAIL gives 42;; includeSubDomains;; HSTS_CTRL off;; write at cleanup with index and total;; write returning DONE or FAIL.
- **HEADERFUNCTION:**: ordering across a 301 -> 302 -> 200 redirect chain with chunked trailers, with follow on and off;; 103 Early Hints and 100-continue;; a short return gives 23.
- **XFERINFOFUNCTION:**: first and last tuples, totals and monotonicity for downloads, chunked bodies, uploads, PUT, HEAD, redirects and multi transfers;; return values 1 and -1 abort with 42;; it is not called when NOPROGRESS has its default value.
- **Callback aborts inside a multi:** prereq 42, xferinfo 42, write returning 0 gives 23, header returning 0 gives 23, READFUNC_ABORT 42.
- **Other calls inside callbacks:** setopt and getinfo; curl_easy_perform of an unrelated handle (0 on both).
- **Linux:** the same set of differences reproduced, and all matching cases matched.

### A.19 doh-ipfs-resolution

- DoH request bytes: POST, Host, `Accept: */*`, `Content-Type: application/dns-message`, Content-Length 26 and no User-Agent. Query ID 0, RD flag, QD=1 and no EDNS. The A/AAAA wire format is identical byte for byte.
- Number of queries: A+AAAA by default, A only with -4 and AAAA only with -6, on two separate connections in both binaries.
- A made-up name resolves to 127.0.0.1 / ::1. %{remote_ip}, %{num_connects}, %{remote_port}, %{local_ip}, %{url_effective} and %{http_code} match.
- An AAAA-only answer with -4 and an A-only answer with -6 exit 6 in both.
- CNAME chains of 1/3/4/5 hops, CNAME to AAAA, a dangling CNAME and a CNAME loop.
- NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, NOERROR with no answer, and NXDOMAIN with SOA authority: exit 6 and "Could not resolve host" in both.
- TTL 0 with two URLs, and --dns-cache-timeout 0.
- Malformed answers: truncated, garbage, empty body, header only, wrong ID, QDCOUNT 0, inflated ANCOUNT, TC bit, QR=0, wrong question name, PTR type, short A/AAAA rdata, wrong type, short RR, class CH, name compression pointer, out-of-range pointer, authority SOA, OPT additional record. The decode-error trace texts match.
- Up to 40 A records, 30 AAAA records, and an answer of more than 3000 bytes (exit 6 in both).
- DoH HTTP status 404/500/301 (with -L), Content-Type variants, chunked response, gzip Content-Encoding (6 in both), a connection closed without a reply, server not listening, a hanging server (exit 28).
- HTTPS DoH: a self-signed certificate with no options (6), -k alone (6), --doh-insecure (0), --cacert (6 without --ssl-no-revoke, 0 with it), --capath, --pinnedpubkey not applied to DoH, the wrong IP name, TLS against a plain server and the reverse, --tlsv1.3 with --tls-max 1.2. On Linux --cacert works and --doh-cert-status fails in both.
- --resolve and its wildcard take priority over DoH, '-host' removal, --resolve for another port, --connect-to to an IP or name (the name resolved by DoH), --connect-to not applied to the DoH server.
- IP-literal URLs (v4, v6, decimal, short form) and localhost / LOCALHOST / *.localhost skip DoH.
- Upper-case names, a trailing-dot name, a 63-character label, a 250-character name, IDN (punycode), underscore, a numeric TLD.
- -x HTTP proxy (DoH is not sent through it), a proxy name resolved by DoH, a DoH server named through -x, --noproxy, --noproxy '*', the http_proxy env with no no_proxy, SOCKS proxies (exit 7 in both).
- -A, -H, -u, -b, -e, --compressed and -0 do not reach the DoH request.
- DoH URL variants: with a query, without a path, with a fragment, an IPv6 literal, a localhost host, ftp scheme (6), empty --doh-url, bad port, `http://` with no host, the last of two --doh-url options wins, doh-url in -K config, --libcurl output.
- Redirects: to a second name (a second DoH lookup), to an NXDOMAIN name, to the same host, to an IP literal. --doh-url per --next group, two hosts, URL globbing, a wss target through DoH.
- IPFS gateway forms: plain, trailing slash, path, deep path, /ipfs/ path, query (3), empty query, fragment, userinfo, no scheme, https, [::1] (3), localhost, a DoH-resolved gateway, ftp, file (3), malformed (43), empty (2), unknown scheme (43), percent-encoded path, refused port (7).
- IPFS URL forms: ipns, ipns with path and query, CID with sub-path, query with a space (3), fragment, trailing slash, query only (3), empty query, upper-case scheme and CID, empty CID (3), CID with port or userinfo, %20 %2F %41 path, space (3), dot segments, --path-as-is, UTF-8 percent-encoded path, %01 (3), dotted / IPv4 / IPv6 CID, globbing, two URLs, -v, -O (exit 1 with the same message), --proto =http/=ipfs/=https, -d POST, -x, -L, --next groups, --url, and the rewritten request line and Host.
- IPFS gateway sources: IPFS_GATEWAY (with path, empty, no scheme, query, bad, leading space), --ipfs-gateway takes priority over the env, the env takes priority over the file, ~/.ipfs/gateway with LF / CRLF / several lines / an empty first line (37) / no scheme / a path / spaces / a BOM / no newline, no gateway (37), IPFS_PATH with and without a trailing slash and with forward slashes, IPFS_PATH with no file (37), HOME only, USERPROFILE only (37), HOME unset, CURL_HOME not used, ipfs-gateway in -K config.
- Linux subset over HTTPS DoH (REF-LINUX 8.18 vs PORT-LINUX): basic, -4, CNAME, NX, SERVFAIL, TTL0, all 15 malformations, 404, text/plain, close, --resolve, --connect-to, IP literal, -x, redirect, --next, --doh-insecure / self-signed / -k, IPFS gateway, env, file, IPFS_PATH and errors all match except the findings above.

### A.20 tls-protocols-revocation

- Harness and server: Windows `E\h.ps1`, Linux `E\linux\lh.sh`, server `E\srv\Program.cs` (tsrv: smtp, imap, pop3, ftp, gopher, mqtt, ws, ldap, http, proxy, crl; implicit TLS or STARTTLS; it logs every client line and whether it arrived inside TLS). About 350 differential runs (b1-b9 on Windows, l1-l4 on Linux), plus the verifier re-runs `E\v.ps1` and `E\linux\lv.sh`.
- Implicit TLS on Windows and Linux: smtps upload, AUTH and VRFY; imaps fetch, list and APPEND; pop3s retr and list; each with `-k` and with `--cacert` (+ `--ssl-no-revoke`).
- STARTTLS success for SMTP, IMAP and POP3 (`--ssl-reqd` and `--ssl`), including a server that advertises AUTH only after TLS, and IMAP LOGINDISABLED. Capabilities are asked again after the upgrade. No plaintext is pipelined after STARTTLS/STLS, and every later command goes inside TLS. Windows and Linux.
- FTPS implicit and explicit (AUTH SSL first in both): passive RETR, LIST, two files on implicit `ftps://`, PASV fallback (`--disable-epsv` is ignored over IPv6 in both); active mode `-P` with PROT P for RETR, LIST, STOR, APPE, a 300 KB upload, stdin upload and `-P -` (Linux, and TLS 1.2 on Windows); `--ftp-ssl-control` with a clear data channel; CCC refused by the server; single-URL CCC (81 on Windows in both; works on Linux in both, including `--ftp-ssl-ccc-mode active`, STOR and active).
- FTPS data-channel session reuse (vsftpd require_ssl_reuse emulation, `E\linux\ftpsreuse.py`; on Windows judged from the handshake byte count): the data channel resumes the control session in both, for TLS 1.2 and 1.3, passive and active, RETR, LIST and STOR.
- gophers:// (`-k`, `--cacert`, no CA gives 60), mqtts:// subscribe and publish, and wss:// on Windows; gophers, wss and ldaps (`-k`, `--cacert`, no CA) on Linux.
- CRL distribution point on Windows: good certificate with default and best-effort checking (0); revoked certificate with `--ssl-no-revoke` and `-k` (0); unreachable CDP (default 60 "revocation status is unknown", best-effort 0, no-revoke 0); no CDP (default 60, best-effort 0); `--crlfile` ignored on Windows by both; `%{ssl_verify_result}` for good and dead CDPs.
- Linux `--crlfile`: good 0; revoked 60 with identical text; `-k` 0; no CRL 0; DER CRL 82; missing file 2; garbage 82; expired CRL 60; a combined CA+CRL file; a CA certificate given as CRL 82; a certificate without CDP; `--ssl-revoke-best-effort`.
- OCSP stapling on Linux with `--cert-status` and `--cacert`: good 0; revoked 91 `SSL certificate revocation reason: keyCompromise (1)`; no staple 91; staple for another certificate 91; TLS 1.2 variants; two URLs; `%{ssl_verify_result}`. On Windows `--cert-status` is ignored by both, and a staple for another certificate gives 60 in both.
- Online OCSP via AIA on Windows: both report "revocation status is unknown" (60), and best-effort gives 0, for good and revoked certificates (see Not tested).
- TLS session resumption with identical options: two URLs, three URLs, `--next`, globbing, `--no-sessionid` (New/New), different hosts (localhost and 127.0.0.1 not shared), a `--tls-max` change, `--cacert` both times, TLS 1.2 and 1.3, Windows and Linux; HTTPS close-delimited connections, SMTPS `--next` and POP3 STARTTLS `--next`. Verification on a resumed session still fails correctly for untrusted, self-signed, wrong-host and expired certificates and bad pins.
- `--ssl-sessions` on Windows: exit 2 in both (neither build has SSLS-EXPORT).
- Server-initiated TLS 1.2 renegotiation (HelloRequest) with GET, POST and two URLs (Windows and Linux), and with a client certificate (Linux); TLS 1.3 post-handshake auth with a client certificate (Linux).
- Missing close_notify at the end of a close-delimited HTTPS body: exit 56 in both, TLS 1.2 and 1.3, `-0`, `-w`; close_notify present gives 0; TCP RST gives 56; close_notify without FIN gives 0.
- HTTPS proxy: `--proxy-pinnedpubkey` sha256 match, file PEM/DER match, bad pin 90, together with a target `--pinnedpubkey` (Windows and Linux); a proxy client certificate (PEM, P12, encrypted key with `--proxy-pass`) presented to the proxy on Linux; Windows PEM proxy certificate 58 in both; Windows P12 proxy certificate over TLS 1.2 gives 0 in both. (Windows P12 over TLS 1.3, REF 35 vs PORT 0, is the same as TLS-10 on the proxy path.)
- FTPS active-mode upload over TLS 1.2 on Windows against the strict server, and over TLS 1.3 on Linux (controls for TPR-05).
- `--disable-eprt` with an IPv4 control connection, and `-P ::1` on `[::1]` (controls for TPR-06).

- -Z with several bodies to stdout: body order and whole-body writes, with no byte interleaving, for 40 B and 300 kB trickled bodies (Win)
- -Z -w with %{urlnum} %{url} %{url_effective} %{exitcode} %{http_code} %{num_connects} %{filename_effective}, and the order of out-of-order completions with --parallel-immediate (Win)
- -w %{stderr}/%{stdout} switching under -Z (Win)
- %{onerror} with -Z, with and without -f, and with %{errormsg} (Win)
- The exit code chosen when several -Z transfers fail with different codes (7/22/18/28/1/3/37, in various orders and timings) (Win)
- 'curl: (N)' error lines for each failing transfer, serial and -Z with -sS, including their order across 7/22/18 (Win)
- --fail-with-body under -Z, with and without --fail-early, and with files and --remove-on-error (Win)
- --fail-early in serial mode, and --fail-early with --parallel-max 1 (Win)
- --retry, --retry-delay and --retry-connrefused inside -Z: request counts, %{num_retries} and error lines (Win). Retry timing was not compared.
- --parallel-max 0/1/2/3 and --parallel-max-host 1: the number of concurrent connections recorded by the server (Win)
- --rate 2/s with 5 URLs in serial mode (one request about every 500 ms), --rate being ignored under -Z, and --rate 30/m and 4/s with slow responses (Win)
- -o with #1/#2 globs, -O with globs, mixed -o/-O, fewer and more -o than URLs, -o with --create-dirs into the same new directory, and --output-dir --create-dirs (Win)
- --skip-existing outputs and notes (apart from PMT-8), and --no-clobber .N naming with existing files and with same-name transfers in one run at different delays (Win)
- --remove-on-error with -f, with a truncated body (18) and with -m 1, serial and -Z (Win)
- -T glob uploads under -Z, a -T glob with several URLs, two -T groups, -T - and -T . with several URLs, -T - with a URL glob, and -d @- and --data-binary @- shared between URLs in one group, serial and -Z (Win)
- --next groups under -Z keep their own -w/-X/-H/-d/-o, -Z given only in a later group, and failure codes across groups (Win)

## Appendix B. Not tested and limitations

### B.0 Limitations that apply to the whole review

- **REF-LINUX is curl 8.18.0, not the 8.22.0 target.** Every Linux-only difference was judged against an older curl. Differences where Windows REF 8.22.0 agrees with the port were treated as 8.18-vs-8.22 version changes and not reported; Linux-only findings that could depend on the curl version are marked Probable. A Linux build of curl 8.22.0 was not available.
- **The Windows REF has no HTTP/2 or HTTP/3** (built without nghttp2/ngtcp2; see GF-0098, GF-0099, GF-0031, GF-0032). HTTP/2 behaviour was compared only against REF-LINUX 8.18.0 (http2-linux area); HTTP/3 was not compared at all. On Windows only accepted-vs-refused for the HTTP/2/3 options was compared.
- **The Windows REF is a Debug build.** Its extra debug lines (`sendrecv_dl`, schannel step lines, `{ [0 bytes data]`, assertion lines) were normalised away, so Windows `-v`/`--trace` output was compared only for lines that a release build also prints. A few REF Debug-build assertions (for example `-J` with filename `""`, `.` or `..`) were not reported.
- **The Windows REF is a non-UNICODE (ANSI argv) build.** Non-ASCII command-line handling differs between ANSI and UNICODE curl builds; the issues that depend on this say so. Only code page 1252 was available.
- **Other optional features missing from the reference builds:** no c-ares (`--dns-*` options), no ECH, no SSLS-EXPORT on REF-LINUX, no mqtts on REF-LINUX, no `--knownhosts` on REF-LINUX 8.18. For these only acceptance or refusal could be compared.
- **Loopback only.** No traffic left the machine, so there are no tests against real DNS, real internet servers, real OCSP/CRL infrastructure, real FTP servers (vsftpd/proftpd), a real LDAP server, a KDC (Kerberos/Negotiate/GSSAPI), or ssh-agent/Pageant. Stand-in servers emulate the relevant behaviour (for example vsftpd's data-TLS ordering and strict EOF).
- **No interactive console.** Password prompts, passphrase prompts, the progress bar on a real TTY, Ctrl+C on Windows, `--styled-output` styling and the binary-output warning on a Windows console were not tested. Linux TTY behaviour was tested through `script(1)` only.
- **Windows disk-full (ENOSPC)** was not testable without admin rights; it was tested on Linux with `/dev/full` only.
- **macOS** was not tested.
- **The libcurl port has no C exports.** Libcurl behaviour was compared by driving REF `libcurl-4.dll`/`libcurl.so.4` through P/Invoke and the port's `Libcurl.dll` through its C# API from the same probe process, not by linking a C program against the port.
- **Out of scope by instruction:** speed, throughput, memory use, binary size and start-up time. Timing values (speed columns, `time_*` jitter, retry-delay timing) were normalised; only constant-zero timing values that indicate missing data were reported.
- **Evidence location.** All repro scripts, servers and captured outputs are in the review scratchpad (`SCR\evidence\<area>\`), which is a temporary folder.
- **Some test-run hygiene notes:** two testers once ran a broad `taskkill /IM server.exe` / `taskkill /IM python.exe`; results from around that time could include connection-refused artefacts in other areas. Every reported issue was re-run afterwards by a verifier.

### B.1 cli-options

- Interactive console behaviour (typing at the password prompt, the progress bar on a real TTY).
- Whether PORT actually uses `--dns-servers` and the related options for resolution (this needs a loopback DNS server).
- The behaviour of HTTP/2, ECH and c-ares (no REF build with those features was available; only accepted-vs-refused was compared).
- Linux against REF 8.22.0 (only 8.18.0 was available).
- The default `.curlrc` lookup and environment-driven options.
- Huge `--retry-delay`/`--retry-max-time` during an actual retry wait.
- Network semantics beyond option acceptance (proxies, SOCKS, TLS, FTP, SSH, mail).

### B.2 config-glob-output

- _curlrc next to the executable (the Windows exe-directory lookup). It was not safe to write there: REF is under Program Files and the PORT bin directory is shared.
- Config lines over 10 MB, already covered by GF-0069.
- Disk-full (ENOSPC) on Windows. It was tested only on Linux via /dev/full, which is why CGO-09 is Probable.
- Huge globs (millions of URLs) run to completion.
- `-K -` from an interactive console. Only pipes were tested.
- -T globs and double reads of upload stdin, beyond a quick check. Upload belongs to another area.
- REF 8.22's debug assertion for -J filename `""`, `.` or `..`. It is a REF defect, not reported.
- The different message for `-o CONIN$` (same exit code, a device-name edge case). Not reported.
- macOS.

### B.3 url-parsing

- **Very long command lines:** Windows command lines over about 32 k characters cannot be passed (the CreateProcess limit), so long URLs were tested only through `-K`.
- **FTP/SFTP/SCP paths on the wire:** CWD splitting, `;type=` and %2F were not tested. They are covered by the ftp area, and only the error paths were compared here.
- **HTTPS end to end:** there was no TLS server, so only connect failures were compared.
- **Real DNS resolution of IDN hosts:** IDN was compared through the Host header with `--connect-to`.
- **Real link-local scope ids:** no interface with fe80:: addresses was used.
- **Windows IDN from percent-decoded or config-file bytes:** the Windows REF passes these to libidn2 as CP1252 and produces mojibake punycode, so these cases were not reported.
- **Linux-only differences caused by REF-LINUX being 8.18:** these were ignored, for example `127.0.0.1 port N` against `127.0.0.1:N`, `disabled` against `is disabled`, and lower-case path escapes.
- **General --globoff/glob-range semantics:** these belong to another area.

### B.4 http-requests

- **HTTPS/TLS request construction:** out of scope for the plain-loopback harness.
- **HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 framing:** the Windows REF has no HTTP/2. This is the known GF-0098/GF-0099.
- **Byte-level chunk boundaries for piped stdin uploads over 64 KB:** they depend on pipe read timing.
- **Linux differences that follow the 8.18.0 vs 8.22.0 version gap:**: query escape case (also seen in this verification as `--url-query q=é`, where REF-LINUX sends `%c3%a9` and the port sends `%C3%A9`); `-u :`, `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked`, -H @file keeping CR, and some error-text wording In each case the port matches Windows REF 8.22.0.
- **Real 100-continue servers that send 100 Continue before the body:** the timing was not compared.
- **Very large headers and header-count limits:** already filed as GF-0075.
- **stdin from a file redirect or a console:** only piped stdin was tested.
- **ANSI code pages other than cp1252:** only cp1252 was available.

### B.5 http-responses

- Binary-output-to-terminal warning on Windows: the harness redirects stdout and has no ConPTY, so this was tested only on Linux, through script(1).
- -J with `filename=""`, `"."` or `".."` on Windows: the REF is a debug build and asserts (`fname && *fname`, tool_cb_wrt.c:45). PORT omits the `Warning: Failed to open the file` line, but release-REF behaviour cannot be shown here. On Linux (release REF 8.18) both match.
- HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 responses, and h2c 101 upgrades: the Windows REF is built without nghttp2 (see GF-0098).
- zstd frames with a content checksum, and brotli/zstd dictionary or windowing extremes: the .NET encoder used for the fixtures does not produce them.
- Content-Length or chunk sizes actually transferred in multi-GB volumes: only declared sizes were tested.
- Verbose (-v) output: compared only for a few cases, because the REF debug build adds lines that were filtered out.
- Windows file names are case-insensitive, so the basic_I.bin fixture overwrote basic_i.bin. This has no effect on the Windows results; the Linux basic_i run used the I fixture for both binaries.

### B.6 http-stateful

- `-u user` with no password: REF prompts on the console (not on stdin), so the prompt path cannot be compared.
- --negotiate/Kerberos and proxy auth (--proxy-*, CONNECT): outside this area, and no KDC or proxy was available.
- HSTS upgrades that actually connect: the upgraded URL hit a plain-text port and both builds exit 35. STS parsing and saving were tested on TLS port 20502 instead.
- Alt-Svc switching to a real h2/h3 alternative: no h2/h3 server was available. Only the file round trip and header parsing were compared.
- Windows SHA-256/SHA-512-256 Digest correctness: the SSPI REF refuses with exit 94, as PORT does, so these were checked only on Linux.
- Digest non-ASCII username percent-encoding against a native-digest curl 8.22: only REF-LINUX 8.18 and the Windows SSPI REF were available.
- Linux-only differences that depend on the curl version were not reported. These are cases where REF-LINUX 8.18 differs from 8.22 and Windows REF 8.22 matches PORT: the connect error text; -b cookie strings sent to another host; Location userinfo credentials without -H Authorization; `-u ':'`; the file:// error text; -z before 1970; some sigv4 canonical forms; STS max-age overflow; `--etag-save -` exit 23; `* closing connection #-1`; the Canonical-request verbose line
- Linux netrc with non-ASCII bytes was not judged either, because REF-LINUX 8.18 itself truncates or rejects such files.
- The Linux progress meter: the Linux runner has no meter normaliser, so the meter was compared on Windows only.
- Not reported, by rule: differences only in timing values, progress speed columns, a 1-second drift in expiry times, or TLS ClientHello bytes.

### B.7 proxy-connect

- --proxy-negotiate / SPNEGO and real SOCKS5 GSSAPI negotiation: these need a KDC, so only method selection was compared.
- --proxy-http2 / HTTP/2 proxies: the Windows REF build has no HTTP2 feature, and they were not compared on Linux.
- Proxy client certificates, --proxy-pinnedpubkey, --proxy-cacert content checks and --proxy-tlsv1.x/ciphers: left to the TLS area.
- Exit 5 from a real DNS failure of the proxy name: it was checked only through bad ports and port-less forms (plus the incidental cases n11 and d05).
- --dns-servers behaviour itself: neither REF build has c-ares.
- --interface by device name on Windows: only if!name was tested (plus `lo` on Linux).
- IPv6 link-local connects through a real zone: only the bytes sent to the proxy were compared.
- -U with a user and no password (interactive prompt): not scriptable.
- --local-port with the same port in back-to-back runs: Windows TIME_WAIT makes the second run fail in both curls.
- Linux-only text differences where REF-LINUX 8.18 is older than the 8.22.0 target and Windows 8.22.0 agrees with the port, not reported: "Establish" vs "Establishing HTTP proxy tunnel", the "Connecting to hostname/port" lines, proxy-refused wording, unix-socket error wording, --haproxy-clientip IPv6 over IPv4, -6 with an IPv4 literal, the --interface if! error text, and the SOCKS4 IPv6-resolve message.
- TLS handshake verbose lines and TLS failure messages: they belong to the TLS area.

### B.8 writeout-verbose

- **Needs a real terminal:**: `--styled-output` styling (bold header names, OSC-8 hyperlinks).; The "Binary output can mess up your terminal" warning.
- **Exit codes not reached:**: 4, 5 and 6 on Windows: resolving names would send DNS traffic off loopback.; 10, 11 and 12: FTP active-mode accept.; 15, 16 and 92: the REF build has no HTTP/2.; 27, 34, 42, 43, 51, 53, 54, 55, 65, 66, 69-75, 79, 80, 81, 83, 88, 91, 94, 95, 96, 98 and 99.
- **Windows REF debug-build lines:** These were normalised away: `sendrecv_dl`, `Curl_xfer_send`, `PSL check`, schannel step lines, `{ [0 bytes data]`, and the `--trace-config` read/write internals. The `--trace-config all` internals are only roughly comparable.
- **Timing-dependent output:**: Speed values in the progress meter and timing-dependent update counts.; The body bytes written before a `-Y`/`-y` abort, which is a race.
- **HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 -v output:** not supported by the REF build (see GF-0099).
- **Operational note:** The original tester ran `taskkill /IM server.exe` and `taskkill /IM python.exe` early in the run. Other agents' loopback servers may have been killed, so their results from around that time may show connection-refused artefacts.

### B.9 tls

- Windows `-v` output in general. REF 8.22.0 is a debug build, so only lines also seen in a release Schannel build are reported.
- FTP active mode (`-P`/EPRT) with TLS, and FTPS uploads to a STOR-capable server. The stand-in server lacks PORT/STOR; a PROT P upload to it also hung in PORT, where REF exited 25.
- Client certificates from the Windows certificate store with a real installed certificate (not imported, to avoid changing the machine).
- OCSP stapling with a real stapled response, and CRL-based revocation (a CRL distribution point, or `--crlfile` with a CRL that revokes the server certificate).
- HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 over TLS (the Windows REF lacks both: GF-0099, GF-0031, GF-0032).
- Linux `--ssl-revoke-*` and `--ca-native` semantics beyond the basic case; SSLKEYLOGFILE (covered by GF-0084).
- Interactive tty passphrase entry; only the no-tty case was compared.
- Linux results are against REF-LINUX 8.18.0, older than the 8.22.0 target, so Linux-only findings are Probable.

### B.10 ftp-file-tftp

- **FTP wildcard matching (CURLOPT_WILDCARDMATCH):** the curl CLI has no option for it.
- **Real FTP servers:** no vsftpd, proftpd or pure-ftpd (none installed, no internet). The stub emulates vsftpd's ordering of data TLS after RETR; its eager-TLS mode shows PORT works when the server handshakes at accept time.
- **FTPS on Linux:** nothing beyond `EV\wsl3.sh` / `EV\vl.sh`. OpenSSL vs Schannel handshake message text was not compared (TLS area).
- **Verbose Schannel trace lines and ClientHello versions:** PORT prints fewer `* schannel:` lines and also offers TLS 1.0/1.1. Left to the TLS area.
- **TFTP edge packets:** duplicate or out-of-order DATA, wrong TID, OACK with unknown options, error mid-transfer. The stub has no knobs for these.
- **TFTP two-URL log order:** the difference is in the order of the multithreaded stub's log lines, not on the wire, so it is not reported.
- **Linux-only message differences:** errno text, the `Failed to connect` format and the range-error wording match on Windows 8.22. They are treated as 8.18 version differences.
- **`--ftp-ssl-ccc` with a server that accepts CCC:** the stub refuses CCC.
- **FTP over IPv6 control connections:** the stub listens on IPv4 only.
- **Remaining b14 items on Linux after the time cap:** their Windows counterparts matched.
- **Speed and timing values:** normalised as the rules require. Only the constant-zero `time_*` values are reported (FTP-9).

### B.11 other-protocols

- **TLS:** smtps, pop3s, imaps, gophers, mqtts and wss, and a successful STARTTLS upgrade. These need a TLS loopback server and Schannel trust setup. Only refusals and plain-text `--ssl`/`--ssl-reqd` were tested.
- **SASL challenge-response:** full NTLM, GSSAPI/Kerberos and SSPI-DIGEST exchanges. DIGEST-MD5 was checked for structure only, because the cnonce is random.
- **LDAP:** anonymous WinLDAP NTLM/Negotiate bind against a server that sends a real challenge; LDAPS; paged or referral results.
- **RTSP:** interleaved RTP, and RTSP-specific libcurl options (the tool has no options for them).
- **`-v` / `--trace` comparisons:** the Windows REF is a debug build, which adds debug lines and interleaves the progress output differently.
- **Non-deterministic cases:**: DICT `-I`: both clients close immediately, so what the server records depends on timing.; The Windows MQTT case killed after a timeout (m36): REF loses its buffered stdout when killed.; Parallel (`-Z`) connection counts for POP3 depend on timing.
- **IMAP `-X 'APPEND x'` with `-T`:** REF itself hangs, so this is a REF fault and was not reported.
- **Partial coverage:** glob cases with Windows paths were not repeated on Linux. The TELNET race on Linux was run only with t17 (20 runs by the tester) and the 410 KB upload (7 runs by the verifier); no SB split was seen on Linux.

### B.12 network-robustness

- Disk-full on Windows: no full volume was available without admin rights. ENOSPC was tested on Linux only, with /dev/full.
- `--connect-timeout` against a host that drops SYNs: the rules allow loopback only, and a loopback connect is refused at once.
- `--keepalive-time` on the wire: there was no packet capture. Only option parsing was compared.
- Real console Ctrl+C on Windows: msys `timeout -s INT` does not deliver one. Only the TERM kill was compared.
- `-v`/`--trace` stderr byte comparison on Windows: the REF build adds extra debug lines.
- Parallel connection counts outside the deterministic NR-7 case depend on timing and were treated as normalised.
- NR-8 and NR-9 on Linux: a closed fd 0 is reused by the socket, so both binaries hang.
- Linux `(7) Failed to connect` wording: an 8.18 vs 8.22 difference (Windows 8.22 matches the port), so it is not reported.
- Note: the original tester once used a broad `taskkill /IM server.exe`, which may have ended other agents' servers. The verifier stopped its own server by PID only.

### B.13 environment

- **TTY detection and the binary-output warning on a real Windows console:** there is no pty harness on Windows. This was tested on Linux only, through `script(1)`.
- **The getpwuid fallback for .netrc/.curlrc on Linux when HOME is unset:** testing it would mean changing the real WSL user's home directory.
- **HTTPS through an environment proxy all the way through a CONNECT tunnel:** the stand-in proxy refuses CONNECT, so only the CONNECT request and the failure path were compared.
- **SSLKEYLOGFILE on Windows Schannel** beyond "neither writes a file" (REF's Schannel build has no keylog support).
- **Unicode console output encoding (chcp 65001 and other code pages) on a real console:** all Windows runs used redirected pipes.
- **Symlink and junction targets for `-o` on Windows:** creating them needs Developer Mode or admin rights.
- **Verbose TLS handshake trace differences on Linux:** missing `TLSv1.3 (OUT)` lines, and `[blank] / UNDEF` in the "SSL connection using" line. These were seen but left to the TLS area.

### B.14 upstream-cases

- Upstream cases that use `<tool>` (229 libtest programs): there is no real-binary equivalent.
- Servers not emulated: SFTP/SCP, MQTT, TFTP, RTSP, DICT, Gopher, LDAP, SMB, WS, HTTPS/FTPS/IMAPS (TLS), http-ipv6 and socks proxies. Telnet was checked by hand only.
- FTP active mode (-P) from Windows: only the 425 path was run on Windows. The other active-mode replays ran on Linux only.
- Cases with `<servercmd>` directives beyond REPLY, `%SRCDIR`/`%PWD`/`%AMP` variables, or complex `%if` expressions: skipped by the replayer.
- Debug-feature cases (CURL_ALTSVC_HTTP, CURL_UPLOAD_SIZE, fake -w values): excluded.
- HTTP/3 cases (2500-2503): REF-WIN has no HTTP/3.
- Linux-only differences that match 8.18-vs-8.22 changes: not reported, because REF-LINUX is older than the target.
- The test1211 accept-timeout path (exit 28 after about 60 s): not run.
- The test1714 replay through WSL interop and the test2114 / test94 progress-meter variants: not re-run by the verifier.
- Ratchet coverage gaps, which are not exercised on Windows and may hide differences: Skipped for a missing feature:; TrackMemory: test96, test558; Unicode: test472 (this hides UC-4), test1703; OpenSSL: test307, test1587; getrlimit: test518, test537; needs no threaded resolver: test506; internet access: test2043; 23 upstream unit programs with no port (unit1300 to unit3306).; 44 listed "passing" cases that run only on another platform. These include test469 and test1714, and replaying them by hand on Windows turned up UC-5 and UC-10.

### B.15 libcurl-api

- A real libcurl 8.22.0 OpenSSL build on Linux (REF-LINUX is 8.18.0).
- Driving the curl_multi interface (perform, poll, socket_action, timer callbacks, PUSHFUNCTION, NOTIFYFUNCTION) beyond setopt and the add/remove codes.
- TLS options at runtime (certificates, pinning, CA blobs, SSL_CTX_FUNCTION, SSLS export/import). These are left to the tls area.
- Non-HTTP protocols through the Libcurl API. UPLOAD_FLAGS was checked only at setopt level.
- Proxy options at runtime (left to the proxy-connect area).
- HSTS callbacks and file; the PREREQ, RESOLVER_START, SOCKOPT, OPENSOCKET, CLOSESOCKET, CHUNK_*, FNMATCH, INTERLEAVE and TRAILER callbacks; and the SSH key callbacks. Only their setopt codes were compared.
- curl_global_init_mem, curl_global_sslset and curl_global_trace, beyond checking that a call does not fail.
- The curl_version_info struct fields.
- The Curl.Api WebSocket, progress, concurrency and cancellation APIs.
- Thread-safety, speed and memory (out of scope).

### B.16 sftp-scp-ssh

- **Successful password or keyboard-interactive login:** a non-root sshd cannot check passwords, so only the failure paths were compared.
- **ssh-agent and Pageant authentication:** no agent was available.
- **CURLOPT_SSH_AUTH_TYPES:** the CLI has no option that sets it.
- **Ed25519 host keys and Ed25519 KEX on Windows:** the REF WinCNG libssh2 cannot use them. Linux covered Ed25519 host keys.
- **--knownhosts on Linux:** REF-LINUX 8.18 does not have the option.
- **Linux-only differences:** these were checked against Windows REF 8.22, which showed them to be version effects, so they are not reported.
- **SSH through HTTP or SOCKS proxies:** no proxy was set up in this area.
- **The interactive password prompt and --netrc-file NUL:** this is generic CLI behaviour, and the cli-options area covers it.
- **Exact partial byte counts under --limit-rate/--max-time, and SFTP read-ahead:** these are timing or performance effects.

### B.17 http2-linux

- **HTTP/2 on Windows REF:** the Windows REF 8.22 has no nghttp2 (GF-0098), so HTTP/2 was compared only against REF-LINUX 8.18. Differences that rely on curl logic rather than nghttp2 RFC checks are therefore Probable.
- **Servers:** no Kestrel-based server was built.
- **Client ALPN list:** the ALPN list the client offers could not be captured server-side. `-v` shows `ALPN: curl offers h2,http/1.1` for both.
- **Out of scope:** HTTP/2 through a proxy (CONNECT tunnel or an h2 proxy), WebSockets over h2, PRIORITY / RFC 9218, and --http3.
- **IPv6:** `[::1]` `:authority` was not tested; the server bound 127.0.0.1 only.
- **Inconclusive:** a 2 MB upload against a server window of 100 (`m_smallwin_2m`) timed out for both because of a server limitation.
- **Request DATA framing:** frame sizes and counts were normalised, not compared.
- **PORT-WIN `h1_*` cases:** `winsrv.sh` lacks the h1 mode, so H2L-9 was not re-checked on Windows by the verifier.
- **HTTP/1.1 chunked -T - termination:** belongs to the http-requests area (GF-0082/GF-0095).

### B.18 libcurl-multi-callbacks

- **TRAILERFUNCTION abort wire bytes:** REF disagrees with itself (Windows 8.22 sends one chunk before aborting, Linux 8.18 sends none), so this is not reported.
- **HSTSWRITEFUNCTION expiry for an entry with no expiry:** REF gives "unlimited" and PORT gives null, which PORT documents as "never". Treated as an API mapping, not a difference.
- **Parallel connection counts when responses arrive at once (C_01):** depends on timing, so not reported.
- **HTTP/2:** multiplexing, PIPEWAIT, MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS and PUSHFUNCTION. There is no HTTP/2 loopback server in this bench.
- **Other wait inputs:** the contents of curl_multi_fdset and curl_multi_waitfds, and extra_fds passed to wait and poll.
- **CURLMOPT_NOTIFYFUNCTION.**
- **CURLSOCKTYPE_ACCEPT** (FTP active mode): no FTP server was set up for this area.
- **A native C driver against PORT:** PORT has no C exports, so it was driven through its C# API.

### B.19 doh-ipfs-resolution

- DoH over HTTP/2: the Windows REF has no HTTP2 support (--http2 gives exit 2, already GF-0031/GF-0099).
- GET-style (`?dns=`) DoH: curl only sends POST, so there is nothing to compare.
- A successful OCSP-stapled --doh-cert-status on Linux: there was no OCSP responder or stapling server on loopback, so only the failure path was compared (it matches).
- A DoH request tunnelled successfully through an HTTP-proxy CONNECT: the test proxy answers CONNECT with 403, so REF's use of the proxy was shown by the CONNECT line and exit 6.
- DoH through SOCKS proxies set by environment variable.
- -Z parallel ordering and the order of the A/AAAA queries: nondeterministic, so wire lines were sorted.
- A non-ASCII DoH URL path: this is a Windows argv code-page question, not DoH.
- Linux --trace-config, the -6 query count and some IPFS error texts: REF-LINUX 8.18 differs from REF-Windows 8.22, which matches PORT, so these are treated as version-dependent.
- --local-port with DoH: the apparent difference was a TIME_WAIT artefact.
- --dns-servers, --dns-interface and --dns-ipv4-addr with DoH: not built into the reference builds.
- ECH / use of HTTPS-RR answers (only the presence of the type-65 query was compared).

### B.20 tls-protocols-revocation

- Online OCSP over AIA on Windows with a real answer: the Windows chain engine never got a usable answer from the loopback `openssl ocsp` responder, even with a noCheck signer and fresh certificates. Both sides gave "revocation status is unknown".
- Revocation checks without `--cacert` (the system-store path) on Windows: this needs the test root in the machine store, which was not installed to avoid changing the machine.
- `--ssl-sessions` export/import on Linux: REF-LINUX 8.18 has no SSLS-EXPORT (exit 2), so there is no oracle. PORT-LINUX advertises it and writes the file.
- mqtts on Linux: REF-LINUX 8.18 lacks mqtts (exit 1).
- Windows FTPS against an OpenSSL-based FTPS server: WSL localhost forwarding is not enabled, so Windows data-session reuse was judged from the server's handshake size (about 141 bytes resumed vs 1380 full).
- TLS 1.3 post-handshake auth on Windows: Schannel does not do PHA, so only Linux exercises it.
- Real FTP servers (vsftpd, proftpd), a real LDAP server, and real OCSP/CRL infrastructure: none are installed and there is no internet. Stand-ins emulate vsftpd's strict EOF (426) and require_ssl_reuse.
- Windows `-v` output in general: REF 8.22.0 is a debug build, so only reuse lines that also exist in release builds were compared.
- Interactive renegotiation driven by `openssl s_server` `R`: the deterministic .NET `NegotiateClientCertificateAsync` path was used instead.

### B.21 parallel-multi-transfer

- A real Ctrl-C on Windows: the harness cannot deliver a console Ctrl-C to a child whose output is redirected. SIGINT was tested only on Linux (refuted above).
- Linux results compare against REF-LINUX 8.18.0, not the 8.22.0 target. Every Linux difference reported above also reproduces on Windows against 8.22.0, except PMT-6, which differs only on Windows.
- HTTP/2 multiplexing under -Z (--http2-prior-knowledge): this harness has no h2 loopback server.
- Exact retry-delay timing, and the speed and time columns of the meter: excluded as timing.
- The order of transfers that finish in the same millisecond (identical delays): it is a race in both REF and PORT, so it was not compared.
- -Z against hosts whose DNS lookup fails (exit 6): this needs a real resolver lookup, so it was skipped to keep all traffic on loopback.

## Appendix C. Refuted and dismissed candidate findings

Candidates that were investigated and are **not** defects of the port (or not reportable differences). Do not re-report them.

### C.1 Refuted by the verifiers

- **upstream-cases: port ratchet "failing" test938 and test836** - not a REF-vs-PORT difference; REF-WIN also fails these ratchet expectations. The real difference is reported as the SMTP/IMAP QUIT/LOGOUT timing issue (upstream-cases UC-9).
- **upstream-cases: port ratchet test1211** - not separate; the reportable difference is the active-mode 425 message (upstream-cases UC-13).
- **upstream-cases: port ratchet test1801** - not separate; the reportable difference is the HTTP/2 exit 55 vs 16 issue (upstream-cases UC-8 / http2-linux H2L-9).
- **upstream-cases: port ratchet test594 (FTP STOR after a refused EPRT hangs)** - REF hangs the same way; not a difference. Also test2500-test2503 (HTTP/3): REF-WIN has no HTTP/3, so the ratchet's skips are not differences.
- **libcurl-api: Curl.Api PUT/PATCH stream body sent POST-style with a form Content-Type** - `CurlContent.FromStream` is documented as POSTFIELDSIZE semantics; Curl.Api is a port-only API and its output is byte-identical to `curl -X PUT --data-binary`, the libcurl POSTFIELDS + CUSTOMREQUEST PUT behaviour. Comparing it with `curl -T -` was an arbitrary choice.
- **parallel-multi-transfer: SIGINT during -Z downloads on Linux** (REF leaves partial files cut to a multiple of 4096 and loses buffered -w output; PORT writes everything it received) - REF's result comes from unflushed libc stdio buffers when the default SIGINT handler kills the process; it depends on buffer size and kill timing. Both exit 130 and PORT writes a superset of the data.

### C.2 Sub-claims corrected during verification (the rest of the finding stands)

- **proxy-connect PC-18 / tls:** the claim that REF sends the `status_request` extension and PORT omits it on Windows was not reproduced; neither side sent it in any run. Only the offered TLS versions differ (kept as an issue).
- **sftp-scp-ssh SSH-06:** the claim that PORT sends no SSH DISCONNECT when the output file cannot be created was wrong; the verifier saw `Received disconnect ... 11: Shutdown` on Windows and Linux. The exit-code and `-w` difference stands.
- **upstream-cases UC-10:** the test1714 sub-claim (REF-WIN sends nothing and exits 0, PORT exits 63) was not re-run and is not reported.
- **upstream-cases UC-12:** the original line counts (1741/1742) came from different data; the off-by-one itself was re-confirmed (1744 vs 1745).
- **http-stateful HS-10:** originally reported as Windows-only; the verifier also reproduced it on Linux (kept as an issue for both platforms).

### C.3 Candidates dismissed as not reportable

- **libcurl-api: LOCALPORT differences in `probe.exe lport`** - they follow run order (whichever side runs second hits TIME_WAIT on the same local port); `lport portfirst` flips the result. Likewise `--local-port` with DoH and back-to-back `--local-port` runs in proxy-connect.
- **libcurl-multi-callbacks: TRAILERFUNCTION abort wire bytes** - REF disagrees with itself (Windows 8.22 sends one chunk before aborting, Linux 8.18 sends none).
- **libcurl-multi-callbacks: HSTSWRITEFUNCTION expiry for an entry with no expiry** - REF reports "unlimited" and PORT reports null, which PORT documents as "never"; treated as an API mapping.
- **libcurl-multi-callbacks: parallel connection counts when responses arrive at once (C_01), and C_09's `global-maxconc` line** - timing-dependent; REF also shows values above the limit.
- **other-protocols: IMAP `-X 'APPEND x'` with `-T`** - REF itself hangs; a REF fault.
- **other-protocols: DICT `-I`, the Windows MQTT case killed after a timeout (m36), parallel POP3 connection counts** - timing-dependent or caused by REF losing buffered stdout when killed.
- **ftp-file-tftp: TFTP two-URL log order** - the difference is in the multithreaded stub's log order, not on the wire.
- **config-glob-output: the message for `-o CONIN$`** - same exit code, a device-name edge case.
- **config-glob-output / http-responses: REF 8.22 Debug-build assertion for `-J` with filename `""`, `.` or `..`** - a REF Debug-build defect; release-build behaviour could not be shown on Windows, and on Linux both match.
- **url-parsing: Windows IDN from percent-decoded or config-file bytes** - the Windows REF passes these to libidn2 as CP1252 and produces mojibake punycode.
- **http-responses: the Windows `basic_I.bin` / `basic_i.bin` fixture overwrite** - a case-insensitive file-name artefact of the test fixtures, not a port difference.
- **All areas: differences that only reflect REF-LINUX 8.18.0 being older than 8.22.0** (wording of connect errors, `Establish` vs `Establishing HTTP proxy tunnel`, config error wording, query-escape case on Linux, `-u :`, `* closing connection #-1`, STS max-age overflow, `--etag-save -` exit 23, gopher CR/LF refusal, MQTT `%00` topic, WS scheme case in `%{scheme}`, some SigV4 canonical forms, and similar) - in each case the port matches Windows REF 8.22.0.
- **All areas: timing-only differences** (speed columns, retry-delay timing, timing-dependent meter update counts, order of transfers finishing in the same millisecond, partial byte counts under `--limit-rate`/`--max-time`) - excluded by the review rules.

| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-03 | [CGR-164](#cgr-164) | TLS sessions are resumed across transfers whose verification settings differ (`-k` then `--cacert`, the reverse, or an added `--pinnedpubkey`); curl starts a new session |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-04 | [CGR-165](#cgr-165) | Explicit FTPS (AUTH TLS) never reuses the control connection for the next URL, while a CCC-cleared plaintext connection is reused where curl reconnects |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-05 | [CGR-006](#cgr-006) | Windows: FTPS uploads in active mode over TLS 1.3 end the data connection with a TCP reset, so a strict server answers 426 and PORT exits 18 |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-06 | [CGR-166](#cgr-166) | `--disable-eprt` on an IPv6 control connection: PORT sends `PORT h,h,h,h,p,p` where curl still sends EPRT |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-07 | [CGR-167](#cgr-167) | Linux: `--cert-status` with `-k` reports the OCSP outcome, and accepts a good staple, where curl fails with "OCSP response verification failed" |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-08 | [CGR-168](#cgr-168) | Linux: `%{ssl_verify_result}` is 0 when `--crlfile` rejects the certificate (curl reports 23 "certificate revoked" or 12 "CRL has expired") |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-09 | [CGR-169](#cgr-169) | Linux: TLS 1.3 post-handshake client authentication without a client certificate fails on the server side for PORT |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-10 | [CGR-287](#cgr-287) | Windows: a revoked server certificate (CRL distribution point or staple) is reported as "untrusted root" or "revocation status is unknown" instead of "has been revoked" |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-11 | [CGR-288](#cgr-288) | Windows `--ftp-ssl-ccc`: curl's Schannel build often clears the control channel on a later connection and completes; PORT fails every URL with exit 81 |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-12 | [CGR-289](#cgr-289) | Windows `ldaps://`: PORT uses one connection with SNI `localhost` and honours `--cacert`; curl's WinLDAP makes a second connection with the machine name as SNI and uses the system store |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-13 | [CGR-290](#cgr-290) | `-v` does not report TLS session reuse (`* schannel: reusing existing credential handle` on Windows, `* SSL reusing session with ALPN '-'` on Linux) |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-14 | [CGR-291](#cgr-291) | Linux: PORT always sends the status_request (OCSP stapling) extension; curl sends it only with `--cert-status` |
| tls-protocols-revocation | TPR-15 | [CGR-292](#cgr-292) | Linux: TLS read-error messages name a hard-coded `OpenSSL/3.5.7` instead of the OpenSSL actually in use |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-1 | [CGR-017](#cgr-017) | Reading stdin twice in one command line makes PORT fail with exit 2 and a .NET exception before it sends anything |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-2 | [CGR-170](#cgr-170) | Under -Z, a later URL that cannot be set up (bad glob, unreadable -T file) makes REF abandon the whole batch, but PORT still runs the other transfers |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-3 | [CGR-171](#cgr-171) | Under -Z, when a host's first transfer closes its connection (Connection: close or a -f error), PORT runs the waiting transfers one at a time, starting with the last; REF starts them all at once |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-4 | [CGR-172](#cgr-172) | Under -Z without --parallel-immediate, REF lets queued same-host transfers start when any transfer ends; PORT holds them until that host's first transfer ends |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-5 | [CGR-173](#cgr-173) | --fail-early under -Z: an aborted transfer that already had its response loses %{http_code} and %{filename_effective}, and --remove-on-error leaves its partial file |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-6 | [CGR-174](#cgr-174) | Two concurrent -Z transfers writing the same -o file: PORT fails one of them with exit 23 on Windows |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-7 | [CGR-175](#cgr-175) | -F name=@- shared by several URLs: PORT sends an empty part and exits 0 in serial mode, where REF fails the later transfers with (26); under -Z the bodies differ |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-8 | [CGR-293](#cgr-293) | --skip-existing under -Z: PORT writes the skipped transfer's -w line at once, but REF writes it after the running transfers |
| parallel-multi-transfer | PMT-9 | [CGR-294](#cgr-294) | --fail-early under -Z: REF still completes in-flight transfers whose response arrives before its abort lands (about 1 s), but PORT cancels them at once |
